title.zh: 卷475 列傳二百六十二 洪秀全
title.raw: 卷475 列傳二百六十二 洪秀全

sentences.zh: 洪秀全，廣東花縣人。

translations.literal: Hong Xiuquan was a native of Huaxian in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Xiuquan came from Huaxian in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 少飲博無賴，以演卜游粵、湘間。

translations.literal: In youth he drank and gambled like a good-for-nothing, and made his living by practicing divination as he wandered through Guangdong and Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he drank and gambled like a rascal, earning his keep by telling fortunes as he wandered through Guangdong and Hunan.

sentences.zh: 有朱九疇者，倡上帝會，亦名三點會，秀全及同邑馮雲山師事之。

translations.literal: There was one Zhu Jiuchou who founded the God Worship Society, also called the Triad Society; Xiuquan and his fellow townsman Feng Yunshan took him as their teacher.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Zhu Jiuchou had founded the God Worship Society, also known as the Triad Society, and both Xiuquan and his fellow townsman Feng Yunshan became his disciples.

sentences.zh: 九疇死，眾以秀全為教主。

translations.literal: When Jiuchou died, the assembly made Xiuquan their cult leader.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiuchou died, the congregation installed Xiuquan as their leader.

sentences.zh: 官捕之急，乃往香港入耶穌教，藉抗官。

translations.literal: When official pursuit grew pressing, he went to Hong Kong and joined the Jesus sect, using it to resist the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: With the authorities pressing hard to arrest him, he went to Hong Kong and joined the Christian church, using that affiliation to shield himself from the government.

sentences.zh: 旋偕雲山傳教至廣西，居桂平。

translations.literal: Soon he went with Yunshan to preach in Guangxi and settled at Guiping.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went with Yunshan to spread their teachings in Guangxi and settled at Guiping.

sentences.zh: 時秀全妹婿蕭朝貴及楊秀清、韋昌輝皆家桂平，與相結納。

translations.literal: At that time Xiuquan's brother-in-law Xiao Chaogui, together with Yang Xiuqing and Wei Changhui, all had homes at Guiping and formed ties with him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xiuquan's brother-in-law Xiao Chaogui, along with Yang Xiuqing and Wei Changhui, all lived in Guiping and entered into alliance with him.

sentences.zh: 貴縣石達開亦來入教。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai of Guixian also came to join the sect.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai of Guixian also joined the movement.

sentences.zh: 秀全嘗患病，詭云病死七日而蘇，能知未來事。

translations.literal: Xiuquan once fell ill and falsely claimed that he had died for seven days and then revived, and that he could know future events.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuquan once fell ill and claimed he had been dead for seven days before returning to life, saying he could foretell the future.

sentences.zh: 謂：「上帝召我，有大劫，惟拜上帝可免。

translations.literal: He said: "God has summoned me; a great calamity is coming, and only by worshiping God can one escape it.
translations.idiomatic: He declared, "God has called me. A great catastrophe is coming, and only those who worship God will be spared.

sentences.zh: 」凡會中人男稱兄弟，女稱姊妹，欲人皆平等，託名西洋教。

translations.literal: " All members of the society called men brothers and women sisters, seeking universal equality under the name of Western religion.
translations.idiomatic: " Within the society men called one another brothers and women sisters, preaching equality for all under the banner of Western religion.

sentences.zh: 自言通天語，謂天父名耶和華，耶穌其長子，己為次子。

translations.literal: He claimed to speak the language of Heaven, saying the Heavenly Father was named Jehovah, Jesus was his eldest son, and he himself was the second son.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed he could speak Heaven's language, declaring that the Heavenly Father was named Jehovah, that Jesus was the elder son, and that he himself was the younger son.

sentences.zh: 嗣是輒臥一室，禁人窺伺，不進飲食，歷數日而後出。

translations.literal: Thereafter he would lie in a single room, forbidding anyone to spy on him, taking no food or drink for several days before emerging.
translations.idiomatic: After that he would shut himself in a room, forbid anyone to look in, and take no food or drink for days before coming out again.

sentences.zh: 出則謂與上帝議事，眾皆駭服。

translations.literal: When he came out he said he had been deliberating with God, and all were awestruck and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When he emerged he said he had been conferring with God, and the congregation was awestruck into obedience.

sentences.zh: 復造寶誥、真言諸偽書，密為傳布。

translations.literal: He also forged spurious scriptures such as the Precious Edicts and True Words and had them secretly circulated.
translations.idiomatic: He also composed forged scriptures such as the Precious Edicts and True Words and had them circulated in secret.

sentences.zh: 潛蓄髮，藏山菁間。

translations.literal: He secretly hoarded hair and hid it among the mountain thickets.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly stockpiled hair and hid supplies in the mountain thickets.

sentences.zh: 嗾人分赴武宣、象州、藤縣、陸川、博白各邑，誘眾入會。

translations.literal: He sent men out separately to Wuxuan, Xiangzhou, Tengxian, Luchuan, Bobai, and other districts to lure the populace into the society.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched agents to Wuxuan, Xiangzhou, Tengxian, Luchuan, Bobai, and other counties to recruit people into the society.

sentences.zh: 初，粵西歲饑多盜，湖南雷再浩、新寧李沅發復竄入為亂。

translations.literal: At first western Guangdong suffered famine year after year and had many bandits; Lei Zaihao of Hunan and Li Yuanfa of Xinning also slipped in to make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Western Guangdong had suffered famine for years and was overrun with bandits; Lei Zaihao from Hunan and Li Yuanfa from Xinning also crossed the border to raise disturbances.

sentences.zh: 粵盜張家福等各率黨數千，四出俘劫。

translations.literal: Guangdong bandits such as Zhang Jiafu each led parties of several thousand and ranged in all directions to seize and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong bandits such as Zhang Jiafu each led gangs of several thousand men on raids in every direction.

sentences.zh: 秀全乘之，與楊秀清創立保良攻匪會，練兵籌餉，歸附者益眾。

translations.literal: Xiuquan seized the opportunity; with Yang Xiuqing he founded the Society for Protecting the Good and Attacking Bandits, drilled troops and raised funds, and those who joined grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuquan took advantage of the chaos; with Yang Xiuqing he founded the Society for Protecting the Good and Attacking Bandits, drilled troops and raised funds, and his following grew steadily.

sentences.zh: 桂平知縣誘而執之，搜獲入教名冊十七本；

translations.literal: The magistrate of Guiping lured and arrested him, and in the search seized seventeen registers of those who had joined the sect;
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Guiping lured him into a trap and arrested him, seizing seventeen membership registers in the search;

sentences.zh: 巡撫鄭祖琛不能決，遂釋之。

translations.literal: the provincial governor Zheng Zuchen could not decide the case and so released him.
translations.idiomatic: but Provincial Governor Zheng Zuchen could not bring himself to decide the matter and released him.

sentences.zh: 秀全既出獄，秀清率眾迎歸，招集亡命，貴縣秦日綱、林鳳祥，揭陽海盜羅大綱，衡山洪大全皆來附，有眾萬人。

translations.literal: After Xiuquan left prison, Xiuqing led the crowd to welcome him back, gathered fugitives, and Qin Rigang and Lin Fengxiang of Guixian, the Jieyang pirate Luo Dagang, and Hong Daquan of Hengshan all came to attach themselves to him, until he had a following of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiuquan was out of prison, Xiuqing led the faithful to welcome him home and gathered desperadoes to his banner; Qin Rigang and Lin Fengxiang of Guixian, the Jieyang pirate Luo Dagang, and Hong Daquan of Hengshan all joined him, and his following reached ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 馮雲山讀書多智計，為部署隊伍、攻守方略。

translations.literal: Feng Yunshan was well read and full of stratagems, and arranged the deployment of units and plans for attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yunshan was learned and resourceful, and took charge of organizing the ranks and planning strategy for attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 以歲值丁未，應「紅羊」之讖，遂乘勢倡亂於金田。

translations.literal: Because the year was dingwei, fulfilling the prophecy of the "Red Sheep," he then seized the momentum to raise rebellion at Jintian.
translations.idiomatic: The year was dingwei, matching the prophecy of the "Red Sheep," and he seized the moment to launch rebellion at Jintian.

sentences.zh: 褫鄭祖琛職，起前雲貴總督林則徐為欽差大臣往督師。

translations.literal: Zheng Zuchen was stripped of his post, and the former governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou Lin Zexu was recalled as Imperial Commissioner to supervise the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zuchen was dismissed from office, and the former governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou, Lin Zexu, was appointed Imperial Commissioner to take command of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 則徐薨於途，以兩廣總督李星沅代之，赴廣西剿寇。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu died on the road; the governor-general of Guangdong-Guangxi Li Xingyuan replaced him and went to Guangxi to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu died en route, and Governor-General Li Xingyuan of the Two Guangs replaced him and marched into Guangxi to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 寇竄平南恩旺墟，副將李殿元擊卻之，復回撲，巡檢張鏞不屈死；

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Enwang market in Pingnan; Vice Commander Li Dianyuan drove them off, but they turned back to attack again, and Sub-Inspector Zhang Yong died rather than yield;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Enwang market in Pingnan; Vice Commander Li Dianyuan repulsed them, but they turned and attacked again, and Sub-Inspector Zhang Yong was killed when he refused to surrender;

sentences.zh: 仍遁金田，星沅檄清江協副將伊克坦布往攻，被圍陣亡。

translations.literal: they still slipped back to Jintian; Xingyuan ordered the Qingjiang Brigade Vice Commander Yiketanbu to attack, and he was surrounded and killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: they still escaped back to Jintian; Xingyuan ordered Brigade Vice Commander Yiketanbu of the Qingjiang detachment to attack, and he was surrounded and killed in action.

sentences.zh: 星沅檄鎮遠總兵周鳳岐往援，戰一晝夜，斃寇數百，圍始解。

translations.literal: Xingyuan ordered the Zhenyuan Regional Commander Zhou Fengqi to relieve them; after fighting a day and a night and killing several hundred rebels, the siege was finally lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan sent Regional Commander Zhou Fengqi of Zhenyuan to the rescue; after a day and night of fighting, during which several hundred rebels were killed, the siege was finally broken.

sentences.zh: 上以寇勢日熾，命前漕運總督周天爵署廣西巡撫，乃請提督向榮專剿金田。

translations.literal: Because rebel strength grew daily, the throne appointed the former grain-transport governor Zhou Tianjue acting governor of Guangxi, and requested that Regional Commander Xiang Rong concentrate on suppressing Jintian.
translations.idiomatic: As rebel strength grew daily, the emperor appointed former grain-transport governor Zhou Tianjue acting governor of Guangxi and ordered Regional Commander Xiang Rong to concentrate on suppressing Jintian.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，秀全僭號偽天王，縱火焚其墟，盡驅眾分擾桂平、貴、武宣、平南等縣，入象州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, Xiuquan presumptuously styled himself false Heavenly King, set fire and burned his stronghold, drove the whole host out to harass Guiping, Gui, Wuxuan, Pingnan, and other counties, and entered Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng, Xiuquan proclaimed himself Heavenly King, burned his base to the ground, and drove his followers out to raid Guiping, Gui, Wuxuan, Pingnan, and other counties before advancing into Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 上命廣州副都統烏蘭泰會討，以大學士賽尚阿為欽差大臣，率都統巴清德、副都統達洪阿馳防。

translations.literal: The throne ordered the Guangzhou Vice Commander-in-Chief Wulantai to join the campaign, appointed Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a Imperial Commissioner, and sent Commanders-in-Chief Ba Qingde and Vice Commander-in-Chief Da Hong'a in haste to take up defense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Vice Commander-in-Chief Wulantai of Guangzhou to join the campaign, appointed Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a Imperial Commissioner, and sent Commanders-in-Chief Ba Qingde and Vice Commander-in-Chief Da Hong'a posthaste to reinforce the defenses.

sentences.zh: 烏蘭泰至象州，三戰皆捷，疏言：「粵西寇眾皆烏合，惟東鄉僭號設官、易服蓄髮有大志，兇悍過群盜，實腹心大患。

translations.literal: Wulantai reached Xiangzhou and won three battles in succession; he memorialized: "The rebel hosts of western Guangdong are all rabble, but only those of Dongxiang who presumptuously title themselves, establish offices, change dress, and let their hair grow have great ambition; they are fiercer than ordinary bandits and are truly the gravest threat at the heart of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Wulantai reached Xiangzhou and won three battles in a row; in his memorial he wrote, "The rebel bands of western Guangdong are mere rabble, but the Dongxiang faction that has proclaimed titles, set up offices, changed their dress, and let their hair grow harbors serious ambition; they are fiercer than ordinary bandits and are the gravest threat we face.

sentences.zh: 」周天爵主滾營進偪，驅諸羅淥洞盡殲之，向榮不謂然。

translations.literal: " Zhou Tianjue favored rolling the camps forward in close pursuit and driving the rebels of Luodong Cave to total annihilation; Xiang Rong did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Tianjue favored pressing forward camp by camp and annihilating the rebels in Luodong Cave, but Xiang Rong disagreed.

sentences.zh: 檄貴州鎮總兵秦定三移營大林，堵北竄象州道，定三亦不奉命。

translations.literal: He ordered the Guizhou Brigade Regional Commander Qin Dingsan to shift camp to Dalin and block the route by which rebels fleeing north might enter Xiangzhou, but Dingsan also disobeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Regional Commander Qin Dingsan of the Guizhou Brigade to move his camp to Dalin and block the northern route into Xiangzhou, but Dingsan refused to obey as well.

sentences.zh: 四月，秀全自大林逸出走象州，犯桂平新墟。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Xiuquan slipped away from Dalin toward Xiangzhou and attacked Xin market in Guiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Xiuquan broke out from Dalin toward Xiangzhou and struck Xin market in Guiping.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿增調川兵，募鄉勇，合三萬人，分兵要隘。

translations.literal: Sai Shang'a brought up additional Sichuan troops and recruited local militia, totaling thirty thousand men, and divided forces to hold the strategic passes.
translations.idiomatic: Sai Shang'a brought up reinforcements from Sichuan and recruited local militia until he had thirty thousand men, whom he deployed to hold the strategic passes.

sentences.zh: 一日戰七勝，斬捕二千，寇仍遁新墟。

translations.literal: In a single day they fought seven victories and killed or captured two thousand, yet the rebels still fled back to Xin market.
translations.idiomatic: In one day they won seven engagements and killed or captured two thousand rebels, yet the rebels still escaped back to Xin market.

sentences.zh: 七月，竄紫金山，山前以新墟為門戶，後以雙髻山、豬仔峽為要隘。

translations.literal: In the seventh month they fled to Purple Gold Mountain; Xin market served as the gateway in front of the mountain, while Twin-Peak Mountain and Piglet Gorge were the vital passes behind.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they withdrew to Purple Gold Mountain, with Xin market as the gateway in front and Twin-Peak Mountain and Piglet Gorge as the vital passes in the rear.

sentences.zh: 巴清德與川、楚鄉勇出其後，上下奪雙髻山，寇大潰，屯風門坳。

translations.literal: Ba Qingde with Sichuan and Huguang militia came up behind them, seized Twin-Peak Mountain from above and below, the rebels were routed in great disorder, and encamped at Fengmen'ao.
translations.idiomatic: Ba Qingde advanced from the rear with Sichuan and Huguang militia, seized Twin-Peak Mountain from both flanks, routed the rebels completely, and drove them to encamp at Fengmen'ao.

sentences.zh: 向榮率諸軍三路攻之，陣斃韋昌輝弟韋亞孫、韋十一等，始遁走。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong led the armies in a three-pronged attack, killed in battle Wei Changhui's younger brothers Wei Yasun and Wei Shiyi and others, and only then did they flee.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong led the armies in a three-pronged assault, killing Wei Changhui's younger brothers Wei Yasun and Wei Shiyi in battle before the rebels finally fled.

sentences.zh: 我軍追之，會大雨，軍仗盡失。

translations.literal: Our army pursued them, but a great rain came and all weapons and equipment were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Our forces pursued them, but a torrential rain fell and all arms and equipment were lost.

sentences.zh: 閏八月，寇分二路東走藤，北犯永安，陷之，遂僭號太平天國。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month the rebels split into two columns, one going east toward Teng, the other invading Yong'an in the north and taking it; they then presumptuously styled their state the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month the rebels split into two columns, one marching east toward Teng and the other striking north at Yong'an and capturing it; they then proclaimed the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 秀全自為天王，妻賴氏為后，建元天德。

translations.literal: Xiuquan made himself Heavenly King, his wife the Lai clan queen, and established the era name Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuquan took the title Heavenly King, made his wife of the Lai clan his queen, and adopted the era name Tiande.

sentences.zh: 以秀清為東王，軍事皆取決，蕭朝貴西王，馮雲山南王，韋昌輝北王，石達開翼王，洪大全天德王；

translations.literal: He made Xiuqing Eastern King, with all military affairs decided by him; Xiao Chaogui Western King, Feng Yunshan Southern King, Wei Changhui Northern King, Shi Dakai Wing King, and Hong Daquan Tiande King;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Xiuqing Eastern King, giving him final say over all military affairs; Xiao Chaogui became Western King, Feng Yunshan Southern King, Wei Changhui Northern King, Shi Dakai Wing King, and Hong Daquan Tiande King;

sentences.zh: 秦日綱、羅亞旺、范連德、胡以晃等四十八人任丞相、軍師偽職。

translations.literal: Qin Rigang, Luo Yawang, Fan Liande, Hu Yihuang, and forty-eight others were given the false offices of Chancellor and Military Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Rigang, Luo Yawang, Fan Liande, Hu Yihuang, and forty-eight others were appointed to the ranks of Chancellor and Military Adviser.

sentences.zh: 時官軍勢勝，寇知不可敵，有散志。

translations.literal: At that time government forces were gaining the upper hand; the rebels knew they could not be resisted and thoughts of dispersing arose.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces were gaining the upper hand, and the rebels, knowing they could not prevail, began to think of scattering.

sentences.zh: 秀清獨建策封王以羈縻之，勢燼而復熾。

translations.literal: Xiuqing alone proposed enfeoffing kings to bind them, and strength that had been extinguished blazed up again.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuqing alone urged enfeoffing them as kings to keep them loyal, and a movement that had nearly collapsed flared up again.

sentences.zh: 九月，大軍移陽朔，會攻永安，賊分屯莫家村。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the main army moved to Yangshuo and jointly attacked Yong'an; the rebels divided their encampments at Mojia Village.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the main army moved on Yangshuo and jointly attacked Yong'an, while the rebels divided their forces and encamped at Mojia Village.

sentences.zh: 烏蘭泰建中軍旗於秀才嶺，上植一紅蓋，下埋地雷，誘敵燔殺四千，大軍乘之，遂克莫家村。

translations.literal: Wulantai set up the central army banner on Xiucai Ridge, planted a red canopy above it, and buried land mines below; he lured the enemy and burned and killed four thousand, the main army pressed the advantage, and Mojia Village was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Wulantai raised the central army banner on Xiucai Ridge with a red canopy above and land mines below; he lured the enemy in and killed four thousand, the main army pressed the advantage, and Mojia Village fell.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，大兵圍永安，燬東、西砲臺。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year the main army besieged Yong'an and destroyed the eastern and western batteries.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year the main army besieged Yong'an and destroyed the eastern and western batteries.

sentences.zh: 二月，石達開分兵為四，敗我軍於壽春營，進破古束沖、小路關。

translations.literal: In the second month Shi Dakai divided his forces into four, defeated our army at Shouchun Camp, and advanced to break Gushuchong and Xiaoluguan passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Shi Dakai divided his forces into four columns, defeated our army at Shouchun Camp, and advanced to capture Gushuchong and Xiaoluguan passes.

sentences.zh: 偽丞相秦日綱由水竇屯仙回嶺。

translations.literal: The false Chancellor Qin Rigang came by Shuidou and encamped at Xianhui Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Chancellor Qin Rigang advanced by Shuidou and encamped at Xianhui Ridge.

sentences.zh: 烏蘭泰分兵夾擊，斃寇數千，擒偽天德王洪大全，檻送京師，磔之市。

translations.literal: Wulantai divided his forces for a pincer attack, killed several thousand rebels, captured the false Tiande King Hong Daquan, sent him in a cage to the capital, and had him dismembered in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Wulantai divided his forces for a pincer attack, killed several thousand rebels, captured the rebel Tiande King Hong Daquan, sent him in a cage to the capital, and had him dismembered in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 時大雨如注，烏蘭泰提精卒入山，山路濘滑，寇乘我軍陣未定，短兵衝突，遂大敗。

translations.literal: At that time rain poured down in torrents; Wulantai led picked troops into the mountains, the mountain paths were muddy and slippery, the rebels seized the moment when our formations were not yet set, charged in close combat, and our army suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Rain was pouring down in torrents; Wulantai led elite troops into the mountains, but the paths were muddy and treacherous, and the rebels struck before our formations were set, charging in at close quarters and inflicting a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 秀全從楊秀清謀，由瑤山、馬嶺間道徑撲桂林。

translations.literal: Xiuquan followed Yang Xiuqing's plan and by the bypaths of Yaoshan and Maling made straight for Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Following Yang Xiuqing's plan, Xiuquan took the mountain trails through Yaoshan and Maling and struck directly at Guilin.

sentences.zh: 烏蘭泰率敗卒追之城南將軍橋，受重創，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Wulantai led the defeated troops in pursuit to Jiangjun Bridge south of the city, received grave wounds, and died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Wulantai led the defeated troops in pursuit to Jiangjun Bridge south of the city, was gravely wounded, and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 三月，賊徑趨廣西省城。

translations.literal: In the third month the rebels made straight for the provincial capital of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the rebels marched straight for the provincial capital of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 向榮先一時繞道至省，寇踵至，已有備，相持不能拔，解圍而北。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong had gone by a roundabout route and reached the capital first; the rebels followed close behind, but defenses were already in place, the two sides faced each other without either being able to take the city, and they raised the siege and went north.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong had reached the capital first by a roundabout route; the rebels followed close behind, but the city was already prepared, neither side could gain the advantage, and the rebels broke off the siege and marched north.

sentences.zh: 馮雲山、羅大綱先驅陷興安、全州，將順流趨長沙。

translations.literal: Feng Yunshan and Luo Dagang as vanguard took Xing'an and Quanzhou and were about to go downstream toward Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yunshan and Luo Dagang led the vanguard in capturing Xing'an and Quanzhou and prepared to sail downstream toward Changsha.

sentences.zh: 浙江知縣江忠源禦之蓑衣渡，馮雲山中砲死，寇退走道州。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongyuan, a magistrate from Zhejiang, met them at Suoyi Ford; Feng Yunshan was killed by cannon fire, and the rebels retreated toward Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongyuan, a magistrate from Zhejiang, met them at Suoyi Ford; Feng Yunshan was killed by cannon fire, and the rebels fell back toward Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 道州俗悍，多會匪，所至爭為效死，勢復張。

translations.literal: The people of Daozhou were fierce by custom and had many secret-society bandits; wherever the rebels went men vied to die for them, and their power swelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Daozhou was a fierce place with many secret-society bandits; wherever the rebels went, men vied to fight to the death for them, and their strength revived.

sentences.zh: 六月，陷江華、寧遠、嘉禾。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they took Jianghua, Ningyuan, and Jiahe.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they captured Jianghua, Ningyuan, and Jiahe.

sentences.zh: 七月，陷桂陽州，江忠源躡至，一戰走之，趨郴州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month they took Guiyang Prefecture; Jiang Zhongyuan pursued close behind, routed them in one battle, and they made for Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they captured Guiyang Prefecture; Jiang Zhongyuan pursued them closely, routed them in a single battle, and drove them toward Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 蕭朝貴以膽智自豪，謂群寇遲懦，又詗長沙守兵單，可襲而取也，乃率李開芳、林鳳祥由永興、茶陵、醴陵趨長沙，設幕城南。

translations.literal: Xiao Chaogui prided himself on his courage and wit, called the other rebel leaders slow and cowardly, and also learned that Changsha's garrison was thin and could be taken by surprise; he then led Li Kaifang and Lin Fengxiang by way of Yongxing, Chaling, and Liling toward Changsha and pitched his headquarters south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chaogui was proud of his courage and cunning, dismissed the other rebel leaders as slow and timid, and learned that Changsha's garrison was thin enough to take by surprise; he led Li Kaifang and Lin Fengxiang through Yongxing, Chaling, and Liling toward Changsha and pitched camp south of the city walls.

sentences.zh: 八月，蕭朝貴攻南門，官兵擊之，殪，尸埋老龍潭，後起出梟其首。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Xiao Chaogui attacked the south gate; government troops struck him down and he was killed; his body was buried at Laolongtan, and later when it was exhumed his head was displayed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Xiao Chaogui attacked the south gate; government troops killed him in the assault, buried his body at Laolongtan, and later exhumed it to display his head.

sentences.zh: 秀全聞朝貴死，自郴州至，督攻益急，九月，掘隧道攻城，屢不獲逞。

translations.literal: When Xiuquan heard of Chaogui's death he came from Chenzhou, pressed the assault ever harder, and in the ninth month dug tunnels to attack the city, but repeatedly failed to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuquan heard of Chaogui's death he came up from Chenzhou and pressed the assault with greater urgency; in the ninth month they dug tunnels to storm the city, but repeatedly failed to break through.

sentences.zh: 十月，秀全於南門外得偽玉璽，稱為天賜，脅眾呼萬歲。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Xiuquan outside the south gate obtained a false jade seal, called it heaven-sent, and compelled the crowd to shout ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Xiuquan found a jade seal outside the south gate, proclaimed it a gift from Heaven, and forced his followers to shout long life.

sentences.zh: 遂夜渡湘水，由回龍塘竄寧鄉，抵益陽。

translations.literal: He then crossed the Xiang River by night, fled by Huilongtang to Ningxiang, and reached Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: That night they crossed the Xiang River, fled through Huilongtang to Ningxiang, and reached Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 擄民船數千，出臨資口，渡洞庭，陷岳州。

translations.literal: They seized several thousand civilian boats, went out from Linzikou, crossed Lake Dongting, and took Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: They seized several thousand civilian boats, sailed out from Linzikou, crossed Lake Dongting, and captured Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 城中舊儲吳三桂軍械，至是盡以資寇。

translations.literal: The city had long stored Wu Sangui's military equipment, and now all of it went to supply the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The city had long stored Wu Sangui's arsenals, and now the rebels took the whole stock for themselves.

sentences.zh: 寇入長江，旬日間奪五千艘，婦孺貨財盡驅之滿載。

translations.literal: The rebels entered the Yangtze; within ten days they seized five thousand vessels, driving women, children, goods, and wealth aboard until every boat was full.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the Yangtze, they seized five thousand boats within ten days, packing every vessel with women, children, goods, and plunder.

sentences.zh: 秀全駕龍舟，樹黃旗，列巨砲，夜則張三十六燈，他船稱是，數十里火光不絕如晝，遂東下，十一月，陷漢陽。

translations.literal: Xiuquan rode a dragon boat, raised yellow banners, and arrayed great cannon; at night he hung thirty-six lamps, the other boats did likewise, and for several tens of li the blaze of lights was unbroken as at noon; they then went downstream, and in the eleventh month took Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuquan sailed in a dragon boat under yellow banners with great cannon ranged along the deck; at night he lit thirty-six lamps, and the other boats followed suit until for miles the river blazed bright as day; they then sailed downstream and in the eleventh month captured Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，攻武昌。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they attacked Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they attacked Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 時楊秀清司軍令，李開芳、林鳳祥、羅大綱掌兵事。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Xiuqing directed military orders, and Li Kaifang, Lin Fengxiang, and Luo Dagang managed military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiuqing held command of military orders, while Li Kaifang, Lin Fengxiang, and Luo Dagang directed operations in the field.

sentences.zh: 值武漢二江屆冬水涸，乃擄船作浮橋，環以鐵索，直達省城，分門攻之。

translations.literal: As the two rivers at Wuhan reached winter and the waters fell, they seized boats to make floating bridges, bound them with iron chains straight to the provincial city, and attacked gate by gate.
translations.idiomatic: Winter had lowered the waters of the two rivers at Wuhan, so they seized boats to build floating bridges bound with iron chains straight to the city walls and attacked each gate in turn.

sentences.zh: 向榮馳至，約城內夾攻，巡撫常大淳慮城啟有失，不許。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong hurried up and proposed a coordinated attack from within and without the city; Provincial Governor Chang Dachun feared that opening the gates would invite disaster and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong hurried up and proposed a coordinated assault from inside and outside the walls, but Provincial Governor Chang Dachun feared that opening the gates would invite disaster and refused.

sentences.zh: 地雷發，城遂陷。

translations.literal: The land mines were set off and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: The land mines detonated and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 秀全出令，民人蓄髮束冠巾，建高臺小別山下，演說弔民伐罪之意。

translations.literal: Xiuquan issued orders that the people should let their hair grow and bind it in caps and turbans; he built a high platform below Xiaobie Mountain and preached the intent of comforting the people and punishing crime.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuquan ordered the people to let their hair grow and bind it in caps and turbans; he built a high platform below Xiaobie Mountain and preached his mission to succor the people and punish wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 三年，上以賽尚阿久無功，授兩廣總督徐廣縉為欽差大臣。

translations.literal: In the third year, because Sai Shang'a had long achieved nothing, the throne appointed Governor-General Xu Guangjin of the Two Guangs Imperial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, with Sai Shang'a still achieving nothing, the emperor appointed Governor-General Xu Guangjin of the Two Guangs Imperial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時石達開攻武昌，廣縉逗留岳州不敢進，上責其罪，更以向榮為欽差大臣，日夜攻之急，寇棄武昌駕船東下，眾號五十萬，資糧、軍械、子女、財帛盡置舟中，分兩岸步騎夾行，進向九江，下黃州、武昌、蘄水等十四州縣；

translations.literal: At that time Shi Dakai was attacking Wuchang; Guangjin lingered at Yuezhou and dared not advance; the throne blamed his offense and replaced him with Xiang Rong as Imperial Commissioner; day and night the assault pressed hard; the rebels abandoned Wuchang, boarded boats, and went downstream; their numbers were claimed at five hundred thousand; provisions, arms, women and children, and wealth were all placed in the boats; infantry and cavalry marched on both banks in parallel; they advanced toward Jiujiang and took Huangzhou, Wuchang, Qishui, and fourteen prefectures and counties;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai was then attacking Wuchang while Guangjin lingered at Yuezhou and dared not advance; the emperor censured him and replaced him with Xiang Rong as Imperial Commissioner; under relentless assault the rebels abandoned Wuchang and sailed downstream, claiming five hundred thousand followers; they loaded provisions, arms, women, children, and plunder onto the boats while infantry and cavalry marched along both banks; they advanced on Jiujiang and captured Huangzhou, Wuchang, Qishui, and fourteen prefectures and counties;

sentences.zh: 抵廣濟縣，下武穴鎮。

translations.literal: they reached Guangji County and descended on Wuxue Town.
translations.idiomatic: they reached Guangji County and descended on Wuxue Town.

sentences.zh: 兩廣總督陸建瀛率兵二萬餘、船千五百艘上溯，遇寇不戰而走，前軍盡覆，建瀛狼狽還金陵。

translations.literal: Governor-General Lu Jianying of the Two Guangs led more than twenty thousand troops and fifteen hundred boats upstream; when he met the rebels he fled without fighting, the vanguard was wholly destroyed, and Jianying fled in disgrace back to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Lu Jianying of the Two Guangs led more than twenty thousand troops and fifteen hundred boats upstream; when he met the rebels he fled without a fight, his vanguard was annihilated, and Jianying fled in disgrace back to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 寇薄九江而下，收官軍委棄砲仗，破安慶，巡撫蔣文慶死之。

translations.literal: The rebels pressed past Jiujiang downstream, gathered up cannon and equipment abandoned by government troops, broke Anqing, and Provincial Governor Jiang Wenqing died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed past Jiujiang downstream, gathered up cannon and equipment the government troops had abandoned, stormed Anqing, and Provincial Governor Jiang Wenqing was killed.

sentences.zh: 寇奪銀米無算，水陸並進，抵金陵，沿城築壘二十四，具戰船，起新州大勝關迤邐至七洲里止，晝夜環攻，掘地道壞城，守兵潰亂。

translations.literal: The rebels seized untold amounts of silver and grain, advanced by land and water together, reached Jinling, built twenty-four stockades along the walls, equipped war boats, and from Xingzhou Dasheng Pass in a continuous line to Qizhouli; day and night they besieged on all sides, dug tunnels to undermine the walls, and the defenders collapsed in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized untold silver and grain, advanced by land and water, reached Jinling, built twenty-four stockades along the walls, and equipped a fleet from Xingzhou Dasheng Pass all the way to Qizhouli; they besieged the city day and night, dug tunnels to undermine the walls, and the defenders collapsed in disorder.

sentences.zh: 建瀛易服走，為寇所戕。

translations.literal: Jianying changed clothes and fled, but was killed by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Jianying changed clothes and tried to flee, but the rebels killed him.

sentences.zh: 將軍祥厚偕副都統霍隆武等守滿城，二日城陷，皆死之。

translations.literal: General Xianghou together with Vice Commander-in-Chief Huo Longwu and others defended the Manchu quarter; on the second day the city fell and all died.
translations.idiomatic: General Xianghou, Vice Commander-in-Chief Huo Longwu, and others defended the Manchu quarter; on the second day the city fell and they all perished.

sentences.zh: 城中男女死者四萬餘，閹童子三千餘人，洩守城之忿。

translations.literal: Within the city more than forty thousand men and women died, and more than three thousand eunuch boys were killed to vent the rage of the siege.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty thousand men and women died in the city, and more than three thousand eunuch boys were slaughtered to vent the fury of the long siege.

sentences.zh: 秀全既破金陵，遂建偽都，擁精兵六十餘萬。

translations.literal: After Xiuquan had taken Jinling he established a false capital and held more than six hundred thousand picked troops.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiuquan had taken Jinling he made it his capital and commanded more than six hundred thousand seasoned troops.

sentences.zh: 群上頌稱明代後嗣，首謁明太祖陵，舉行祀典。

translations.literal: The assembly praised him as a descendant of the Ming dynasty; he first paid homage at the tomb of the Ming founding emperor and held sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: His followers hailed him as a descendant of the Ming dynasty; he first paid homage at the tomb of the Ming founding emperor and performed the sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 其祝詞曰：「不肖子孫洪秀全得光復我大明先帝南部疆土，登極南京，一遵洪武元年祖制。

translations.literal: The prayer ran: "The unworthy descendant Hong Xiuquan has recovered the southern territories of our Great Ming founding emperor, ascended the throne at Nanjing, and follows entirely the ancestral institutions of the first year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer read, "The unworthy descendant Hong Xiuquan has recovered the southern territories of our Great Ming founding emperor, ascended the throne at Nanjing, and follows entirely the institutions of Hongwu's first year.

sentences.zh: 」軍士夾道呼漢天子者三，頒登極制誥。

translations.literal: " Soldiers lining the road shouted "Son of Heaven of Han" three times, and the accession proclamation was issued.
translations.idiomatic: " Soldiers lining the road shouted "Son of Heaven of Han" three times, and the accession proclamation was promulgated.

sentences.zh: 大封將卒，王分四等，侯為五等。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed generals and soldiers on a grand scale: kings were divided into four grades, marquises into five.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed his generals and soldiers on a grand scale, dividing kings into four grades and marquises into five.

sentences.zh: 設天、地、春、夏、秋、冬六官丞相為六等，殿前三十六檢點為七等，殿前七十二指揮為八等，炎、水、木、金、土正副一百將軍為九等，炎、水、木、金、土九十五總制為十等，炎、水、木、金、土正副一百監軍為十一等，前、後、左、右、中九十五軍帥為十二等，前、後、左、右、中四百四十五師帥為十三等，前、後、左、右、中二千三百七十五旅帥為十四等，前、後、左、右、中一萬一千八百七十五卒長為十五等，前、後、左、右、中四萬七千五百兩司馬為十六等；

translations.literal: He established the six Chancellors of the Heaven, Earth, Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter Offices as the sixth grade; thirty-six Inspectors before the Hall as the seventh; seventy-two Commanders before the Hall as the eighth; one hundred Generals of Fire, Water, Wood, Metal, and Earth, principal and deputy, as the ninth; ninety-five Chief Controllers of Fire, Water, Wood, Metal, and Earth as the tenth; one hundred Military Supervisors of Fire, Water, Wood, Metal, and Earth, principal and deputy, as the eleventh; ninety-five Army Chiefs of Front, Rear, Left, Right, and Center as the twelfth; four hundred forty-five Division Chiefs of Front, Rear, Left, Right, and Center as the thirteenth; two thousand three hundred seventy-five Brigade Chiefs of Front, Rear, Left, Right, and Center as the fourteenth; eleven thousand eight hundred seventy-five Company Chiefs of Front, Rear, Left, Right, and Center as the fifteenth; and forty-seven thousand five hundred Platoon Chiefs of Front, Rear, Left, Right, and Center as the sixteenth;
translations.idiomatic: He established six grades of Chancellor for the Heaven, Earth, Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter Offices; thirty-six Hall Inspectors as the seventh grade; seventy-two Hall Commanders as the eighth; one hundred Generals of Fire, Water, Wood, Metal, and Earth as the ninth; ninety-five Chief Controllers as the tenth; one hundred Military Supervisors as the eleventh; ninety-five Army Chiefs for the front, rear, left, right, and center as the twelfth; four hundred forty-five Division Chiefs as the thirteenth; two thousand three hundred seventy-five Brigade Chiefs as the fourteenth; eleven thousand eight hundred seventy-five Company Chiefs as the fifteenth; and forty-seven thousand five hundred Platoon Chiefs as the sixteenth;

sentences.zh: 又自檢點以下至兩司馬，皆有職同名目。

translations.literal: Moreover from Inspectors down to Platoon Chiefs, each office had duties and a corresponding title.
translations.idiomatic: From Inspectors down to Platoon Chiefs, every rank had defined duties and a matching title.

sentences.zh: 其制大抵分朝內、軍中、守土三途：朝內官如掌朝門左右史之類，名目繁多，日新月異；

translations.literal: The system broadly divided into three paths—court, army, and territorial administration: court officials such as keepers of the court gates and left and right recorders were numerous in title and changed day by day;
translations.idiomatic: The system fell broadly into three branches—court, army, and territorial administration: court officials such as keepers of the palace gates and left and right recorders multiplied in title and changed almost daily;

sentences.zh: 軍中官為總制、監軍、軍帥、師帥、旅帥、卒長、兩司馬，凡攻城略地，嘗以國宗或丞相領軍，而練士卒，分隊伍，屯營結壘，接陣進師，皆責成軍帥，由監軍總制上達於領兵大帥以取決焉，其大小相制，臂使指應，統系分明，甚得馭眾之道；

translations.literal: army officials were Chief Controllers, Military Supervisors, Army Chiefs, Division Chiefs, Brigade Chiefs, Company Chiefs, and Platoon Chiefs; whenever they stormed cities or seized territory they often had a royal clansman or Chancellor lead the army, while drilling soldiers, dividing units, encamping and building stockades, and joining battle to advance—all were charged to the Army Chiefs, reported upward by Military Supervisors and Chief Controllers to the commanding general for decision; great and small checked one another, moving like arm and fingers, the chain of command clear, and they were very skilled in the way of controlling masses;
translations.idiomatic: army officials included Chief Controllers, Military Supervisors, Army Chiefs, Division Chiefs, Brigade Chiefs, Company Chiefs, and Platoon Chiefs; when storming cities or seizing territory they often placed a royal clansman or Chancellor at the head of the army, while drilling troops, dividing units, building camps and stockades, and advancing into battle were all the responsibility of the Army Chiefs, reported upward through Military Supervisors and Chief Controllers to the commanding general for final decision; ranks checked one another in a clear chain of command that moved like arm and fingers, and they were remarkably adept at controlling large forces;

sentences.zh: 守土官為郡總制、州縣監軍、鄉軍帥、鄉師帥、鄉旅帥、鄉卒長、鄉兩司馬，凡地方獄訟錢糧，由軍帥、監軍區畫，而取成於總制，民事之重，皆得決之。

translations.literal: territorial officials were Prefectural Chief Controllers, District and County Military Supervisors, Township Army Chiefs, Township Division Chiefs, Township Brigade Chiefs, Township Company Chiefs, and Township Platoon Chiefs; all local lawsuits, taxes, and grain were laid out by Army Chiefs and Military Supervisors and finalized by Chief Controllers, and weighty civil matters could all be decided by them.
translations.idiomatic: territorial officials included Prefectural Chief Controllers, District and County Military Supervisors, and Township Army, Division, Brigade, Company, and Platoon Chiefs; local lawsuits, taxes, and grain were organized by Army Chiefs and Military Supervisors and finalized by Chief Controllers, who could decide even the weightiest civil matters.

sentences.zh: 自都金陵，分兵攻克府、廳、州、縣，遂即其地分軍，立軍帥以下各官，而統於監軍，鎮以總制，監軍、總制受命於偽朝。

translations.literal: From the time he made Jinling his capital he divided forces to take prefectures, departments, districts, and counties, then in each place divided armies, established officials from Army Chiefs downward, placed them under Military Supervisors, garrisoned them with Chief Controllers, and Military Supervisors and Chief Controllers received orders from the false court.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jinling became his capital he sent forces to capture prefectures, departments, districts, and counties, then in each place divided the armies, appointed officials from Army Chiefs downward, placed them under Military Supervisors and garrisoned them with Chief Controllers, all of whom received orders from the rebel court.

sentences.zh: 自軍帥至兩司馬為鄉官，鄉官者以其鄉人為之也。

translations.literal: From Army Chief down to Platoon Chief served as township officials; township officials were appointed from men of that township.
translations.idiomatic: From Army Chief down to Platoon Chief they served as township officials, drawn from the local populace of each township.

sentences.zh: 軍帥兼理軍民之政，師帥、旅帥、卒長、兩司馬以次相承，皆如軍制。

translations.literal: The Army Chief concurrently administered both military and civilian affairs; Division Chiefs, Brigade Chiefs, Company Chiefs, and Platoon Chiefs succeeded one another in rank, all following the army system.
translations.idiomatic: The Army Chief handled both military and civilian government, while Division Chiefs, Brigade Chiefs, Company Chiefs, and Platoon Chiefs formed a descending chain modeled on the army organization.

sentences.zh: 此外又有女官，曰女軍師、女丞相、女檢點、女指揮、女將軍、女總制、女監軍、女軍帥、女卒長、女管長，即兩司馬也，共女官六千五百八十四人。

translations.literal: Beyond this there were also female officials, called Female Strategist, Female Chancellor, Female Inspector, Female Commander, Female General, Female Chief Controller, Female Military Supervisor, Female Army Chief, Female Company Chief, and Female Platoon Chief—the latter being Platoon Chiefs—numbering six thousand five hundred eighty-four female officials in all.
translations.idiomatic: There were also female officials—Female Strategist, Female Chancellor, Female Inspector, Female Commander, Female General, Female Chief Controller, Female Military Supervisor, Female Army Chief, Female Company Chief, and Female Platoon Chief (equivalent to Platoon Chief)—six thousand five hundred eighty-four in all.

sentences.zh: 女軍四十，女兵十萬人，而職同官名目亦同。

translations.literal: There were forty women's armies and one hundred thousand women soldiers, with duties and official titles identical to those of the male officials.
translations.idiomatic: They fielded forty women's armies with one hundred thousand women soldiers, whose duties and titles mirrored those of the men.

sentences.zh: 總計男女官三十餘萬，而臨時增設及恩賞各偽職尚不在此數也。

translations.literal: In all, male and female officials exceeded three hundred thousand, not counting those appointed temporarily or granted false titles as rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Male and female officials together exceeded three hundred thousand, not counting temporary appointments or reward grants of false offices.

sentences.zh: 其軍制，每一軍領一萬二千五百人，以軍帥統之，總制、監軍監之。

translations.literal: Their army organization: each army led twelve thousand five hundred men, commanded by an Army Chief and overseen by Chief Controllers and Military Supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: In their army system each corps mustered twelve thousand five hundred men under an Army Chief, with Chief Controllers and Military Supervisors supervising.

sentences.zh: 其下則各轄五師帥，各分領二千五百人。

translations.literal: Beneath them each commanded five Division Chiefs, each leading two thousand five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Below them each army had five Division Chiefs, each commanding two thousand five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 每師帥轄五旅帥，各分領五百人。

translations.literal: Each Division Chief commanded five Brigade Chiefs, each leading five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Each Division Chief oversaw five Brigade Chiefs, each with five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 每旅帥轄五卒長，各分領百人。

translations.literal: Each Brigade Chief commanded five Company Chiefs, each leading one hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Each Brigade Chief oversaw five Company Chiefs, each with one hundred men.

sentences.zh: 每卒長轄四兩司馬，每兩司馬領伍長五人，伍卒二十人，共二十五人。

translations.literal: Each Company Chief commanded four Platoon Chiefs; each Platoon Chief led five Squad Chiefs and twenty soldiers, twenty-five men in all.
translations.idiomatic: Each Company Chief commanded four Platoon Chiefs; each Platoon Chief led five Squad Chiefs and twenty soldiers—twenty-five men per platoon.

sentences.zh: 其陣法有四：曰牽陣法。

translations.literal: Their battle formations were four in number: first, the Linked Formation.
translations.idiomatic: They had four battle formations. The first was the Linked Formation.

sentences.zh: 凡由此至彼，必下令作牽陣行走法。

translations.literal: Whenever marching from one place to another, they always ordered the Linked Formation marching method.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they moved from one place to another, they ordered troops to march in the Linked Formation.

sentences.zh: 每兩司馬執一旗，後隨二十五人。

translations.literal: Each Platoon Chief carried one banner, with twenty-five men following behind.
translations.idiomatic: Each Platoon Chief bore a banner with twenty-five men trailing behind.

sentences.zh: 百人則間卒長一旗，五百人則間旅帥一旗，二千五百人則間師帥一旗，一萬二千五百人則間軍帥一旗，軍帥、監軍、總制乘輿馬隨行。

translations.literal: At every hundred men a Company Chief's banner was interposed, at every five hundred a Brigade Chief's, at every two thousand five hundred a Division Chief's, at every twelve thousand five hundred an Army Chief's; Army Chiefs, Military Supervisors, and Chief Controllers rode in carriages alongside.
translations.idiomatic: Every hundred men a Company Chief's banner appeared, every five hundred a Brigade Chief's, every two thousand five hundred a Division Chief's, and every twelve thousand five hundred an Army Chief's, while Army Chiefs, Military Supervisors, and Chief Controllers rode in carriages alongside.

sentences.zh: 一軍盡，一軍續進。

translations.literal: When one army had passed, the next army continued forward.
translations.idiomatic: One army would finish passing before the next advanced.

sentences.zh: 寬路則令雙行，狹路單行，魚貫以進。

translations.literal: On wide roads they were ordered to march double file; on narrow roads single file, advancing like a strung fish.
translations.idiomatic: On wide roads they marched two abreast; on narrow roads single file, moving in a continuous line like a strung fish.

sentences.zh: 凡行軍亂其行列者斬。

translations.literal: Whoever on the march disturbed the ranks was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who broke formation on the march was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 其牽線行走時，一遇敵軍，首尾蟠屈鉤連，頃刻岔集。

translations.literal: When the linked line was marching and suddenly met enemy troops, head and tail would coil and hook together, assembling in an instant though scattered.
translations.idiomatic: If the linked column met the enemy while marching, front and rear would coil and link together, gathering into formation in an instant.

sentences.zh: 敗則聞敲金方退，仍牽線以行，不得斜奔旁逸。

translations.literal: On defeat they withdrew only upon hearing the striking of gongs, still marching in linked formation and not daring to flee diagonally or break away to the side.
translations.idiomatic: In retreat they withdrew only at the sound of gongs, still keeping the linked formation and never bolting sideways or scattering.

sentences.zh: 曰螃蟹陣。

translations.literal: Second, the Crab Formation.
translations.idiomatic: The second was the Crab Formation.

sentences.zh: 乃三隊平列陣也。

translations.literal: This was a formation of three columns arrayed level.
translations.idiomatic: It was a three-column formation deployed on a level front.

sentences.zh: 中一隊人數少，兩翼人數多。

translations.literal: The center column had fewer men; the two wings had more.
translations.idiomatic: The center column was smaller; both wings were larger.

sentences.zh: 其法視敵軍分幾隊，即變陣以應之。

translations.literal: The method was to observe how many columns the enemy deployed and change formation to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: They watched how many enemy columns appeared and shifted formation to match.

sentences.zh: 如敵軍僅左右隊，即以中隊分益左右，亦為兩隊。

translations.literal: If the enemy had only left and right columns, the center column would be divided to reinforce left and right, likewise becoming two columns.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy fielded only left and right wings, they split the center to reinforce both sides, forming two columns.

sentences.zh: 如敵軍前後各一隊，則分左右翼之前鋒為一隊，以後半與中一隊合而平列，為前隊接應。

translations.literal: If the enemy had one column before and one behind, the vanguards of the left and right wings would be made one column, and the rear half joined with the center column and arrayed level, forming a forward column in support.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy advanced in front and rear columns, they detached the left and right vanguards into one column and merged the rear half with the center into a supporting front line.

sentences.zh: 如敵軍左右何隊兵多，則變偏左右翼以與之敵。

translations.literal: If either left or right enemy column had more troops, they would shift the left or right wing obliquely to engage it.
translations.idiomatic: Whichever enemy wing was stronger, they angled the corresponding wing to meet it.

sentences.zh: 如敵軍分四五隊，亦分為四五隊次第迎拒。

translations.literal: If the enemy divided into four or five columns, they likewise divided into four or five columns to meet and resist in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy split into four or five columns, they fielded four or five columns in turn to meet them.

sentences.zh: 其大陣包小陣法，或先以小隊嘗敵，後出大陣包之；

translations.literal: Their method of a large formation enveloping a small one: sometimes they first sent a small detachment to test the enemy, then brought out the large formation to envelop them;
translations.idiomatic: For large formations enveloping small ones, they sometimes sent a small unit to probe the enemy, then deployed the main force to surround them;

sentences.zh: 或詐敗誘敵追，伏兵四起以包敵軍，窮極變化。

translations.literal: or they feigned defeat to lure the enemy in pursuit, then ambush troops rose on all sides to envelop the enemy army—changes beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: or they feigned defeat to draw pursuit, then ambush troops sprang up on every side to trap the enemy—endlessly varied.

sentences.zh: 至於損左益右，移後置前，臨時指揮，操之司令，兵士悉視大旗所往而奔赴之，無敢或後。

translations.literal: As for weakening the left to strengthen the right, moving the rear to the front, and commanding on the spot, the commander-in-chief wielded it; soldiers all watched whither the great banner went and rushed there, none daring to lag behind.
translations.idiomatic: They could strip the left to reinforce the right or shift the rear to the front at a word from the commander; every soldier watched the great banner and rushed where it pointed, none daring to hang back.

sentences.zh: 曰百鳥陣。

translations.literal: Third, the Hundred Birds Formation.
translations.idiomatic: The third was the Hundred Birds Formation.

sentences.zh: 此陣用之平原曠野，以二十五人為一小隊，分百數十隊，散布如星，使敵軍驚疑，不知其數之多寡。

translations.literal: This formation was used on open plains and wild fields: twenty-five men formed one small squad, divided into scores or hundreds of squads scattered like stars, so that the enemy army would be startled and uncertain whether their numbers were many or few.
translations.idiomatic: Used on open ground, it broke the force into squads of twenty-five, scores or hundreds of them scattered like stars so the enemy could not tell how many they faced.

sentences.zh: 敵軍氣餒，即合而攻之。

translations.literal: When the enemy army's spirit was broken, they would unite and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Once enemy morale broke, the squads converged to attack.

sentences.zh: 曰伏地陣。

translations.literal: Fourth, the Ground-Lying Formation.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth was the Ground-Lying Formation.

sentences.zh: 敵兵追北至山窮水阻之地，忽一旗偃，千旗齊偃，瞬息千里，皆伏地不見。

translations.literal: When enemy troops pursued them north to places where mountains ended and water blocked the way, suddenly one banner would drop and a thousand banners drop together; in an instant for a thousand li all lay on the ground and vanished.
translations.idiomatic: When pursuit drove them into mountains or against water, one banner would drop and a thousand with it; in a flash their host vanished along miles of ground as if swallowed by the earth.

sentences.zh: 敵軍見前寂無一卒，詫異徘徊。

translations.literal: The enemy army saw not a single soldier ahead and, astonished, hesitated and wandered.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers saw not a man ahead and halted in astonished confusion.

sentences.zh: 賊伏半時，忽一旗立，千旗齊立，急趨撲敵，往往轉敗為勝。

translations.literal: The rebels lay hidden half a watch; then suddenly one banner rose and a thousand banners rose together, rushing swiftly to strike the enemy, often turning defeat into victory.
translations.idiomatic: After half a watch the rebels lay hidden; then one banner rose, a thousand rose with it, and they charged—often snatching victory from defeat.

sentences.zh: 其營壘或夾江、夾河、浮筏、阻山、據村市，及包敵營，為營動合古法。

translations.literal: Their stockades might straddle rivers, straddle streams, use floating rafts, block mountains, occupy market towns, or surround enemy camps—building camps and combining them followed ancient methods.
translations.idiomatic: Their camps might span rivers, use pontoon rafts, cling to mountains, occupy market towns, or ring enemy encampments, all in ways that echoed classical encampment practice.

sentences.zh: 每數營必立一望樓瞭敵。

translations.literal: Every several camps they invariably erected a watchtower to observe the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Every few camps they built a watchtower to spy on the enemy.

sentences.zh: 守城無布帳，每五垛架木為板屋。

translations.literal: In defending cities they used no cloth tents; every five crenellations they erected a wooden plank shelter.
translations.idiomatic: When defending cities they used no cloth tents; every five crenellations they built a wooden plank shelter on the wall.

sentences.zh: 木牆、土牆亦環庋板屋。

translations.literal: Wooden walls and earthen walls likewise had plank shelters built along them.
translations.idiomatic: Wooden and earthen walls likewise had plank shelters ranged along them.

sentences.zh: 地當敵衝，則浚重壕，築重牆，壕務寬深，密插竹簽。

translations.literal: Where the ground lay in the enemy's path of attack, they dug deep moats and built double walls; moats were made wide and deep, and bamboo spikes were densely planted.
translations.idiomatic: On threatened ground they dug deep moats and raised double walls—moats as wide and deep as possible, thick with planted bamboo spikes.

sentences.zh: 重牆用雙層板片，約以橫木，虛其中如複壁，中填沙石塼土。

translations.literal: Double walls used twin layers of boards braced with crossbeams, hollow in the middle like a double wall, filled within with sand, stone, and brick.
translations.idiomatic: Double walls were twin board skins tied with crossbeams, hollow like a cavity wall and packed with sand, stone, and brick.

sentences.zh: 築二重牆築物無定，或密排樹株，或積鹽包、糖包，及水浸棉花包，異常堅固。

translations.literal: Materials for building double walls were not fixed: sometimes trees were densely planted in rows, sometimes salt bags or sugar bags were piled, or cotton bales soaked in water—exceptionally solid.
translations.idiomatic: Fill for double walls varied: they might plant trees in tight rows, stack salt or sugar sacks, or pack water-soaked cotton bales—making them extraordinarily strong.

sentences.zh: 其攻城專恃地道，謂之鼇翻。

translations.literal: In storming cities they relied solely on tunnels, calling the method Turtle's Overturn.
translations.idiomatic: For sieges they relied chiefly on mining, which they called Turtle's Overturn.

sentences.zh: 土營而外，又有木營、金營。

translations.literal: Beyond the Earth Corps there were also the Wood Corps and the Metal Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Besides the Earth Corps they had Wood and Metal Corps as well.

sentences.zh: 組織諸匠，各營以指揮統之。

translations.literal: They organized all craftsmen, each corps being commanded by a Commander.
translations.idiomatic: They grouped craftsmen by corps, each under a Commander.

sentences.zh: 其總制至兩司馬皆如土營之制。

translations.literal: From Chief Controller down to Platoon Chief all followed the organization of the Earth Corps.
translations.idiomatic: From Chief Controller down to Platoon Chief their ranks mirrored the Earth Corps.

sentences.zh: 立水營九軍，每軍以軍帥統之。

translations.literal: They established nine naval armies, each army commanded by an Army Chief.
translations.idiomatic: They raised nine naval armies, each led by an Army Chief.

sentences.zh: 但未經訓練，不能作戰，專以船多威敵而已。

translations.literal: But they had not been trained and could not fight; they relied solely on numerous ships to overawe the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: These crews were untrained and could not fight; they counted only on numbers of ships to intimidate the enemy.

sentences.zh: 其旗幟亦有差等，偽東王黃綢旗，紅字綠緣，方一丈；

translations.literal: Their banners also had grades of distinction: the false Eastern King's yellow silk banner, red characters with green border, one square zhang;
translations.idiomatic: Their banners too were graded: the false Eastern King flew yellow silk with red characters and a green border, one square zhang;

sentences.zh: 以下皆黃綢旗、紅字，而以緣別。

translations.literal: below him all were yellow silk banners with red characters, distinguished by the border.
translations.idiomatic: below him all used yellow silk with red characters, the border color marking rank.

sentences.zh: 如偽西王白緣，偽南王紫緣，偽北王黑緣。

translations.literal: The false Western King had a white border, the false Southern King a purple border, the false Northern King a black border.
translations.idiomatic: The false Western King had a white border, the false Southern King purple, the false Northern King black.

sentences.zh: 偽翼王藍緣，其尺丈長闊則以五寸遞減。

translations.literal: The false Winged King had a blue border; length and width diminished by five cun at each step.
translations.idiomatic: The false Winged King had a blue border; each lower rank lost five cun in length and width.

sentences.zh: 豫王、燕王皆黃綢尖旗、紅字、水紅緣，國宗黃綢尖旗、紅字。

translations.literal: The Princes of Yu and Yan both had pointed yellow silk banners, red characters, and pink borders; royal clansmen had pointed yellow silk banners with red characters.
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Yu and Yan carried pointed yellow silk with red characters and pink borders; royal clansmen carried pointed yellow silk with red characters.

sentences.zh: 其緣視何王國宗，即從何色，皆長闊八尺。

translations.literal: The border followed whichever prince or royal clansman one served; all were eight chi in length and width.
translations.idiomatic: Border color matched one's prince or clansman; all were eight chi square.

sentences.zh: 侯，黃綢尖旗，長闊七尺八寸。

translations.literal: Marquises: pointed yellow silk banners, seven chi eight cun in length and width.
translations.idiomatic: Marquises: pointed yellow silk banners, seven chi eight cun square.

sentences.zh: 丞相，黃綢尖旗，長闊七尺五寸。

translations.literal: Chancellors: pointed yellow silk banners, seven chi five cun in length and width.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors: pointed yellow silk banners, seven chi five cun square.

sentences.zh: 檢點，黃綢尖旗，長闊七尺。

translations.literal: Inspectors: pointed yellow silk banners, seven chi in length and width.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors: pointed yellow silk banners, seven chi square.

sentences.zh: 以上皆紅字、水紅緣。

translations.literal: All the above had red characters and pink borders.
translations.idiomatic: All of these bore red characters with pink borders.

sentences.zh: 指揮，黃綢尖旗，黑字、水紅緣，長闊六尺五寸。

translations.literal: Commanders: pointed yellow silk banners, black characters and pink border, six chi five cun in length and width.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders: pointed yellow silk with black characters and pink border, six chi five cun square.

sentences.zh: 將軍至兩司馬，皆黃旗無緣，形尖，黑字，自長闊六尺以下遞減至二尺五寸。

translations.literal: From General down to Platoon Chief, all had plain yellow banners without borders, pointed in shape, with black characters, decreasing from six chi in length and width down to two chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: From General down to Platoon Chief all flew plain pointed yellow banners without borders and with black characters, stepping down from six chi square to two chi five cun.

sentences.zh: 每一軍大小黃旗至六百五十六面之多。

translations.literal: Each army had as many as six hundred fifty-six large and small yellow banners.
translations.idiomatic: A single army might carry as many as six hundred fifty-six yellow banners large and small.

sentences.zh: 軍中號令，惟擊鼓、敲金、吹螺、搖旗。

translations.literal: Army signals relied solely on beating drums, striking gongs, blowing conch shells, and waving banners.
translations.idiomatic: Army commands used only drums, gongs, conch horns, and banner signals.

sentences.zh: 凡起行出隊，俱擂鼓、吹螺、搖旗以集眾。

translations.literal: Whenever setting out or leaving ranks, they all beat drums, blew conch shells, and waved banners to assemble the host.
translations.idiomatic: To march out or muster, they beat drums, blew conchs, and waved banners to gather the troops.

sentences.zh: 打仗則擊鼓吶喊，收隊則鳴鉦。

translations.literal: In battle they beat drums and shouted; in withdrawing ranks they sounded gongs.
translations.idiomatic: In combat they drummed and shouted; to recall units they clanged gongs.

sentences.zh: 有老軍、新軍、童子軍。

translations.literal: There were veteran armies, new armies, and youth armies.
translations.idiomatic: They fielded veteran, new, and youth corps.

sentences.zh: 尤善用間諜，混入敵營。

translations.literal: They were especially skilled at using spies, mixing into enemy camps.
translations.idiomatic: They were especially adept at espionage, slipping agents into enemy camps.

sentences.zh: 又能取遠勢，聲東擊西，就虛避實，其以進為退，以退為進，往往令人不測，墮其術中。

translations.literal: They could also take distant positions, strike east while attacking west, hit emptiness and avoid solidity; advancing as though retreating and retreating as though advancing, they often made their moves impossible to foresee, and men fell into their stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: They seized distant advantages, feinted east and struck west, struck voids and avoided strength, and advanced as if retreating or retreated as if advancing—moves so unpredictable that opponents routinely fell into their traps.

sentences.zh: 此其行軍之大略也。

translations.literal: This is the broad outline of their marching.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the broad outline of their campaigning.

sentences.zh: 其服色尚黃。

translations.literal: Their dress color favored yellow.
translations.idiomatic: They favored yellow in dress.

sentences.zh: 偽天王金冠，雕鏤龍鳳，如圓規沙帽式，上繡滿天星斗，下繡一統山河，中留空格，鑿金為「天王」二字。

translations.literal: The false Heavenly King's golden crown, carved and inlaid with dragons and phoenixes, was like a circular gauze-cap style; the upper part was embroidered with stars filling the sky, the lower with a unified mountains and rivers, a blank space left in the center, and gold cut to form the two characters "Heavenly King."
translations.idiomatic: The false Heavenly King wore a golden crown carved with dragons and phoenixes in the style of a round gauze cap: stars across the upper band, mountains and rivers below, and a blank center inset with gilt characters reading Heavenly King.

sentences.zh: 東王、北王、翼王冠如古兜鍪式，冠額繡雙龍單鳳，中立金字職銜。

translations.literal: The Eastern King, Northern King, and Winged King wore crowns like ancient helmets; the brow was embroidered with twin dragons and a single phoenix, and gilt characters for their office stood in the center.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern, Northern, and Winged Kings wore helmet-style crowns with twin dragons and a single phoenix on the brow and gilt rank titles in the center.

sentences.zh: 國宗略同諸王式。

translations.literal: Royal clansmen were largely the same as the princes' style.
translations.idiomatic: Royal clansmen followed the princes' style with little difference.

sentences.zh: 自檢點至兩司馬，皆獸頭兜鍪式，帽上龍以節數分等差。

translations.literal: From Inspector down to Platoon Chief, all wore beast-head helmet style; dragons on the cap were graded by the number of segments.
translations.idiomatic: From Inspector down to Platoon Chief all wore beast-head helmets, the dragon segments on the cap marking rank.

sentences.zh: 如諸王九節，侯相七節，檢點、指揮、將軍五節，總制、監軍、軍帥三節是也。

translations.literal: Princes had nine segments, marquises and chancellors seven, inspectors, commanders, and generals five, and chief controllers, military supervisors, and army chiefs three—such was the rule.
translations.idiomatic: Princes bore nine segments, marquises and chancellors seven, inspectors, commanders, and generals five, and chief controllers, military supervisors, and army chiefs three.

sentences.zh: 袍服則黃龍袍、紅袍、黃紅馬褂。

translations.literal: Robe attire consisted of yellow dragon robes, red robes, and yellow-red jackets.
translations.idiomatic: Robes included yellow dragon gowns, red gowns, and yellow-red jackets.

sentences.zh: 偽天王黃緞袍，繡九龍。

translations.literal: The false Heavenly King wore a yellow satin robe embroidered with nine dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The false Heavenly King wore yellow satin embroidered with nine dragons.

sentences.zh: 自諸王以下至侯相，遞減至四龍。

translations.literal: From the princes down to marquises and chancellors, the number decreased step by step to four dragons.
translations.idiomatic: From princes down through marquises and chancellors the dragon count stepped down to four.

sentences.zh: 檢點素黃袍，指揮至兩司馬皆素紅袍。

translations.literal: Inspectors wore plain yellow robes; from Commander down to Platoon Chief all wore plain red robes.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors wore unadorned yellow robes; commanders through platoon chiefs wore plain red.

sentences.zh: 自偽王至兩司馬，皆繡職銜於馬褂前團內。

translations.literal: From the false kings down to Platoon Chiefs, all embroidered their office title within the round medallion on the front of the jacket.
translations.idiomatic: From false kings down to platoon chiefs each embroidered his title in the roundel on the jacket breast.

sentences.zh: 儀衞輿馬，諸王皆黃緞轎繡雲龍，侯、相、檢點、指揮皆紅緞轎，將軍、總制、監軍綠轎，軍帥、師帥、旅帥藍轎，卒長、兩司馬黑轎。

translations.literal: For ceremonial guard, carriages, and horses: all princes had yellow satin sedan chairs embroidered with cloud dragons; marquises, chancellors, inspectors, and commanders had red satin sedan chairs; generals, chief controllers, and military supervisors had green sedan chairs; army chiefs, division chiefs, and brigade chiefs had blue sedan chairs; company chiefs and platoon chiefs had black sedan chairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial transport ran by rank: princes rode yellow satin sedans embroidered with cloud dragons; marquises, chancellors, inspectors, and commanders red satin; generals, chief controllers, and military supervisors green; army, division, and brigade chiefs blue; company and platoon chiefs black.

sentences.zh: 至金陵，始建宮室，毀總督署，復擴民居以廣其址，役夫萬餘，窮極奢麗。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Jinling they first built palaces, demolished the governor-general's yamen, and again expanded by tearing down commoners' houses to enlarge the site; more than ten thousand laborers were impressed, with luxury pushed to the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinling they first raised palaces, razed the governor-general's compound, and seized more commoners' homes to widen the grounds—over ten thousand laborers toiled in extravagant splendor.

sentences.zh: 雕鏤螭龍、鳥獸、花木，多以金為之。

translations.literal: Carved dragons, birds, beasts, and flowers were mostly wrought in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Carvings of dragons, birds, beasts, and flowers were largely wrought in gold.

sentences.zh: 偽王皆建偽府，馮雲山、蕭朝貴早授首，其子亦襲封建府。

translations.literal: All false kings established false mansions; Feng Yunshan and Xiao Chaogui had long since been executed, yet their sons also inherited enfeoffment and built mansions.
translations.idiomatic: Every false king maintained a false mansion; though Feng Yunshan and Xiao Chaogui had been executed early, their sons were enfeoffed and built mansions in turn.

sentences.zh: 其宗教制度，半效西洋。

translations.literal: Their religious institutions half imitated the West.
translations.idiomatic: Their religious institutions were half modeled on Western practice.

sentences.zh: 日登高殿，集眾演說，與人民以自由權，解婦人拘束。

translations.literal: Daily they ascended the high hall, gathered the multitude for preaching, granted the people rights of freedom, and released women from restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Each day they mounted the high hall to preach to the masses, proclaiming popular freedom and lifting constraints on women.

sentences.zh: 定偽律六十二條，最為慘酷。

translations.literal: They codified sixty-two false laws, the most cruel.
translations.idiomatic: They enacted sixty-two false statutes, among the most brutal known.

sentences.zh: 然行軍嚴搶奪之令，官軍在三十里外，始准擄劫；

translations.literal: Yet on the march they strictly enforced orders against plunder: government troops had to be thirty li away before looting was permitted;
translations.idiomatic: Yet on campaign they enforced strict plunder rules: only when government troops lay thirty li distant might looting begin;

sentences.zh: 若官軍在前，有取民間尺布、百錢者，殺無赦。

translations.literal: if government troops were ahead, anyone who took so much as a foot of cloth or a hundred cash from the populace was executed without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: if imperial forces were nearer, taking even a foot of cloth or a hundred cash from civilians meant summary execution.

sentences.zh: 於安慶大星橋設榷關，撥砲船十艘，環以鐵索，木筏橫截江濱，以防偷漏。

translations.literal: At the Great Star Bridge in Anqing they established a monopoly pass, deployed ten gunboats ringed with iron chains, and timber rafts stretched across the riverbank to prevent smuggling.
translations.idiomatic: At Anqing's Great Star Bridge they set a revenue barrier, moored ten gunboats linked by iron chains, and stretched timber rafts across the shore to block smuggling.

sentences.zh: 九江、蕪湖，及沿江州縣岔河、小港地當衝要者，一律設立偽卡，徵收雜稅。

translations.literal: At Jiujiang, Wuhu, and wherever along the river districts a forked river or small inlet lay on a vital route, they uniformly established false checkpoints to levy miscellaneous taxes.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiujiang, Wuhu, and every vital fork or inlet along the Yangtze they posted false customs stations to collect miscellaneous levies.

sentences.zh: 此其建國大略也。

translations.literal: This is the broad outline of their state-building.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the broad outline of how they built their rebel state.

sentences.zh: 既都金陵，欲圖河北，羅大綱曰：「欲圖北必先定河南。

translations.literal: Once they had made Jinling their capital and wished to scheme for Hebei, Luo Dagang said: "To scheme north one must first secure Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After making Jinling their capital they turned toward Hebei; Luo Dagang said, "To march north you must first secure Henan.

sentences.zh: 大駕駐河南，軍乃渡河，至皖、豫一出。

translations.literal: Station the imperial presence in Henan, then the army may cross the river; one sortie from Anhui and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Place the imperial seat in Henan, then cross the river—a single thrust out of Anhui and Henan.

sentences.zh: 否則先定南九省，無內顧憂，然後三路出師：一出湘、楚；

translations.literal: Otherwise first secure the nine southern provinces without worry for the rear, then send three armies forth: one out through Hunan and Hubei;
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise secure the nine southern provinces first so the rear is safe, then advance on three fronts: one through Hunan and Hubei;

sentences.zh: 一出漢中，疾趨咸陽；

translations.literal: one out through Hanzhong, hurrying to Xianyang;
translations.idiomatic: one through Hanzhong straight for Xianyang;

sentences.zh: 以徐、揚席捲山左，再出山右，會獵燕都。

translations.literal: with Xu and Yang rolling up Shandong, then emerging west of the mountains, joining in a hunt at the Yan capital.
translations.idiomatic: and with Xu and Yang sweeping Shandong, then coming west of the mountains to rendezvous at the Yan capital.

sentences.zh: 若懸軍深入，犯險無後援，必敗之道也。

translations.literal: If one suspends the army and penetrates deep, courting danger without rear support, that is the path of certain defeat.
translations.idiomatic: To drive deep alone without rear support is the sure road to defeat.

sentences.zh: 且既都金陵，宜多備戰艦，精練水師，然後可戰可守。

translations.literal: Moreover, having made Jinling the capital, one should prepare many warships in abundance and drill the navy with care; only then can one fight and hold.
translations.idiomatic: And with Jinling as capital they should build a large fleet and train the navy thoroughly—only then could they fight and hold.

sentences.zh: 若待粵之拖罟咸集長江，則運道梗矣。

translations.literal: If one waits until Guangdong's tow-net vessels all gather on the Yangtze, the transport route will be blocked.
translations.idiomatic: If we wait until Guangdong's war junks all mass on the Yangtze, the grain route will be severed.

sentences.zh: 今宜先備木筏，堵截江面，以待戰艦之成，猶可及也。

translations.literal: Now one ought first to prepare timber rafts, block the river surface, and wait for the warships to be completed—it can still be in time.
translations.idiomatic: We should prepare rafts now and seal the river while the fleet is built—it is not yet too late.

sentences.zh: 」秀清方專政，不納。

translations.literal: " Yang Xiuqing was then monopolizing government power and would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiuqing held sole power at the time and rejected the counsel.

sentences.zh: 乃遣偽丞相林鳳祥、李開芳、羅大綱、曾立昌率眾東下，秀全詔之曰：「師行間道，疾趨燕都，無貪攻城奪地糜時日。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent the false chancellors Lin Fengxiang, Li Kaifang, Luo Dagang, and Zeng Lichang to lead the masses eastward; Xiuquan charged them, saying: "The army shall march by bypaths, hurry to the Yan capital, and not be greedy to storm cities and seize territory, wasting days."
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched the rebel chancellors Lin Fengxiang, Li Kaifang, Luo Dagang, and Zeng Lichang eastward at the head of a great host. Xiuquan ordered them: "March by hidden routes, press swiftly on the Yan capital, and do not waste time besieging towns and seizing territory."

sentences.zh: 」大綱語人曰：「天下未定，乃欲安居此都，其能久乎？

translations.literal: " Dagang said to others: "The realm is not yet settled, yet you wish to dwell at peace in this capital—can that last long?"
translations.idiomatic: Dagang told others, "The empire is not yet won, yet they mean to settle peacefully in this capital—how long can that endure?"

sentences.zh: 吾屬無類矣！

translations.literal: Our sort will be wiped out without remnant!
translations.idiomatic: None of us will survive!

sentences.zh: 二月，林鳳祥等陷鎮江、揚州，令吳如孝等留守，分據浦口、瓜洲諸隘。

translations.literal: In the second month Lin Fengxiang and others took Zhenjiang and Yangzhou, ordered Wu Ruxiao and others to remain on garrison, and separately held the passes at Pukou and Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Lin Fengxiang and his commanders seized Zhenjiang and Yangzhou, left Wu Ruxiao and others to garrison them, and posted troops at the passes of Pukou and Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 向榮既復武昌，躡寇而東，抵金陵，軍孝陵衞，是謂江南大營。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong having recovered Wuchang, pursued the rebels east, reached Jinling, and encamped at Xiaolingwei—this was called the Jiangnan Grand Camp.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiang Rong recovered Wuchang he pursued the rebels east to Jinling and encamped at Xiaolingwei—the force known as the Jiangnan Grand Camp.

sentences.zh: 都統琦善亦以欽差大臣率直隸、陝西、黑龍江馬步諸軍軍揚州城外，是謂江北大營。

translations.literal: Military governor Qishan also, as Imperial Commissioner, led the cavalry and infantry of Zhili, Shaanxi, and Heilongjiang to encamp outside Yangzhou—this was called the Jiangbei Grand Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Military governor Qishan likewise marched as Imperial Commissioner at the head of Zhili, Shaanxi, and Heilongjiang horse and foot to camp outside Yangzhou—the Jiangbei Grand Camp.

sentences.zh: 三月，向榮破通濟門寇壘，襲占七橋甕，奪獲鍾山圍，殲寇無算，遂移大營逼城而軍。

translations.literal: In the third month Xiang Rong broke the rebel fortifications at Tongji Gate, seized Qiqiao'ao by surprise, captured Zhongshanwei, and destroyed rebels beyond count; he then moved the grand camp to press close and encamp against the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Xiang Rong stormed the rebel works at Tongji Gate, seized Qiqiao'ao by surprise, and took Zhongshanwei, slaughtering rebels beyond count before shifting the grand camp to press the walls.

sentences.zh: 四月，漕運總督楊殿邦進攻揚州，毀城外木城土壘，東路寇悉避入城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Grain Transport Governor Yang Dianbang advanced on Yangzhou, destroyed the wooden walls and earthen ramparts outside the city, and rebels on the eastern route all shrank back into the city.
