translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Grain Transport Governor Yang Dianbang attacked Yangzhou, tore down the wooden walls and earthen works outside the walls, and the eastern rebels all withdrew into the city.

sentences.zh: 琦善、勝保先後督攻，五戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Qishan and Senggebao successively supervised the attacks; in five battles all were victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan and Senggebao took command in turn; five engagements, five victories.

sentences.zh: 鳳祥留立昌踞揚城，驅婦女及所劫貨財運回金陵；

translations.literal: Fengxiang left Lichang holding Yangzhou city, drove women and plundered goods and wealth back to Jinling;
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang left Lichang to hold Yangzhou, drove women and loot back to Jinling;

sentences.zh: 率三十六軍北竄，分擾滁州，踞臨淮關，陷鳳陽府。

translations.literal: led thirty-six armies north in flight, separately harassed Chuzhou, held Linhuai Pass, and took Fengyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: and led thirty-six columns north in flight, raiding Chuzhou, seizing Linhuai Pass, and capturing Fengyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其酋朱錫錕、黃益芸等別率悍黨犯浦口，攻六合，知縣溫紹原率鄉團拒之，夜火其營，寇遁回金陵。

translations.literal: Their chiefs Zhu Xikun, Huang Yiyun, and others separately led fierce bands to attack Pukou and assault Luhe; Magistrate Wen Shaoyuan led militia to resist them, burned their camp by night, and the rebels fled back to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Their chiefs Zhu Xikun and Huang Yiyun led fierce bands against Pukou and Luhe; Magistrate Wen Shaoyuan rallied the militia, burned their camp by night, and the rebels fled back to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 五月，大兵圍揚州，殺敵逾萬。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the imperial army besieged Yangzhou and killed more than ten thousand enemies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the imperial army besieged Yangzhou and killed more than ten thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 勝保自揚州躡其後，力攻鳳陽，寇遁河南。

translations.literal: Senggebao from Yangzhou pursued close behind them, attacked Fengyang with force, and the rebels fled into Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Senggebao pursued from Yangzhou, stormed Fengyang, and the rebels fled into Henan.

sentences.zh: 楊秀清遣偽丞相吉文元由浦口竄亳州，偕林鳳祥陷永城，犯開封。

translations.literal: Yang Xiuqing sent the false Chancellor Ji Wenyuan from Pukou to flee toward Bozhou; with Lin Fengxiang he took Yongcheng and attacked Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiuqing sent the rebel Chancellor Ji Wenyuan from Pukou toward Bozhou; with Lin Fengxiang he seized Yongcheng and struck at Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 省官兵擊破之，又敗之汜水。

translations.literal: Provincial government troops defeated and broke them, and defeated them again at Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial troops routed them and defeated them again at Sishui.

sentences.zh: 寇奔黃河渡口，溺死無算。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to a Yellow River ford; drowned without count.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to a Yellow River crossing; countless drowned.

sentences.zh: 楊秀清遣偽豫王胡以晃陷安慶，又遣偽丞相賴漢英、石祥禎攻九江、湖口，進圍南昌。

translations.literal: Yang Xiuqing sent the false King of Yu Hu Yihuang to take Anqing, and also sent the false chancellors Lai Hanying and Shi Xiangzhen to attack Jiujiang and Hukou and advance to besiege Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiuqing sent the rebel King of Yu Hu Yihuang to seize Anqing and dispatched the rebel chancellors Lai Hanying and Shi Xiangzhen against Jiujiang and Hukou, then on to besiege Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 湖北按察使江忠源馳援江西，入城固守。

translations.literal: Hubei Surveillance Commissioner Jiang Zhongyuan rushed to aid Jiangxi, entered the city, and held it firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongyuan, surveillance commissioner of Hubei, rushed to Jiangxi, entered the city, and held it fast.

sentences.zh: 鳳祥等自汜水敗退，犯鄭州、滎陽。

translations.literal: Fengxiang and others, defeated and retreating from Sishui, attacked Zhengzhou and Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang and his commanders, beaten back from Sishui, struck at Zhengzhou and Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 六月，圍懷慶，以地道攻城，不克。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they besieged Huaiqing, used a tunnel to attack the city, and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they besieged Huaiqing and tried mining the walls, but could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 鎮江寇出城撲我軍，戰北固山下，伏寇縱火，七營皆被焚。

translations.literal: Zhenjiang rebels came out of the city to assault our army; they fought below Beigu Hill; ambush rebels set fire, and seven camps were all burned.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels at Zhenjiang sallied against our troops; below Beigu Hill ambushers set fires that consumed seven camps.

sentences.zh: 鄧紹良退守丹陽，都司劉廷鍈等督潮勇馳援。

translations.literal: Deng Shaoliang retreated to defend Danyang; Battalion Commander Liu Tingjun and others supervised Chaozhou braves rushing to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shaoliang fell back on Danyang while Battalion Commander Liu Tingjun led Chaozhou braves to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 寇退入城，復擾丹徒鎮，劉廷鍈復擊退之。

translations.literal: The rebels retreated into the city, again harassed Dantu town, and Liu Tingjun again struck and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew into the city, then raided Dantu; Liu Tingjun drove them off again.

sentences.zh: 向榮檄總兵和春與劉廷鍈紥徒陽運河之新豐鎮，寇始不敢南竄，常州獲安。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong ordered Commander He Chun and Liu Tingjun to camp at Xinfeng town on the Ziyang Canal; the rebels then dared not flee south, and Changzhou obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong ordered Commander He Chun and Liu Tingjun to encamp at Xinfeng on the Ziyang Canal; the rebels no longer dared flee south, and Changzhou was secured.

sentences.zh: 寇之圍懷慶也，立木柵為城，深溝高壘，我兵相持幾至六旬。

translations.literal: When the rebels besieged Huaiqing they erected wooden palisades as walls, with deep moats and high ramparts; our troops held them off for nearly sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: While besieging Huaiqing the rebels ringed themselves with wooden palisades, deep trenches, and high ramparts; our troops faced them for nearly sixty days.

sentences.zh: 訥爾經額親督諸將分五路攻壘，毀其木柵，斃敵酋吉文元。

translations.literal: Ne'erjing'e personally supervised the generals in five routes attacking the fortifications, destroyed their wooden palisades, and killed the enemy chieftain Ji Wenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ne'erjing'e personally led his generals in a five-pronged assault, smashed their palisades, and killed the rebel chief Ji Wenyuan.

sentences.zh: 鳳祥受重創，解圍而遁，河北肅清。

translations.literal: Fengxiang received grave wounds, raised the siege and fled, and Hebei was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang was gravely wounded, lifted the siege and fled, and Hebei was pacified.

sentences.zh: 八月，鳳祥竄山西，陷平陽，直抵洪洞；

translations.literal: In the eighth month Fengxiang fled into Shanxi, took Pingyang, and reached Hongdong directly;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Fengxiang fled into Shanxi, seized Pingyang, and pressed on to Hongdong;

sentences.zh: 竄直隸，踞臨洺關，擾至深州。

translations.literal: fled into Zhili, held Linming Pass, and harassed as far as Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: then fled into Zhili, seized Linming Pass, and raided as far as Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 賴漢英等解南昌圍，入湖北，踞田家鎮之半壁山。

translations.literal: Lai Hanying and others raised the siege of Nanchang, entered Hubei, and held Banbishan at Tianjia town.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Hanying and his commanders lifted the siege of Nanchang, entered Hubei, and seized Banbishan at Tianjia town.

sentences.zh: 九月，踞入楚要隘，水陸並進，陷黃州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month they occupied and entered Chu's vital passes, advanced by land and water together, and took Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they seized the vital passes of Chu, advanced by land and water, and took Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其竄深州者，旁擾欒城。

translations.literal: Those who had fled to Shenzhou on the side harassed Luancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The band that had fled to Shenzhou raided Luancheng on the flank.

sentences.zh: 十月，竄天津，踞靜海，屯獨流、楊柳青諸鎮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they fled to Tianjin, held Jinghai, and garrisoned Duliujiu, Yangliuqing, and other towns.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they fled to Tianjin, seized Jinghai, and garrisoned Duliujiu, Yangliuqing, and neighboring towns.

sentences.zh: 漢陽之寇，分股北竄：一陷孝感、黃陂諸縣，一由應城犯德安府，為防兵所遏，合眾退黃州。

translations.literal: Rebels at Hanyang split forces north in flight: one column took Xiaogan, Huangpi, and other counties; one by Yingcheng attacked De'an Prefecture, was stopped by defense troops, united their masses, and retreated to Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels at Hanyang split north: one column seized Xiaogan, Huangpi, and neighboring counties; another from Yingcheng struck De'an Prefecture, was blocked by defensive troops, reunited, and withdrew to Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秦日綱等陷安徽桐城、舒城，侍郎呂賢基死之。

translations.literal: Qin Rigang and others took Tongcheng and Shucheng in Anhui; Vice Minister Lü Xianji died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Rigang and his commanders seized Tongcheng and Shucheng in Anhui; Vice Minister Lü Xianji was killed.

sentences.zh: 舒城既失，賊遂徑撲廬州，陷之。

translations.literal: Once Shucheng was lost, the bandits then made straight for Luzhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shucheng fell, the rebels struck straight at Luzhou and seized it.

sentences.zh: 廬州者，安徽文武大吏之所僑寓以為省治者也。

translations.literal: Luzhou was where Anhui's civil and military grand officials had been stationed in exile to serve as the provincial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou was where Anhui's civil and military officials had made their temporary provincial seat.

sentences.zh: 十一月，秀全以揚州、鎮江攻圍急，遣賴漢英等領江西眾，糾合儀徵黨援揚州；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Xiuquan, because the attacks and sieges at Yangzhou and Zhenjiang were urgent, sent Lai Hanying and others leading Jiangxi forces, gathering Yizheng bandits to aid Yangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, with Yangzhou and Zhenjiang under heavy siege, Xiuquan sent Lai Hanying at the head of Jiangxi forces and rallied Yizheng rebels to relieve Yangzhou;

sentences.zh: 又令由安徽寧國灣沚進薄高淳湖，窺伺東壩，圖解鎮江之圍，我軍均擊退之。

translations.literal: he also ordered them through Ningguo and Wanzhi in Anhui to press close to Gaochun Lake, spy on Dongba, and scheme to relieve the siege of Zhenjiang; our army repulsed them all.
translations.idiomatic: he also ordered a column through Ningguo and Wanzhi in Anhui toward Gaochun Lake to watch Dongba and break the siege of Zhenjiang; our troops repulsed every thrust.

sentences.zh: 寇復由三汊河進撲，死戰不退。

translations.literal: The rebels again advanced from Sanhe River to assault; they fought to the death and would not retreat.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels again advanced from Sanhe River and fought to the death without yielding.

sentences.zh: 揚州寇曾立昌突出，與賴漢英同竄瓜洲。

translations.literal: The Yangzhou rebel Zeng Lichang broke out, and with Lai Hanying fled together to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Lichang broke out of Yangzhou and fled with Lai Hanying to Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 上以寇擾長江，非立水師不能制其死命，乃命在籍侍郎曾國藩練鄉勇、創水師討寇。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because rebels harassed the Yangtze and without establishing a navy one could not control their lives, ordered the retired Vice Minister Zeng Guofan to drill militia and create a navy to attack rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged that with rebels harrying the Yangtze only a navy could break their power, and ordered the retired Vice Minister Zeng Guofan to drill militia and build a river fleet to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 初，寇圍南昌，城外寇壘僅文孝廟數座，官軍屢攻不能克。

translations.literal: Initially, when rebels besieged Nanchang, outside the city rebel forts numbered only a few at Wenxiao Temple; government troops repeatedly attacked and could not take them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels first besieged Nanchang their outworks numbered only a few around Wenxiao Temple; imperial troops attacked again and again without success.

sentences.zh: 郭嵩燾偶獲諜訊之，則寇皆舟居，其壘則環三面築牆而虛其後，專蔽舟楫而已。

translations.literal: Guo Songtao accidentally obtained spy intelligence on this: the rebels all lived on boats; their forts ringed three sides with walls while leaving the rear open, solely to screen boats and oars.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Songtao chanced upon intelligence revealing that the rebels lived entirely on boats; their forts were walled on three sides with the rear left open—mere screens for their fleet.

sentences.zh: 嵩燾因與江忠源議曰：「東南州縣多阻水，江湖遇風，一日可數百里。

translations.literal: Songtao thus discussed with Jiang Zhongyuan, saying: "Southeast prefectures and counties are mostly blocked by water; on lakes and rivers, meeting wind, one day can cover several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Songtao said to Jiang Zhongyuan, "The southeast is a country of rivers and lakes; with a fair wind a fleet can run hundreds of li in a day.

sentences.zh: 官軍率由陸路躡寇，其勢常不及。

translations.literal: Government troops mostly pursue rebels by land routes; their momentum often cannot keep up.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops mostly pursue by land and rarely catch up.

sentences.zh: 長江數千里之險獨為敵有。

translations.literal: The Yangtze's defenses for thousands of li are held alone by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: For thousands of li along the Yangtze the enemy holds the river alone.

sentences.zh: 且寇上犯以舟楫，而官軍以營壘禦之，求與一戰而不可得，宜寇勢之日昌也。

translations.literal: Moreover rebels advance upstream by boats and oars, while government troops defend with camps and ramparts; seeking one battle yet unable to obtain it—fitting that rebel power grows daily.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels strike upstream by boat while we answer with earthworks; we can scarcely bring them to battle—no wonder their power grows day by day.

sentences.zh: 」忠源即具疏請飭湖南北、四川仿廣東拖罟船式，各造戰艦數千，飭廣東製備砲位以供戰艦之用，並交曾國藩督帶部署，奉旨允行。

translations.literal: " Zhongyuan immediately drew up a memorial requesting that Hunan-Hubei and Sichuan imitate Guangdong's tow-net boat pattern, each build several thousand warships, order Guangdong to prepare gun mounts for warship use, and hand deployment to Zeng Guofan to supervise and lead; the imperial edict assented.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan memorialized at once that Hunan, Hubei, and Sichuan should build thousands of warships on the Guangdong tow-net model, that Guangdong should furnish guns for them, and that Zeng Guofan should command the fleet; the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 國藩遂治戰船於衡湘，至是始成。

translations.literal: Guofan then built warships at Heng and Xiang; by now they were completed.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan had been building warships at Hengyang and Xiangtan; by now the fleet was ready.

sentences.zh: 共募水勇四千，分為十營；

translations.literal: In all he recruited four thousand water braves, divided into ten camps;
translations.idiomatic: He raised four thousand sailors in ten battalions;

sentences.zh: 募陸勇五千，亦分十營。

translations.literal: recruited five thousand land braves, also in ten camps.
translations.idiomatic: and five thousand foot soldiers in ten more.

sentences.zh: 以塔齊布為軍鋒。

translations.literal: He made Ta Qibu the army vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Ta Qibu led the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 國藩親統大軍發衡州，水陸夾江而下。

translations.literal: Guofan personally commanded the great army departing from Hengzhou, land and water flanking the river downward.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan marched from Hengzhou at the head of the host, land and river columns moving down the stream together.

sentences.zh: 初，鎮江、揚州、儀徵、瓜洲四處寇互相應援，不得破。

translations.literal: Initially rebels at Zhenjiang, Yangzhou, Yizheng, and Guazhou mutually supported one another and could not be broken.
translations.idiomatic: At first the rebels at Zhenjiang, Yangzhou, Yizheng, and Guazhou supported one another and could not be broken.

sentences.zh: 十二月，琦善以揚州寇退，瓜洲勢孤，督軍攻復儀徵，乘勝追抵瓜洲。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Qishan, because Yangzhou rebels had retreated and Guazhou's position was isolated, supervised the army to recover Yizheng and, pressing the victory, pursued to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, with the Yangzhou rebels withdrawn and Guazhou isolated, Qishan recovered Yizheng and pressed the pursuit to Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 楊秀清遣胡以晃率黨十餘萬攻廬州，巡撫江忠源晝夜抵禦，以眾寡不敵，城陷，死之。

translations.literal: Yang Xiuqing sent Hu Yihuang leading more than a hundred thousand bandits to attack Luzhou; Governor Jiang Zhongyuan resisted day and night; outnumbered, the city fell and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiuqing sent Hu Yihuang at the head of more than a hundred thousand rebels against Luzhou; Governor Jiang Zhongyuan resisted day and night, but outnumbered, the city fell and he perished.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，黃州寇張燈高會，總督吳文鎔出其不意襲之，會大雪罷戰。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year Huangzhou rebels hung lamps for a high feast; Governor Wu Weng attacked them unexpectedly; they met great snow and the battle ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year the rebels at Huangzhou feasted by lantern light; Governor Wu Weng struck by surprise, but heavy snow ended the fighting.

sentences.zh: 越數日，秀清分兵設伏山崗，命其黨率城軍撲營，文鎔拒戰，伏起火發，十三營皆潰，文鎔死之。

translations.literal: Several days later Xiuqing divided troops to set ambush on hill ridges, ordered his band to lead city troops to assault the camps; Weng resisted; ambush fires rose; thirteen camps were all routed; Weng died.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Xiuqing set ambushes on the hills and ordered his followers to lead the garrison in a camp assault; Wu Weng met them in battle, but fires broke out on every flank; thirteen camps were routed and Wu Weng was killed.

sentences.zh: 賊乘勝遂陷漢陽。

translations.literal: The bandits seized the victory and then took Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed their victory and seized Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 二月，揚州軍進剿瓜洲，總兵瞿騰龍陣亡。

translations.literal: In the second month the Yangzhou army advanced to suppress Guazhou; Commander Qu Tenglong was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Yangzhou force advanced on Guazhou; Commander Qu Tenglong fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 寇遣偽將孫寅山陷太平府，踞為巢。

translations.literal: The rebels sent the false general Sun Yinshan to take Taiping Prefecture and held it as a nest.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent the rebel general Sun Yinshan to seize Taiping Prefecture and made it their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 自瓜洲結壘屬於江，以達金陵，往來不絕。

translations.literal: From Guazhou they linked forts along the river to reach Jinling; traffic was unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: From Guazhou they strung forts along the river to Jinling, and traffic between them never ceased.

sentences.zh: 秀清復遣石祥禎會漢、黃寇黨溯江直上，陷岳州，溯流至銅官渚，逼近長沙。

translations.literal: Xiuqing again sent Shi Xiangzhen joining Han and Huang rebel bands up the river straight upward; they took Yuezhou, went upstream to Tongguan shoal, and pressed close to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuqing again sent Shi Xiangzhen with the Han and Huang rebel columns upriver; they seized Yuezhou, pushed upstream to Tongguan shoal, and threatened Changsha.

sentences.zh: 曾國藩邀之靖港，而寇已由間道襲湘潭，副將塔齊布率兵千三百同水師血戰五晝夜，斃寇數萬。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan intercepted them at Jinggang, but rebels had already by a bypath attacked Xiangtan; Deputy Commander Ta Qibu led thirteen hundred troops together with the navy in bloody battle for five days and nights, killing tens of thousands of rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan met them at Jinggang, but the rebels had already struck Xiangtan by a hidden route; Deputy Commander Ta Qibu with thirteen hundred men and the fleet fought five days and nights of bloody combat and killed tens of thousands of rebels.

sentences.zh: 論者謂微此戰，寇溯湘源以達粵，直下金陵，首尾一江相貫注，大局不可支矣。

translations.literal: Commentators said that without this battle, rebels would have traced the Xiang to its source to reach Guangdong, then straight down to Jinling; head and tail one river connecting through, and the great situation could not have been sustained.
translations.idiomatic: Later writers said that but for this battle the rebels might have traced the Xiang to its headwaters in Guangdong and then swept down to Jinling, the whole river one continuous rebel highway—and the empire could not have held.

sentences.zh: 是月，參贊大臣僧格林沁攻克獨流寇巢，靜海寇復竄踞阜城。

translations.literal: That month Consultant Minister Senggelinqin captured the rebel nest at Duliujiu; Jinghai rebels again fled to hold Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: That month Consultant Minister Senggelinqin took the rebel nest at Duliujiu; the Jinghai rebels fled again and seized Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁攻毀堆村、連村、林家場三處寇壘，擒殺偽指揮、監軍以下一百餘人，悉遁入城。

translations.literal: Senggelinqin attacked and destroyed rebel fortifications at Duicun, Liancun, and Linjiachang, captured and killed more than a hundred false commanders, military supervisors, and those below, and all fled into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Senggelinqin stormed the rebel works at Duicun, Liancun, and Linjiachang, killed or captured more than a hundred rebel commanders and staff officers, and the survivors fled into the city.

sentences.zh: 秀全念河北不能支，遣皖黨由豐豆工偷渡黃河，竄山東金鄉，進撲臨清州，冀抒阜城之困。

translations.literal: Xiuquan, thinking Hebei could not hold, sent Anhui bandits from the Fengdou crossing to steal across the Yellow River, fled to Jinxian in Shandong, advanced to assault Linqing Prefecture, hoping to relieve Fucheng's distress.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Hebei failing, Xiuquan sent Anhui rebels across the Yellow River at the Fengdou crossing into Shandong at Jinxian, then struck at Linqing Prefecture to relieve the siege of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 三月，寇以地雷陷城，尋為我軍攻復，竄冠縣、鄆城，復據曹縣，築木城拒守。

translations.literal: In the third month rebels used land mines to take the city; soon our army attacked and recovered it; they fled to Guan county and Yuncheng, again held Cao county, and built a wooden city to resist and hold.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the rebels mined a city wall and took it, but our troops soon recaptured it; they fled through Guan county and Yuncheng, reoccupied Cao county, and threw up wooden walls to hold out.

sentences.zh: 四月，勝保破其巢，追至漫口支河，逼溺水，偽丞相曾立昌、許宗揚皆溺死。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Senggebao broke their nest, pursued to the Mankou branch river, forced them to drown; the false chancellors Zeng Lichang and Xu Zongyang both drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Senggebao destroyed their stronghold and pursued them to the Mankou branch channel, driving them into the water; the rebel chancellors Zeng Lichang and Xu Zongyang drowned.

sentences.zh: 偽副丞相陳世保已先於冠縣燒斃，悉數殲除。

translations.literal: The false Vice Chancellor Chen Shibao had already earlier been burned to death at Guan county; all were entirely exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Vice Chancellor Chen Shibao had already been burned to death at Guan county; the force was wiped out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 踞阜城者即於是日全股南竄入連鎮。

translations.literal: Those holding Fucheng on that very day fled south in their entire force into Lian town.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels holding Fucheng fled south that same day in a body to Lian town.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁及勝保會軍合剿破之，誅林鳳祥；

translations.literal: Senggelinqin and Senggebao united armies in combined suppression, broke them, and executed Lin Fengxiang;
translations.idiomatic: Senggelinqin and Senggebao joined forces, broke the rebels, and executed Lin Fengxiang;

sentences.zh: 復破之高唐州馮官屯，生擒李開芳，磔之京市。

translations.literal: again defeated them at Fengguantun in Gaotang Prefecture, captured Li Kaifang alive, and dismembered him in the capital marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: then defeated them again at Fengguantun in Gaotang Prefecture, took Li Kaifang alive, and had him dismembered in the capital.

sentences.zh: 河北肅清，是後不復北犯，我軍遂無後顧憂。

translations.literal: Hebei was cleared; thereafter they no longer invaded north, and our army then had no rear concern.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei was pacified; the rebels never marched north again, and our armies fought without fear for the rear.

sentences.zh: 初，長江為寇往來道，荊州當四路之衝，至省道梗，特召荊州將軍官文統軍討寇。

translations.literal: Initially the Yangtze was the rebels' thoroughfare; Jingzhou lay at the crossing of four routes; until provincial routes were blocked, the Jingzhou General Guanwen was specially summoned to command the army to suppress rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze had become the rebels' highway; Jingzhou stood at the crossing of four routes; when the provincial roads were cut, the Jingzhou general Guanwen was summoned to command the suppression.

sentences.zh: 時沔陽、安陸、荊門、監利、京山、天門均陷，進窺荊州。

translations.literal: At the time Mianyang, Anlu, Jingmen, Jianli, Jingshan, and Tianmen had all fallen; they advanced to spy on Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mianyang, Anlu, Jingmen, Jianli, Jingshan, and Tianmen had all fallen, and the rebels pressed toward Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 雲南普洱營游擊王國才奉調至，一戰敗之，重鎮始安。

translations.literal: Wang Guocai, patrol officer of Yunnan's Pu'er Camp, received orders and arrived; in one battle he defeated them, and the important town began to be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guocai, patrol officer of Yunnan's Pu'er battalion, arrived on orders and routed them in a single battle; the great town was saved.

sentences.zh: 並克復監利、宜昌，寇遁洞庭湖，合股犯常德府。

translations.literal: He also recovered Jianli and Yichang; rebels fled to Dongting Lake and united forces to attack Changde Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He also recovered Jianli and Yichang; the rebels fled onto Dongting Lake and united to strike Changde Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先是李侍賢常與陳玉成、李秀成謀解金陵圍，犯江西、福建。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Shixian had often with Chen Yucheng and Li Xiucheng schemed to relieve the siege of Jinling and invaded Jiangxi and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Shixian had often joined Chen Yucheng and Li Xiucheng in plans to raise the siege of Jinling by striking into Jiangxi and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 偽啟王梁成先犯陝西，後與捻合，欲犯湖南、河南，而陳玉成志在武昌、漢陽，乃領一隊入梁子湖達武昌，渡江分犯，以全力圖武昌，六月，陷之，並踞漢陽。

translations.literal: The false Prince Qi Liang Chengxian first attacked Shaanxi, later joined the Nian, and wished to invade Hunan and Henan; but Chen Yucheng aimed at Wuchang and Hanyang, led one column into Liangzi Lake to reach Wuchang, crossed the river in divided attacks, and with full force aimed at Wuchang; in the sixth month he took it and also held Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Prince Qi Liang Chengxian struck Shaanxi first, later joined the Nian rebels, and meant to invade Hunan and Henan; but Chen Yucheng set his heart on Wuchang and Hanyang, led a column through Liangzi Lake to Wuchang, crossed the river in separate thrusts, and threw his full strength at Wuchang; in the sixth month he took it and seized Hanyang as well.

sentences.zh: 巡撫青麟自縊不死，棄城走，尋正法。

translations.literal: Governor Qing Lin hanged himself but did not die, abandoned the city and fled, and was soon executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Qing Lin tried to hang himself but failed, fled the city, and was soon executed.

sentences.zh: 秀全以秦日綱留守武昌，授玉成偽殿右十八指揮；

translations.literal: Xiuquan left Qin Rigang to garrison Wuchang and granted Yucheng the false Palace Right Eighteen Command.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuquan left Qin Rigang to garrison Wuchang and made Yucheng rebel Commander of the Palace Right, Eighteenth Rank;

sentences.zh: 還陷田家鎮，破廣濟、黃梅，連陷九江，升偽殿右三十檢點。

translations.literal: He returned to take Tianjia town, broke Guangji and Huangmei, successively took Jiujiang, and was promoted to false Palace Right Thirty Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: he returned to seize Tianjia town, stormed Guangji and Huangmei, took Jiujiang in succession, and was promoted to rebel Inspector of the Palace Right, Thirtieth Rank.

sentences.zh: 楊秀清雖在軍，而金陵之事一決於己，驛騎絡繹，多稽時日。

translations.literal: Although Yang Xiuqing was at the army, yet affairs of Jinling were all decided by himself; courier horses came in continuous streams, and much time was delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yang Xiuqing was in the field, every decision at Jinling rested with him; dispatches poured in and out, and campaigns lost days to the relay.

sentences.zh: 向榮軍孝陵衞，稱江南勁旅，秀清憂之，既克武昌，遂馳還金陵，命石達開代守武漢。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong encamped at Xiaolingwei, called the Jiangnan elite force; Xiuqing worried over this; having taken Wuchang, he then galloped back to Jinling and ordered Shi Dakai to replace him in guarding Wuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong's camp at Xiaolingwei was reckoned the finest army in the south; Xiuqing feared it; after Wuchang fell he raced back to Jinling and left Shi Dakai to hold Wuhan.

sentences.zh: 官文自荊州下剿，克沔陽。

translations.literal: Guanwen from Jingzhou descended in suppression and took Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guanwen marched down from Jingzhou and recovered Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 初，寇欲先取長沙，踞上游為破竹之勢，而韋志俊略湘潭不得志，退踞岳州，築壘毀橋，意圖久抗。

translations.literal: Initially rebels wished first to take Changsha, hold the upper reaches for a bamboo-splitting momentum; but Wei Zhijun raided Xiangtan without success, retreated to hold Yuezhou, built forts and destroyed bridges, intending long resistance.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had meant to seize Changsha first and hold the upper river for a rolling conquest; but Wei Zhijun failed at Xiangtan, fell back on Yuezhou, fortified the place, and broke the bridges for a long defense.

sentences.zh: 我軍水師設伏誘敗之，七月，復岳州。

translations.literal: Our navy set ambush and lured them to defeat; in the seventh month Yuezhou was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Our fleet ambushed and routed them; in the seventh month Yuezhou was recovered.

sentences.zh: 寇由城陵磯來犯，我軍分五路迎擊，斃偽丞相汪得勝等二人，獲船七十六，殲賊千餘人。

translations.literal: Rebels came attacking from Chenglingji; our army met them in five routes; killed the false chancellors Wang Desheng and one other; obtained seventy-six boats; destroyed more than a thousand bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels attacked from Chenglingji; our forces met them on five fronts, killed the rebel chancellors Wang Desheng and another, captured seventy-six boats, and destroyed more than a thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 塔齊布陣斬悍酋偽丞相曾天養。

translations.literal: Ta Qibu in formation beheaded the fierce chieftain, the false Chancellor Zeng Tianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ta Qibu cut down the fierce rebel chancellor Zeng Tianyang in the line of battle.

sentences.zh: 閏七月，寇奔城陵磯，塔齊布策馬率湘勇直入，毀營十三，斃二千人。

translations.literal: In the intercalary seventh month rebels fled to Chenglingji; Ta Qibu spurred his horse and led Xiang braves straight in, destroyed thirteen camps, and killed two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary seventh month the rebels fled to Chenglingji; Ta Qibu spurred his horse, led the Hunan braves straight in, destroyed thirteen camps, and killed two thousand.

sentences.zh: 陸軍既勝，曾國藩飭李孟羣率水師追剿，荊河東、西兩岸寇壘悉夷。

translations.literal: The land army having won, Zeng Guofan ordered Li Mengqun to lead the navy in pursuit and suppression; rebel fortifications on both east and west banks of the Jing River were all leveled.
translations.idiomatic: With the land victory won, Zeng Guofan ordered Li Mengqun to pursue with the fleet; rebel works on both banks of the Jing River were leveled.

sentences.zh: 自此由荊入川，由岳州入湘，門戶始固。

translations.literal: From this the gates from Jing into Chuan and from Yuezhou into Xiang began to be secure.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the gateways from Jingzhou into Sichuan and from Yuezhou into Hunan were secure.

sentences.zh: 初，武昌失陷，上以楊霈代總督，台勇克京山、安陸，復天門，生擒孔昭文等正法。

translations.literal: Early on, when Wuchang fell, the Emperor replaced the governor-general with Yang Pei; Tai Yong's brigades took Jingshan and Anlu, recovered Tianmen, and captured alive Kong Zhaowen and others, who were put to death according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Wuchang fell, the emperor replaced the governor-general with Yang Pei. Tai Yong's forces captured Jingshan and Anlu, retook Tianmen, and took Kong Zhaowen and others alive; they were then executed.

sentences.zh: 餘皆下竄，踞沔陽州仙桃鎮。

translations.literal: The remainder all fled downward and seized Xiantao Town in Mianyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The rest fled south and occupied Xiantao in Mianyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是月破其巢，並收復下游孝感、黃州、麻城諸縣。

translations.literal: That month they destroyed their nest and also recovered downstream the counties Xiaogan, Huangzhou, Macheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: That month government forces destroyed the rebel stronghold and also retook downstream counties including Xiaogan, Huangzhou, and Macheng.

sentences.zh: 寇悉竄黃州。

translations.literal: The rebels all fled to Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels all fled toward Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時金陵寇分股嘯聚於太平府，與鎮江遙為應援。

translations.literal: At that time rebel bands from Jinling gathered in separate groups at Taiping Prefecture, giving distant mutual support with Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile rebel detachments from Nanjing had gathered at Taiping Prefecture, coordinating from afar with their comrades at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 向榮分兵四隊擊之，斃其偽國宗韋得玲、偽檢點陳贄見、偽將軍李長有、偽總制吳春和，遂復府城。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong divided his forces into four columns to attack them, killing the rebel state clansman Wei Deling, rebel inspector Chen Zanjian, rebel general Li Changyou, and rebel chief controller Wu Chunhe, then recovered the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong attacked in four columns, killing the rebel leaders Wei Deling, Chen Zanjian, Li Changyou, and Wu Chunhe, and retook the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 楊秀清自率戰，圍軍不利，三路皆潰；

translations.literal: Yang Xiuqing personally led the battle; the besieging army fared ill and all three routes were routed;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiuqing led the fight himself, but the siege went badly and all three columns were routed;

sentences.zh: 退入城，謂韋昌輝等曰：「江南大營不走，吾輩無安枕日矣！

translations.literal: He retreated into the city and said to Wei Changhui and others: "If the Jiangnan Grand Camp does not withdraw, we shall have no day to sleep in peace!"
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew into the city and told Wei Changhui and the others, "As long as the Jiangnan Grand Camp stays put, we will never sleep easy again!

sentences.zh: 現其勢方銳，不可敵也。

translations.literal: Now their momentum is just sharp; they cannot be opposed.
translations.idiomatic: Their momentum is too strong to fight head-on.

sentences.zh: 當乘其罷徐圖之。

translations.literal: We ought to take advantage when they are weary and plan gradually.
translations.idiomatic: We must wait until they tire, then strike by degrees.

sentences.zh: 」金陵寇以乏糧，驅婦女之老而無色者出城，聽其自散。

translations.literal: " The Jinling rebels, for lack of grain, drove out of the city women who were old and without beauty, allowing them to scatter on their own.
translations.idiomatic: " The Nanjing rebels, short of food, expelled elderly women they deemed unattractive from the city and let them go where they would.

sentences.zh: 盡取年十五以上、五十以下之婦女，指配給眾，不從則殺之，守志者多自盡，死者萬計。

translations.literal: They took all women from fifteen years up and under fifty, assigning them to the masses; those who did not obey were killed, and many who kept their virtue killed themselves—the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: They seized every woman between fifteen and fifty and assigned them to the ranks; those who refused were killed, and many who would not yield took their own lives—tens of thousands died.

sentences.zh: 八月，總督楊霈收復黃州府屬蘄水、廣濟、羅田諸縣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Governor-General Yang Pei recovered under Huangzhou Prefecture the counties Qishui, Guangji, Luotian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Governor-General Yang Pei retook Qishui, Guangji, Luotian, and other counties in Huangzhou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾國藩自克岳州後，議乘勝東下，先與塔齊布會攻崇陽，克之，生擒偽丞相金之亨等十一人。

translations.literal: After Zeng Guofan took Yuezhou, he proposed to press the advantage eastward; first he joined Ta Qibu to attack Chongyang together, took it, and captured alive the rebel chancellor Jin Zhiheng and eleven others.
translations.idiomatic: After Zeng Guofan captured Yuezhou, he planned to drive east while momentum held. He and Ta Qibu jointly attacked Chongyang, took the city, and captured eleven rebels alive, including the false chancellor Jin Zhiheng.

sentences.zh: 惟廖二逃竄，復句結餘黨，重失縣城。

translations.literal: Only Liao Er escaped and fled, again colluded with remnant bands, and the county seat was lost anew.
translations.idiomatic: But Liao Er escaped, rallied the remaining rebels, and the county seat was lost again.

sentences.zh: 國藩親督水陸諸軍攻武昌、漢陽。

translations.literal: Guofan personally supervised the land and naval forces in attacking Wuchang and Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan personally directed the combined land and naval forces against Wuchang and Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 寇守城之法，不守陴而守險，洪山、花園兩路皆精銳所在。

translations.literal: The rebels' method of defending cities was not to hold the parapets but to hold the passes; on the Hongshan and Huayuan routes were all their elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels defended not the walls but the high ground; their best troops held the Hongshan and Huayuan approaches.

sentences.zh: 大軍自螺山下剿，楊載福等率水師，羅澤南率陸師，三路同進，連克寇壘，焚毀敵船數千。

translations.literal: The great army suppressed from below Luoshan; Yang Zaifu and others led the naval force, Luo Zenan led the land force, and three routes advanced together, taking rebel fortifications in succession and burning thousands of enemy vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The main force attacked from Luoshan. Yang Zaifu commanded the fleet, Luo Zenan the infantry; all three columns advanced together, storming rebel strongpoints in succession and burning thousands of enemy boats.

sentences.zh: 李孟羣、塔齊布進薄武昌，寇宵遁。

translations.literal: Li Mengqun and Ta Qibu pressed close to Wuchang, and the rebels fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mengqun and Ta Qibu pressed up to Wuchang, and the rebels fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 楊昌泗亦攻漢陽，克之。

translations.literal: Yang Changsi also attacked Hanyang and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Changsi attacked Hanyang as well and captured it.

sentences.zh: 黃州府城、武昌縣均收復。

translations.literal: Huangzhou prefectural city and Wuchang county were both recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Both Huangzhou city and Wuchang county were retaken.

sentences.zh: 九月，提督和春敗寇廬江，擒偽監軍任大綱等十七名。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Commander-in-Chief He Chun defeated the rebels at Lujiang and captured the rebel military overseer Ren Dagang and seventeen others.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Commander-in-Chief He Chun routed the rebels at Lujiang and took seventeen prisoners, including the false military overseer Ren Dagang.

sentences.zh: 下游知官軍分路進剿，乃由田家鎮糾黨六千餘，一由興國分抄大冶以拒武昌軍，一踞興國以拒金牛軍。

translations.literal: Learning downstream that government troops were advancing on separate routes to suppress them, they rallied over six thousand followers at Tianjia Town—one column from Xingguo to raid Daye by a detour and block the Wuchang army, one holding Xingguo to block the Jinniu army.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that imperial forces were advancing on several fronts, downstream rebels mustered more than six thousand men at Tianjia Town: one column from Xingguo would strike Daye and block the Wuchang army, while another held Xingguo against the Jinniu force.

sentences.zh: 羅澤南馳至興國，敗之，克州城。

translations.literal: Luo Zenan rushed to Xingguo, defeated them, and took the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zenan hurried to Xingguo, routed them, and captured the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 塔齊布赴大冶，擊斃千餘。

translations.literal: Ta Qibu went to Daye and killed over a thousand in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Ta Qibu marched to Daye and killed more than a thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 彭玉麟、楊載福抵蘄州，燒寇船九十餘艘。

translations.literal: Peng Yulin and Yang Zaifu reached Qizhou and burned over ninety rebel vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yulin and Yang Zaifu reached Qizhou and burned more than ninety rebel boats.

sentences.zh: 十月，楚軍攻半壁山，寇置橫江鐵鎖四道，攔以木牌，遍列槍砲。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the Chu army attacked Banbishan; the rebels set four iron chains across the river, blocked with wooden palisades, and lined them throughout with muskets and cannon.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Chu army assaulted Banbishan. The rebels stretched four iron chains across the river, backed them with wooden barriers, and lined the works with guns.

sentences.zh: 楊載福等率水師至田家鎮，會陸師進攻，乘風縱火，破其壘，燔舟一萬有奇。

translations.literal: Yang Zaifu and others led the naval force to Tianjia Town, joined the land army in the attack, exploited the wind to set fires, broke their fortifications, and burned over ten thousand vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaifu led the fleet to Tianjia Town, joined the land forces in the assault, and used the wind to set fires that broke the rebel works and destroyed more than ten thousand boats.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成棄蘄州竄陷廣濟，聯合秦日綱、羅大綱等分扼要隘。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng abandoned Qizhou, fled, and seized Guangji, joining Qin Rigang, Luo Dagang, and others to hold key passes in separate groups.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng abandoned Qizhou, fled into Guangji, and joined Qin Rigang, Luo Dagang, and others in holding the strategic passes.

sentences.zh: 塔齊布渡江追之，收復廣濟。

translations.literal: Ta Qibu crossed the river in pursuit and recovered Guangji.
translations.idiomatic: Ta Qibu crossed the river in pursuit and retook Guangji.

sentences.zh: 寇退踞黃梅，黃梅為湖北、江西、安徽三省總匯之區。

translations.literal: The rebels fell back and held Huangmei; Huangmei was the converging zone of the three provinces Hubei, Jiangxi, and Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew to Huangmei, a junction where Hubei, Jiangxi, and Anhui met.

sentences.zh: 寇死拒，以萬餘守小池口抗水師，以數萬拒大河埔，以萬餘紥北城外，又以數千游弋聯絡之。

translations.literal: The rebels resisted to the death: with over ten thousand they held Xiaochikou against the naval force, with tens of thousands they blocked Dahepu, with over ten thousand they encamped outside the north wall, and with several thousand more they skirmished to link them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fought to the last: more than ten thousand held Xiaochikou against the fleet, tens of thousands blocked Dahepu, over ten thousand camped north of the walls, and several thousand more skirmished to keep the positions linked.

sentences.zh: 塔齊布與羅澤南登山下擊兜殺，陳玉成縋城而逸，遂克黃梅。

translations.literal: Ta Qibu and Luo Zenan descended the mountain to strike and slaughter in encirclement; Chen Yucheng lowered himself by rope from the wall and escaped, and Huangmei was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: Ta Qibu and Luo Zenan attacked from the heights and slaughtered the encircled rebels. Chen Yucheng lowered himself from the wall by rope and escaped, and Huangmei fell.

sentences.zh: 玉成自請罪，而秀成反加偽勳號曰成天裕。

translations.literal: Yucheng asked to be punished, but Xiucheng instead gave him the false title of merit, Chengtianyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng asked to be punished, but Xiucheng instead bestowed on him the false title Chengtianyu.

sentences.zh: 時捻匪蠭起，粵寇與之聯合，或令分擾，或令前驅，以牽制我軍。

translations.literal: At that time Nian bandits swarmed up; the Guangdong rebels joined with them, sometimes ordering them to harass in diversion, sometimes to march ahead as vanguard, to tie down our armies.
translations.idiomatic: Nian bandits were rising everywhere, and the Taiping rebels allied with them—sometimes sending them to raid on the flanks, sometimes to march ahead—to pin down imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 秀成由廬州踞舒城，並扼桐城大、小二關，阻我南路之師。

translations.literal: Xiucheng moved from Luzhou to hold Shucheng and also seized the great and small passes of Tongcheng, blocking our southern-route army.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng advanced from Luzhou to hold Shucheng and seized the great and small passes at Tongcheng, blocking the southern imperial column.

sentences.zh: 二關為安慶通衢，屢復屢失。

translations.literal: The two passes were the main thoroughfare to Anqing; they were recovered and lost repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: The two passes were the main road to Anqing and changed hands again and again.

sentences.zh: 京堂袁甲三檄參將劉玉豹、舉人臧紆青等戰奪兩關，斬其目吳鳳珠等十二名，進抵桐城。

translations.literal: Inspector Yuan Jiasan issued orders to Regiment Commander Liu Yubao, Licentiate Zang Shuqing, and others to fight and seize both passes, beheading twelve including their officer Wu Fengzhu, and advanced to Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Yuan Jiasan ordered Regiment Commander Liu Yubao, Licentiate Zang Shuqing, and others into battle; they retook both passes, beheaded twelve rebels including the officer Wu Fengzhu, and advanced on Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 廬江寇糾安慶黨來援，我軍兜戮殆盡，而潛山援寇復至，臧紆青歿於陣。

translations.literal: The Lujiang rebels called Anqing bands to come to their aid; our army slaughtered nearly all of them in encirclement, but when Qianshan relief rebels arrived again, Zang Shuqing died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Lujiang rebels summoned reinforcements from Anqing; imperial troops nearly annihilated them in the encirclement, but when relief forces from Qianshan arrived, Zang Shuqing was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 十一月，國藩進軍九江。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Guofan advanced his army on Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Guofan marched on Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 玉成自黃梅敗後，復糾安慶新到之眾踞孔壠驛、小池口，與對岸九江相句連。

translations.literal: After Yucheng's defeat at Huangmei, he again rallied the newly arrived masses from Anqing to hold Konglu Post and Xiaochikou, linked with Jiujiang on the opposite bank.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat at Huangmei, Yucheng rallied fresh troops from Anqing at Konglu Post and Xiaochikou, linking his position with Jiujiang across the river.

sentences.zh: 李孟羣七戰七捷。

translations.literal: Li Mengqun fought seven battles and won seven victories.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mengqun fought seven engagements and won every one.

sentences.zh: 塔齊布與羅澤南等由北岸進至濯港，進攻孔壠驛，破土城，縱火焚街市，寇無得脫者。

translations.literal: Ta Qibu and Luo Zenan and others advanced from the north bank to Zhuogang, attacked Konglu Post, breached the earthen wall, set fires and burned the market streets, and no rebel could escape.
translations.idiomatic: Ta Qibu and Luo Zenan advanced along the north bank to Zhuogang and assaulted Konglu Post. They breached the earthen walls, burned the streets, and left no rebel alive.

sentences.zh: 小池口寇聞之，亦遁。

translations.literal: The Xiaochikou rebels, hearing this, also fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the rebels at Xiaochikou fled as well.

sentences.zh: 乃調陸軍攻九江，水師乘勝攻湖口，大綱趨救，大戰梅家洲，燬小河簰船、沙洲橋壘。

translations.literal: They then shifted the land army to attack Jiujiang while the naval force pressed its advantage to attack Hukou; Dagang rushed to the rescue, and a great battle was fought at Meijiazhou, destroying small river rafts and sandbar bridge fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: The land army was then turned on Jiujiang while the fleet pressed the attack at Hukou. Dagang rushed to the rescue; at Meijiazhou a fierce battle destroyed the rebel river rafts and sandbar fortifications.

sentences.zh: 十二月，蕭捷三率水師馳入鄱陽湖內，追至大姑塘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xiao Jiesan led the naval force in a dash into Poyang Lake in pursuit as far as Dagutang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Xiao Jiesan led the fleet into Poyang Lake in pursuit as far as Dagutang.

sentences.zh: 石達開聯船為卡斷其後，捷三不能返，遂與外江水師隔絕。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai linked ships into a barrier to cut off their rear; Jiesan could not return and was thus separated from the outer-river naval force.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai chained his boats into a barrier across their rear. Jiesan could not get back and was cut off from the fleet on the main river.

sentences.zh: 達開潛以小舟馳襲國藩坐船，國藩跳入羅澤南營以免。

translations.literal: Dakai secretly sent small boats in a swift raid on Guofan's command vessel; Guofan jumped into Luo Zenan's camp to escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai secretly sent light boats to attack Guofan's flagship. Guofan leaped into Luo Zenan's camp and escaped.

sentences.zh: 大軍之攻九江也，敗寇收合潰散，分三道東陷黃梅。

translations.literal: As the great army attacked Jiujiang, defeated rebels gathered scattered forces and in three columns marched east to seize Huangmei.
translations.idiomatic: While the main force besieged Jiujiang, defeated rebels regrouped and in three columns marched east to retake Huangmei.

sentences.zh: 值歲除，潛至廣濟，火楊霈大營，霈突圍出，不敢入武昌，走保德安。

translations.literal: On New Year's Eve they secretly reached Guangji, set fire to Yang Pei's grand camp; Pei broke out of the encirclement but dared not enter Wuchang and fled to secure De'an.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve they slipped into Guangji and burned Yang Pei's headquarters. Pei broke out of the encirclement but dared not re-enter Wuchang and fled to De'an.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，江蘇巡撫吉爾杭阿克上海縣，縣自三年秋陷於賊，至是始復。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Jiangsu Governor Ji'erhang'e recovered Shanghai County; the county had fallen to bandits since autumn of the third year, and only now was it recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, Jiangsu Governor Ji'erhang'e retook Shanghai County, which had been in rebel hands since the autumn of the third year.

sentences.zh: 秀全令皖寇大舉犯湖北，中道自小池口沿江陷黃、蘄；

translations.literal: Xiucheng ordered Anhui rebels to invade Hubei in great force; midway from Xiaochikou along the river they seized Huang and Qi;
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng ordered a major rebel thrust into Hubei from Anhui; marching from Xiaochikou down the Yangtze, they seized Huangzhou and Qizhou;

sentences.zh: 復分黨從富池渡江西，陷興國、通城、崇陽、咸寧、通山，且掠江西武寧，所至脅眾以行。

translations.literal: They again split parties crossing west from Fuchi Ford, seizing Xingguo, Tongcheng, Chongyang, Xianning, Tongshan, and also raiding Wuning in Jiangxi; wherever they went they compelled the masses to march with them.
translations.idiomatic: other columns crossed the river at Fuchi and swept west through Xingguo, Tongcheng, Chongyang, Xianning, and Tongshan, raiding as far as Wuning in Jiangxi and pressing civilians to march with them wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 湖北巡撫陶恩培甫蒞任數日，時總督在外，未及議守備。

translations.literal: Hubei Governor Tao Enpei had only just taken office for a few days; the governor-general was away at the time, and there was no time yet to discuss defense preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei Governor Tao Enpei had been in office only a few days; the governor-general was away, and there was no time to organize a defense.

sentences.zh: 城中兵僅二千，徵兵半途聞警皆潰去。

translations.literal: Troops in the city numbered only two thousand; conscripted soldiers halfway heard the alarm and all dispersed in rout.
translations.idiomatic: The city held barely two thousand troops; conscripts summoned on the road heard the alarm and scattered.

sentences.zh: 湖北、江西方千里，旬日騷然矣。

translations.literal: For a thousand li across Hubei and Jiangxi, within ten days all was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days a thousand li of Hubei and Jiangxi were in uproar.

sentences.zh: 始寇之起，所行無留難。

translations.literal: When the rebels first rose, wherever they marched they met no obstacle or delay.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels first rose, they met almost no resistance on the march.

sentences.zh: 其踞省府，脅取民財米。

translations.literal: When they occupied provincial seats, they extorted the people's wealth and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Once they held a provincial capital, they extorted grain and money from the people.

sentences.zh: 行道掠人夫，不用則遣還，未嘗增眾。

translations.literal: On the road they seized laborers; those not needed they sent back—they never increased their numbers.
translations.idiomatic: On the march they seized porters but released those they did not need, and rarely swelled their ranks.

sentences.zh: 及屢敗，乃結土寇屯城鎮，頗收拔悍鷙者，而任用石達開、陳玉成等，極稱得人之盛。

translations.literal: After repeated defeats, they then joined with local bandits to hold towns and cities, recruited many fierce and ruthless men, and employed Shi Dakai, Chen Yucheng, and others, greatly boasting that they had found outstanding men.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated defeats they allied with local bandits, garrisoned towns, recruited the fiercest fighters, and put Shi Dakai, Chen Yucheng, and others in command—boasting that they had found the right men at last.

sentences.zh: 自漢口進襄河，上犯漢川，擾沔陽，進犯武昌，踞漢陽府城。

translations.literal: From Hankou they advanced on the Xiang River, marched up to invade Hanchuan, harassed Mianyang, pressed on to invade Wuchang, and occupied Hanyang prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: From Hankou they advanced up the Han, raided Hanchuan, harassed Mianyang, pressed on Wuchang, and occupied Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 沿江築壘，並於漢陽下南岸嘴高築砲臺，以阻下游之師。

translations.literal: Along the river they built fortifications, and below Hanyang at Zuianzui they built high batteries to block armies coming from downstream.
translations.idiomatic: They fortified the riverbank and built high batteries at Zuianzui south of Hanyang to block imperial forces coming upriver.

sentences.zh: 時江西寇入腹地陷饒州。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangxi rebels penetrated the interior and seized Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Jiangxi rebels penetrated the interior and took Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 國藩親至南昌，修整內湖水師，與羅澤南陸軍相依。

translations.literal: Guofan went personally to Nanchang, rebuilt the inner-lake naval force, and relied on Luo Zenan's land army.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan went to Nanchang in person, rebuilt the lake fleet, and coordinated with Luo Zenan's infantry.

sentences.zh: 二月，韋國宗等攻陷武昌，巡撫陶恩培等死之。

translations.literal: In the second month, Wei Guozong and others attacked and seized Wuchang; Governor Tao Enpei and others died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Wei Guozong and others captured Wuchang; Governor Tao Enpei and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 寇溯漢江而上，以岳家口、仙桃鎮為老巢。

translations.literal: The rebels advanced up the Han River, taking Yuejiakou and Xiantao Town as their old nests.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pushed up the Han, making Yuejiakou and Xiantao their strongholds.

sentences.zh: 上以胡林翼巡撫湖北，國藩進吳城鎮，屢書與議東南大勢，以武昌據金陵上游，宜厚集兵力為恢復計。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Hu Linyi governor of Hubei; Guofan advanced to Wucheng Town and repeatedly wrote to discuss the great southeast situation, holding that Wuchang commanded upstream of Jinling and that heavy forces ought to be massed to plan recovery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Hu Linyi governor of Hubei. Guofan advanced to Wucheng and wrote repeatedly on the strategic situation in the southeast: Wuchang lay upstream of Nanjing, he argued, and a major force should be assembled to retake it.

sentences.zh: 四月，陷德安府，楊霈退走襄陽，上褫其職，以官文為湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, De'an Prefecture fell; Yang Pei retreated to Xiangyang; the Emperor stripped him of his office and appointed Guan Wen governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month De'an fell. Yang Pei retreated to Xiangyang; the emperor stripped him of rank and appointed Guan Wen governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 國藩屯南康，思整軍出江謀進取，然寇已由都昌陷饒州，別由東流、建德窺樂平，屯景德鎮，東犯祁門、休寧諸處。

translations.literal: Guofan was stationed at Nankang, intending to reorganize the army and go downriver to seek advance, but rebels from Duchang had seized Raozhou, and another route from Dongliu and Jiande eyed Leping, held Jingde Town, and invaded east to Qimen, Xiuning, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan was at Nankang, planning to reorganize his army and advance downriver, but rebels from Duchang had taken Raozhou while another column from Dongliu and Jiande threatened Leping, held Jingdezhen, and pushed east toward Qimen and Xiuning.

sentences.zh: 而湘軍僅萬餘人，水陸分為四：李孟羣等水師回援武昌，塔齊布留攻九江，羅澤南入江西攻饒州，國藩收蕭捷三水師三營屯南康。

translations.literal: Yet the Xiang Army had only a little over ten thousand men; land and water were divided into four: Li Mengqun's naval force returned to aid Wuchang, Ta Qibu remained to attack Jiujiang, Luo Zenan entered Jiangxi to attack Raozhou, and Guofan gathered Xiao Jiesan's three naval camps stationed at Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiang Army numbered barely ten thousand, split four ways: Li Mengqun's fleet returned to aid Wuchang, Ta Qibu remained at Jiujiang, Luo Zenan entered Jiangxi against Raozhou, and Guofan kept Xiao Jiesan's three naval battalions at Nankang.

sentences.zh: 羅澤南奔走往來，克廣信府，收景德。

translations.literal: Luo Zenan rushed back and forth, took Guangxin Prefecture, and recovered Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zenan rushed back and forth, captured Guangxin Prefecture, and retook Jingdezhen.

sentences.zh: 寇之踞徽州者，與土匪相結，據險以抗我軍。

translations.literal: The rebels holding Huizhou allied with local bandits and held difficult terrain to resist our army.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels holding Huizhou allied with local bandits and used the rugged terrain to resist imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 浙軍出境擊寇，復徽州，乘勝克休寧、黟縣、婺源，生擒偽將軍、兩司馬等八名。

translations.literal: Zhejiang troops crossed the border to strike rebels, recovered Huizhou, took advantage of victory to take Xiuning, Yixian, and Wuyuan, and captured alive eight including false generals and deputy marshals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang forces crossed the border, retook Huizhou, and pressed on to capture Xiuning, Yixian, and Wuyuan, taking eight rebel officers alive, including false generals and deputy marshals.

sentences.zh: 秀全命北固山、鎮江、瓜洲、金山四路，約期進犯揚州。

translations.literal: Xiucheng ordered four routes—from Beigu Mountain, Zhenjiang, Guazhou, and Jinshan—to coordinate a date for invading Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng ordered four columns—from Beigu Mountain, Zhenjiang, Guazhou, and Jinshan—to attack Yangzhou on a set date.

sentences.zh: 托明阿伏兵九洑洲，迎擊破之，斷鐵鎖船鍊，焚船三百。

translations.literal: Tuoming'a ambushed at Jiufuzhou, met and broke them, severed the iron-chained boat chains, and burned three hundred vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoming'a ambushed them at Jiufuzhou, routed the attack, cut the iron chains, and burned three hundred boats.

sentences.zh: 諸路寇被創而遁。

translations.literal: Rebel forces on all routes were wounded and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Every rebel column was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 饒州之寇分據樂平、德興、弋陽，江西軍率水陸師往剿。

translations.literal: Raozhou rebels divided and held Leping, Dexing, and Yiyang; Jiangxi forces led land and naval columns to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Raozhou rebels held Leping, Dexing, and Yiyang in separate garrisons; Jiangxi forces marched against them by land and water.

sentences.zh: 寇出五隊來撲，不克而奔，郡城立復。

translations.literal: The rebels came out in five columns to attack; they did not succeed and fled, and the prefectural city was quickly recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sallied in five columns, failed, and fled; the prefectural seat was retaken at once.

sentences.zh: 秀全以金陵山三山為濱江要區，以精卒守之，水師不能上駛。

translations.literal: Xiucheng regarded Jinling's three mountains as key riverfront zones, garrisoned elite troops there, and the naval force could not sail upstream.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng treated the three mountains below Nanjing as the key to the riverfront, posted elite troops there, and blocked the fleet from sailing upstream.

sentences.zh: 托明阿督水師總兵吳全美沿江掃蕩，焚船二百餘艘，獲拖罟、快蟹等船二十五艘、大小砲八十餘尊，生擒偽先鋒陳長順等六十一名。

translations.literal: Tuoming'a directed Naval Commander Wu Quanmei to sweep along the river, burning over two hundred vessels, capturing twenty-five tow-net boats, fast-crab boats, and others, over eighty cannon large and small, and capturing alive sixty-one including the rebel vanguard Chen Changshun.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoming'a directed Naval Commander Wu Quanmei to sweep the riverbank, burning more than two hundred boats and capturing twenty-five vessels—including tow-boats and fast-crabs—plus more than eighty guns of all sizes and sixty-one prisoners, including the false vanguard Chen Changshun.

sentences.zh: 吳全美乘勢上山，蹋平營卡。

translations.literal: Wu Quanmei took advantage of momentum to ascend the mountain and trample flat the stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Quanmei pressed up the slopes and overran the stockades.

sentences.zh: 江西肅清，水師始棹行無阻。

translations.literal: Jiangxi was cleared and pacified, and the naval force could at last row without obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiangxi cleared, the fleet could sail without hindrance.

sentences.zh: 五月，秀全謀襲金口，斷楚軍糧道。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Xiucheng plotted to strike Jinkou and cut the Chu Army's supply route.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Xiucheng planned to strike Jinkou and sever the Chu Army's supply line.

sentences.zh: 林翼督軍屢戰，斬其偽丞相陳大為等，進屯紙坊，逼省城小東門。

translations.literal: Linyi supervised the army in repeated battles, beheaded the rebel chancellor Chen Dawei and others, advanced to camp at Zhifang, and pressed the provincial city's small east gate.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi fought battle after battle, beheaded the false chancellor Chen Dawei and others, and encamped at Zhifang, pressing the provincial city's lesser east gate.

sentences.zh: 寇潛自他門出掠。

translations.literal: The rebels secretly sallied from other gates to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels slipped out through other gates to raid.

sentences.zh: 林翼建議先攻漢陽，扼溳口、蔡店要隘，絕竄湘之路；

translations.literal: Linyi proposed first attacking Hanyang, holding the key passes of Yukou and Caidian, and cutting off the route of flight into Hunan;
translations.idiomatic: Linyi proposed attacking Hanyang first, seizing the passes at Yukou and Caidian, and cutting the rebels' escape route into Hunan;

sentences.zh: 開濬江隄，以水師腹背攻之，則漢陽可破，而鄂省咽喉已通，不難併力於武昌矣。

translations.literal: dredging the river dike so the naval force could attack from front and rear—then Hanyang could be broken, the throat of E Province would be open, and it would not be difficult to combine forces on Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: then dredging the river dike so the fleet could attack from both sides. Hanyang would fall, the gateway to Hubei would open, and concentrating on Wuchang would become straightforward.

sentences.zh: 初，寇由府河入湘，所過州邑悉殘破無完土，復為官文伏軍所狙擊，分途潰退。

translations.literal: Early on, rebels by the prefecture river entered Hunan; every prefecture and county they passed was ravaged to incomplete soil, then again were ambushed by Guan Wen's hidden troops and split routes and retreated in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, rebels had entered Hunan by the Fu River, laying waste to every district they passed until Guan Wen's ambushes broke them up and drove them back in disorder.

sentences.zh: 六月，收復雲夢、應城，二城者府河出入要道也，寇失之，大恐。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Yunmeng and Yingcheng were recovered; the two cities were the vital passage of the prefecture river in and out—the rebels lost them and were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yunmeng and Yingcheng were retaken. They guarded the Fu River corridor; the rebels' loss of them threw them into panic.

sentences.zh: 我軍進攻德安，斷其出入，寇始不敢窺伺荊襄。

translations.literal: Our army advanced to attack De'an, cutting their coming and going; the rebels then dared not spy on Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial forces pressed De'an and cut the rebels' lines of movement; they no longer dared threaten Jingzhou and Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 七月，塔齊布卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Ta Qibu died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Ta Qibu died in camp.

sentences.zh: 寇陷義寧，國藩遣羅澤南出奇兵復之。

translations.literal: The rebels seized Yining; Guofan sent Luo Zenan with a surprise force to recover it.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels took Yining; Guofan sent Luo Zenan with a flanking force to retake it.

sentences.zh: 寇嚴守襄河蔡店，上通德安，下達漢鎮，互為應援。

translations.literal: The rebels strictly held the Xiang River at Caidian, communicating up to De'an and down to Hankou, mutually supporting one another.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Caidian on the Xiang River in strength, linking De'an above with Hankou below.

sentences.zh: 十二月，彭玉麟克蔡店，水陸並進，毀襄河鐵索浮橋，蹋平南岸敵巢，而下游塘角、漢陽、大別山營壘焚毀殆盡，德安之寇益蹙。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Peng Yulin took Caidian; land and water advanced together, destroyed the Xiang River iron chains and floating bridge, trampled flat the south-bank enemy nests, while downstream Tangjiao, Hanyang, and Dabie Mountain camps were almost all burned, and the De'an rebels were increasingly cornered.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Peng Yulin took Caidian. Land and naval forces advanced together, destroyed the iron chains and pontoon bridge on the Xiang, and overran the south-bank strongpoints. Downstream, camps at Tangjiao, Hanyang, and Dabie Mountain were nearly all burned, and the rebels at De'an were driven into a tighter corner.

sentences.zh: 林翼既克蔡店，而漢川為蔡店後路，寇據此游行衝突，德安亦資以通聲氣。

translations.literal: After Linyi had taken Caidian, Hanchuan was the rear route to Caidian; rebels held this place to roam and strike in raids, and De'an also relied on it for communication.
translations.idiomatic: After Linyi took Caidian, Hanchuan remained the rebels' line of retreat; they used it to raid at will and keep in touch with De'an.

sentences.zh: 林翼與官文會軍克復漢川，武漢首尾始聯絡一氣。

translations.literal: Linyi and Guan Wen combined armies and recovered Hanchuan; Wuhan's head and tail were at last linked in one breath.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi and Guan Wen joined forces and retook Hanchuan, at last linking the Wuhan positions into a single front.

sentences.zh: 蕪湖之陷幾二載矣，江、皖往來道梗。

translations.literal: Wuhu's fall had been nearly two years; traffic between Jiang and Anhui on the road was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhu had been in rebel hands for nearly two years, blocking traffic between Jiangsu and Anhui.

sentences.zh: 寇以為上下關鍵，水則聯艦，陸則砌臺，我軍屢攻不能拔。

translations.literal: The rebels regarded it as the upper and lower key; on water they linked warships, on land they built platforms—our army repeatedly attacked but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels treated it as the linchpin of the region, chaining boats on the water and building platforms on land; imperial forces attacked again and again without success.

sentences.zh: 是月，向榮督軍分道擊之，縣城始復。

translations.literal: That month, Xiang Rong supervised the army attacking on separate routes, and the county seat was at last recovered.
translations.idiomatic: That month Xiang Rong attacked on several fronts and retook the county seat.

sentences.zh: 楚南軍亦攻復湖口、都昌。

translations.literal: The Chu southern army also attacked and recovered Hukou and Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Chu forces also retook Hukou and Duchang.

sentences.zh: 八月，按察使李孟群守金口，崇寧寇句結武昌城黨分道來撲，陸營失守，林翼亦敗於奓山，退保大軍山。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Surveillance Commissioner Li Mengqun defended Jinkou; Chongning rebels colluded with Wuchang city partisans to attack on separate routes; the land camp lost its position, and Linyi was also defeated at Zhail Mountain and retreated to secure Dajun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Li Mengqun held Jinkou. Chongning rebels joined forces with partisans inside Wuchang and attacked from several directions. The land camp gave way, Linyi was beaten at Zhail Mountain, and fell back to Dajun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 寇勢復熾，分擾漢陽，並繞道襲陷漢川。

translations.literal: Rebel momentum revived; they harassed Hanyang in separate groups and also made a detour to strike and seize Hanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel strength surged again. They raided Hanyang in separate columns and outflanked imperial forces to retake Hanchuan.

sentences.zh: 九月，官文、林翼檄調羅澤南援武漢，澤南上書請率所部以行，謂：「得武昌乃可控制江、皖，屏蔽江西，而後內湖外江聲息可通，攻九江始操勝券。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Guan Wen and Linyi issued orders transferring Luo Zenan to aid Wuhan; Zenan memorialized asking to lead his command on the march, saying: "Only with Wuchang can we control Jiang and Anhui, shield Jiangxi, and then inner-lake and outer-river communications can connect—attacking Jiujiang will then hold the winning hand."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Guan Wen and Linyi ordered Luo Zenan to relieve Wuhan. Zenan petitioned to lead his troops in person, arguing that only with Wuchang could they control the Yangtze provinces, shield Jiangxi, reopen communications between the lake fleet and the river fleet, and make an attack on Jiujiang winnable.

sentences.zh: 」國藩從之，乃部署援師五千人，自義寧趨通城。

translations.literal: Guofan agreed and deployed five thousand relief troops marching from Yining toward Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan agreed and sent five thousand reinforcements from Yining toward Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 寇聞我軍至桂口，分眾來援，設木城重壕自固。

translations.literal: Rebels heard our army had reached Guikou and divided forces to come to the rescue, setting up wooden walls and deep moats to fortify themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that imperial troops had reached Guikou, the rebels split their forces to reinforce the position and ringed it with wooden walls and deep trenches.

sentences.zh: 澤南會軍克之，進攻崇陽。

translations.literal: Zenan joined forces and took it, then advanced to attack Chongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zenan joined the assault, took the position, and marched on Chongyang.

sentences.zh: 桂口寇退入崇陽，密約通山來援。

translations.literal: Guikou rebels retreated into Chongyang and secretly arranged for Tongshan to come to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: The Guikou rebels withdrew into Chongyang and secretly summoned aid from Tongshan.

sentences.zh: 桂口與湖南、江西、湖北交界，形勢奧衍，米糧充足。

translations.literal: Guikou bordered Hunan, Jiangxi, and Hubei; its terrain was deep and complex, and grain was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Guikou lay where Hunan, Jiangxi, and Hubei met—rugged country with ample grain.

sentences.zh: 曩偽丞相鍾酋義寧敗後，踞此修土木城，跨山引澗，袤斜六里，欲踞一隅以掣三省之師，伺隙而動。

translations.literal: Formerly the rebel chancellor Zhong You, after defeat at Yining, had held this place building earthen and wooden walls, spanning mountains and drawing streams, six li in winding extent, intending to hold one corner to tie down armies of three provinces and watch for openings to strike.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat at Yining, the false chancellor Zhong You had fortified the place with earthen and wooden walls stretching six li across the hills, hoping to pin down armies from three provinces and strike when he saw an opening.

sentences.zh: 澤南移得勝之兵先奪是隘，進克崇陽，焚寇壘，馳赴羊樓司扼敵上竄。

translations.literal: Zenan shifted his victorious troops first to seize this pass, advanced to take Chongyang, burned rebel fortifications, and rushed to Yanglousi to block the enemy's flight upward.
translations.idiomatic: Zenan sent his victorious troops to seize the pass first, took Chongyang, burned the rebel works, and hurried to Yanglousi to block the enemy's retreat upriver.

sentences.zh: 十月，克復廬州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Luzhou was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Luzhou was retaken.

sentences.zh: 廬州陷已三年矣，守之者為偽豫王胡以晃，與我軍大小數百戰，死傷萬餘，皆受創而去，是月始克之。

translations.literal: Luzhou had fallen for three years; the defender was the rebel Prince of Yu Hu Yihuang; with our army they fought hundreds of battles large and small, over ten thousand dead and wounded—all left wounded—and only this month was it taken.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou had been in rebel hands for three years, defended by the false Prince of Yu, Hu Yihuang. Imperial forces fought hundreds of engagements there, suffering more than ten thousand casualties before the city fell that month.

sentences.zh: 其據德安者，眾不過數千，恃武漢為下游奧主，襄、府二河群蟻聚。

translations.literal: Those holding De'an numbered only a few thousand, relying on Wuhan as the downstream stronghold, with swarms of rebels gathered on the Xiang and Fu rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The De'an garrison numbered only a few thousand, but they relied on Wuhan downstream and on rebel swarms along the Xiang and Fu rivers.

sentences.zh: 我軍勝東挫西，疲於奔命。

translations.literal: Our army won in the east and lost in the west, exhausted from running to and fro.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial forces won in the east and lost in the west, worn out by constant marches.

sentences.zh: 至是官文督兵力戰，守城寇黨陸長年、馬超羣潛赴大營投誠，約為內應。

translations.literal: By then Guan Wen supervised repeated fierce battles; defending-city rebel partisans Lu Changnian and Ma Chaoqun secretly went to the grand camp to surrender, arranging to serve as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen fought battle after battle until rebel officers Lu Changnian and Ma Chaoqun secretly came over, offering to open the gates from within.

sentences.zh: 值大風雨，放火開門納師，遂復其城。

translations.literal: During great wind and rain they set fires and opened the gate to admit the army, and the city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In a driving storm they set fires, opened the gates, and admitted imperial troops, and the city was retaken.

sentences.zh: 時寇之牽制我軍者三路：自隨、棗至襄陽為北路，武昌上下為南路，漢川中路。

translations.literal: At that time rebels tying down our army had three routes: from Suizhou and Zaoyang to Xiangyang as the northern route, above and below Wuchang as the southern route, and Hanchuan as the middle route.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were pinning imperial forces on three fronts: the northern route from Suizhou and Zaoyang toward Xiangyang, the southern route along the Wuchang stretch of the Yangtze, and the middle route through Hanchuan.

sentences.zh: 尾潛、沔，首德安為尤要，屢收屢陷。

translations.literal: Tail at Qian and Mian, head at De'an was especially vital—recovered and lost repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: The line from Qianjiang and Mianyang to De'an was the most critical—and changed hands again and again.

sentences.zh: 官文督軍分四道齊集漢川，克之，遂率兵東下，與林翼合謀武漢。

translations.literal: Guan Wen supervised the army in four columns gathering at Hanchuan, took it, then led troops east downriver to join Linyi in planning for Wuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen concentrated four columns on Hanchuan, retook it, then marched east to join Linyi in planning the recovery of Wuhan.

sentences.zh: 石達開自安慶率三萬人上援武昌。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai from Anqing led thirty thousand men upriver to relieve Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai marched from Anqing with thirty thousand men to relieve Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 澤南會林翼夾攻，連克蒲圻、咸寧；

translations.literal: Zenan joined Linyi in pincer attack, taking in succession Puqi and Xianning;
translations.idiomatic: Zenan and Linyi attacked together and in succession retook Puqi and Xianning;

sentences.zh: 至金口，會攻武昌，破城外敵壘，駐軍洪山。

translations.literal: reaching Jinkou, they jointly attacked Wuchang, broke outer enemy fortifications, and encamped on Hongshan.
translations.idiomatic: at Jinkou they joined in the assault on Wuchang, stormed the outer rebel works, and encamped on Hongshan.

sentences.zh: 寇之踞武昌者，城外大壘八、小壘二。

translations.literal: Rebels holding Wuchang had eight large outer forts and two small ones.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuchang garrison held eight large outer forts and two smaller ones.

sentences.zh: 林翼與戰，澤南襲之，破大壘一、小壘二。

translations.literal: Linyi fought them; Zenan raided them, breaking one large fort and two small ones.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi engaged them in front while Zenan struck from the flank, taking one large fort and two small ones.

sentences.zh: 李孟羣亦薄攻漢南，與官文軍相聲援。

translations.literal: Li Mengqun also pressed attacks on Hannan, coordinating with Guan Wen's army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mengqun pressed the attack on southern Hanyang in coordination with Guan Wen.

sentences.zh: 水師往來南北燒敵船，都興阿以馬隊護之。

translations.literal: The naval force traveled north and south burning enemy vessels; Du Xing'a protected them with cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet ranged north and south burning rebel boats while Du Xing'a's cavalry screened the operations.

sentences.zh: 群帥輯和，寇益不得逞。

translations.literal: Commanders worked in harmony; rebels were increasingly unable to prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders cooperated, and the rebels could make less and less headway.

sentences.zh: 漢陽城外自龜山沿河而下，敵船林立。

translations.literal: Outside Hanyang city from Guishan along the river downward, enemy boats lined the banks.
translations.idiomatic: From Tortoise Hill down the Hanyang waterfront, rebel boats lined the shore.

sentences.zh: 上游入江之梁子湖，下游金牛鎮，群寇赴援。

translations.literal: Upstream Liangzi Lake where it enters the river, downstream Jinniu Town—swarms of rebels came to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel reinforcements poured in from Liangzi Lake upriver and Jinniu Town downriver.

sentences.zh: 水陸各軍督團勇犁巢掃穴，武漢外患至此盡除。

translations.literal: Land and naval forces with militia uprooted nests and swept lairs; Wuhan's external threats were at last wholly removed.
translations.idiomatic: Land and naval forces with local militia uprooted rebel strongpoints, and the threats around Wuhan were at last cleared.

sentences.zh: 秀全以瓜、鎮屢挫敗，圖往援，十一月，出龍脖子等處。

translations.literal: Xiucheng, with Guazhou and Zhenjiang repeatedly defeated, planned to go to their aid; in the eleventh month he sallied from Longbozi and other places.
translations.idiomatic: With Guazhou and Zhenjiang suffering repeated defeats, Xiucheng planned to reinforce them and in the eleventh month marched out from Longbozi and other points.

sentences.zh: 向榮飭張國樑敗之仙鶴門、甘家巷，又戰七霞街，斃偽丞相周少魁等四十名；

translations.literal: Xiang Rong ordered Zhang Guoliang to defeat them at Xianhemen and Ganjiaxiang, again fought at Qixia Street, killing forty including the rebel chancellor Zhou Shaokui;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong ordered Zhang Guoliang to rout them at Xianhemen and Ganjiaxiang, then at Qixia Street killed forty rebels including the false chancellor Zhou Shaokui;

sentences.zh: 追至石埠橋，馘二千餘，逃入城不敢復出。

translations.literal: pursued to Shibuqiao, took over two thousand heads; they fled into the city and dared not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: pursued them to Shibuqiao and killed more than two thousand; the survivors fled into the city and dared not sally again.

sentences.zh: 秀全於對江九洑洲築石壘，浚深壕，悉銳守之，為金陵屏蔽。

translations.literal: Xiucheng built stone fortifications on Jiufuzhou across the river, dug deep moats, and stationed all elite troops to guard it as a screen for Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng built stone fortifications on Jiufuzhou across the river, dug deep moats, and posted elite troops there to shield Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 寇竄江北，以此為出路，屢攻之未下也。

translations.literal: Rebels fleeing north of the river used this as their outlet—repeated attacks failed to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels crossing to the north bank used it as their escape route; repeated imperial attacks failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 六合知縣溫紹原克其壘，後復為寇據，同治二年始復之。

translations.literal: Liuhe Magistrate Wen Shaoyuan took its fort; later rebels seized it again and it was not recovered until the second year of Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Liuhe Magistrate Wen Shaoyuan captured the fort, but rebels seized it again and it was not retaken until the second year of the Tongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 瓜洲、鎮江一水相望，兩城往來無阻，並時有合竄揚州圖北犯意。

translations.literal: Guazhou and Zhenjiang faced each other across the water with unimpeded traffic; both cities at times planned combined raids on Yangzhou intending to invade north.
translations.idiomatic: Guazhou and Zhenjiang faced each other across a narrow stretch of water with easy traffic between them, and at times coordinated plans to strike north through Yangzhou.
