sentences.zh: 揚州軍與瓜洲相持已二年餘，托明阿以日戰無效，諭士民築長圍於瓜洲之北以扼之，至是圍成。

translations.literal: Yangzhou forces had faced off with Guazhou for over two years; Tuoming'a, with daily battles ineffective, instructed officials and people to build a long encirclement north of Guazhou to choke them—by now the encirclement was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou forces had faced Guazhou for more than two years. Tuoming'a, finding daily fighting ineffective, ordered officials and civilians to build a long encirclement north of Guazhou to choke the rebels—and by now it was complete.

sentences.zh: 寇水路分撲，大敗去，奪其簰船，生擒偽參護鄭金柱等十名。

translations.literal: Rebels attacked by water in separate columns, were greatly defeated and fled; their rafts were seized and ten captured alive including the false aide-de-camp Zheng Jinzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels attacked by water in several columns, were routed, and lost their rafts; ten prisoners were taken alive, including the false aide-de-camp Zheng Jinzhu.

sentences.zh: 吉爾杭阿既克上海，移軍鎮江，是月營小九華山。

translations.literal: Ji'erhang'e, having taken Shanghai, moved his army to Zhenjiang and this month encamped at Xiaojiuhua Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After retaking Shanghai, Ji'erhang'e shifted his army to Zhenjiang and that month encamped on Xiaojiuhua Mountain.

sentences.zh: 又於黃鶴山、京畿嶺築城置砲臺以逼之，並為地道轟城，寇死拒不得入。

translations.literal: Also at Huanghe Mountain and Jingji Ridge built cities and set batteries to press them, and made tunnels to bombard the walls; rebels resisted to the death and entry was not gained.
translations.idiomatic: He also built fortifications and batteries on Huanghe Mountain and Jingji Ridge to press the siege, and dug tunnels to blast the walls, but the rebels held to the death and the city did not fall.

sentences.zh: 十二月，無為寇糾合安慶、蕪湖諸黨東下，圖解鎮江之圍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Wuwu rebels joined Anqing and Wuhu bands marching east to relieve the siege of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month rebels from Wuwei joined bands from Anqing and Wuhu marching east to break the siege of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 蕪湖下至揚州，沿江汊河套港皆寇通藪。

translations.literal: From Wuhu down to Yangzhou, along the river every fork, inlet, and harbor was a rebel thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: From Wuhu down to Yangzhou, every creek, inlet, and harbor along the river served rebel traffic.

sentences.zh: 向榮檄水師泝江會攻，敗之神塘河，又敗裕溪口援寇於陶陽浦，生擒偽檢點趙元發、偽將軍王化興等數十名。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong ordered the naval force upstream in joint attack, defeated them at Shentang River, again defeated relief rebels at Yuxikou at Taoyangpu, capturing alive dozens including false inspector Zhao Yuanfa and false general Wang Huaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong ordered the fleet upstream in a joint attack, routed them at Shentang River, then defeated relief forces at Yuxikou near Taoyangpu, taking dozens of prisoners including the false inspector Zhao Yuanfa and the false general Wang Huaxing.

sentences.zh: 十二日，秀全遣李秀成等援鎮江，我軍禦之石埠橋，尋由江州下竄下蜀街。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day Xiucheng dispatched Li Xiucheng and others to relieve Zhenjiang; our army met them at Shibuqiao, then they fled downriver through Jiangzhou to Xiaqushu Street.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth Xiucheng sent Li Xiucheng and others to relieve Zhenjiang. Imperial forces met them at Shibuqiao; the rebels then fled downriver through Jiangzhou toward Xiaqushu Street.

sentences.zh: 先是楊秀清調上游蕪湖，江北和、含及廬州眾還江寧，統以李秀成及偽丞相陳玉成、偽春官丞相涂鎮興、偽夏官副丞相陳仕章、偽夏官正丞相周勝坤，取道棲霞、石埠，而豫遣城寇四出絓我軍。

translations.literal: Earlier Yang Xiuqing had transferred upstream from Wuhu, bringing north-of-the-river He, Han, and Luzhou forces back to Jiangning, all under Li Xiucheng and the rebel chancellor Chen Yucheng, rebel Spring Office chancellor Tu Zhenxing, rebel Summer Office vice chancellor Chen Shizhang, and rebel Summer Office chief chancellor Zhou Shengkun, taking the route through Qixia and Shibu, while in advance ordering city rebels to sally on all sides to entangle our army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yang Xiuqing had recalled forces from Wuhu and from north of the river at He county, Hanyang, and Luzhou to Jiangning under Li Xiucheng, the false chancellor Chen Yucheng, the false Spring Office chancellor Tu Zhenxing, the false Summer Office vice chancellor Chen Shizhang, and the false Summer Office chief chancellor Zhou Shengkun. They marched through Qixia and Shibu while city garrisons sallied on every side to tie down imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 向榮大營存兵不敷分布，檄蕪湖鄧紹良分軍為張國樑、秦如虎應援，令吳全美以師船攻大勝關，以分敵勢。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong's grand camp had insufficient troops to deploy; he ordered Wuhu's Deng Shaoliang to divide forces as relief for Zhang Guoliang and Qin Ruhu, commanded Wu Quanmei to attack Dashengguan with war junks to divide enemy strength.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong's main camp had too few men to cover every front. He ordered Deng Shaoliang at Wuhu to detach troops for Zhang Guoliang and Qin Ruhu and sent Wu Quanmei with war junks against Dashengguan to divide rebel strength.

sentences.zh: 明安泰嚴堵秣陵關，咨吉爾杭阿等守丹陽，以固蘇、常要隘。

translations.literal: Ming Antai strictly blocked Moling Pass, consulted Ji'erhang'a and others to defend Danyang, to secure the key passes of Su and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Antai sealed Moling Pass and coordinated with Ji'erhang'a and others to hold Danyang and secure the approaches to Suzhou and Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，澤南既去江西，石達開乘虛復入義寧，敗江西官軍，陷新昌、瑞州、臨江、袁州、安福、分宜、萬載。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Zenan had left Jiangxi, Shi Dakai seized the opening to re-enter Yining, defeated Jiangxi government troops, and seized Xinchang, Ruizhou, Linjiang, Yuanzhou, Anfu, Fenyi, and Wanzai.
translations.idiomatic: After Zenan left Jiangxi, Shi Dakai seized the opening, re-entered Yining, routed Jiangxi government troops, and took Xinchang, Ruizhou, Linjiang, Yuanzhou, Anfu, Fenyi, and Wanzai.

sentences.zh: 江西、湖北隔絕，軍勢不能復振。

translations.literal: Jiangxi and Hubei were cut off; military momentum could not revive.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi and Hubei were cut off from each other, and imperial momentum in the region could not recover.

sentences.zh: 曾國藩飛調副將周鳳山統九江全軍往援，遇寇樟樹鎮，以鉤連槍敗其籐簰手，並會水師燬敵船，新淦寇聞風竄走，遂復其城。

translations.literal: Guofan urgently transferred Deputy Commander Zhou Fengshan commanding the entire Jiujiang army to the rescue; at Zhangshu Town they met rebels and with hooked spears defeated their rattan-shield men, also joined the naval force to burn enemy boats; Xingan rebels fled on the wind and the city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan urgently transferred Deputy Commander Zhou Fengshan with the entire Jiujiang force. At Zhangshu Town they met the rebels and, using hooked spears, broke the rattan-shield corps, joined the fleet in burning rebel boats, and retook Xingan when the garrison fled.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，石達開陷吉安，乃由湖北入通城。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, Shi Dakai seized Ji'an, then entered from Hubei into Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year Shi Dakai took Ji'an, then entered Tongcheng from Hubei.

sentences.zh: 達開悍而多詐，肆擾江西，不急犯省城，不直指南康，先旁收郡縣，遍置偽官，迫其土民，劫以助逆，因糧因兵，愈蔓愈廣。

translations.literal: Dakai was fierce and full of stratagems, wantonly harassing Jiangxi—not urgently attacking the provincial capital, not heading straight for Nankang—first gathering prefectures and counties on the flanks, placing false officials everywhere, forcing local people, extorting them to aid rebellion, relying on local grain and troops, spreading ever wider.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai was fierce and cunning. He ravaged Jiangxi without rushing the provincial capital or striking straight for Nankang, but first swallowed surrounding counties, installed false officials, pressed locals into service, and fed his army on local grain until the rebellion spread ever wider.

sentences.zh: 其陷瑞州者為偽檢點賴裕新，先陷袁州者為偽豫王胡以晃，先攻臨江後攻吉安者為偽春官丞相張遂謀。

translations.literal: Those who seized Ruizhou were led by false inspector Lai Yuxin; those who first seized Yuanzhou were the false Prince of Yu Hu Yihuang; those who first attacked Linjiang then Ji'an were the false Spring Office chancellor Zhang Suimou.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizhou fell to the false inspector Lai Yuxin; Yuanzhou to the false Prince of Yu, Hu Yihuang; Linjiang and then Ji'an to the false Spring Office chancellor Zhang Suimou.

sentences.zh: 廣東土匪入江西者，以周培春黨為眾。

translations.literal: Guangdong bandits entering Jiangxi were most numerous in Zhou Peichun's band.
translations.idiomatic: The largest Guangdong bandit force in Jiangxi was Zhou Peichun's faction.

sentences.zh: 又匪目葛耀明、鄧象等均於瑞州入達開大股之中，匪目王義潮、劉夢熊分屯吉安、泰和，亦與達開合併為一。

translations.literal: Also bandit chiefs Ge Yaoming, Deng Xiang, and others all entered Dakai's main force at Ruizhou; bandit chiefs Wang Yichao and Liu Mengxiong garrisoned separately at Ji'an and Taihe, also merging with Dakai as one.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit chiefs Ge Yaoming and Deng Xiang and others joined Dakai's main body at Ruizhou, while Wang Yichao and Liu Mengxiong held Ji'an and Taihe before merging with Dakai as well.

sentences.zh: 達開久居臨江，為上下適中之地，凶悍之眾，皆萃於此。

translations.literal: Dakai long dwelt at Linjiang as the central point between upper and lower reaches; fierce and brutal masses all gathered there.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai made his headquarters at Linjiang, the hub between upper and lower Jiangxi, where his fiercest troops gathered.

sentences.zh: 南則窺伺贛州、南安以通粵匪，北則踞守武寧、新昌以通九江。

translations.literal: South they eyed Ganzhou and Nan'an to link with Guangdong bandits; north they held Wuning and Xinchang to link with Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: To the south he eyed Ganzhou and Nan'an to link with Guangdong bandits; to the north he held Wuning and Xinchang to keep contact with Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 達開進攻南昌，周鳳山以九江全軍守樟樹鎮。

translations.literal: Dakai pressed the attack on Nanchang; Zhou Fengshan with the entire Jiujiang army guarded Zhangshu Town.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai pressed the attack on Nanchang while Zhou Fengshan with the Jiujiang army held Zhangshu Town.

sentences.zh: 時達開眾才數千餘，乃張燈火山谷間為疑兵，率敢死士乘夜來襲，我軍不戰而潰。

translations.literal: At that time Dakai's force was only a few thousand; he lit lamps on mountains and valleys as a ruse, led dare-to-die troops to raid by night, and our army dispersed without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai had only a few thousand men, but he lit fires along the hills as a ruse and led a night attack with his shock troops; the imperial force broke without a fight.

sentences.zh: 鳳山走南昌，國藩亦移軍省城。

translations.literal: Fengshan fled to Nanchang; Guofan also moved his army to the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshan fled to Nanchang, and Guofan moved his headquarters to the provincial city as well.

sentences.zh: 秀全益以皖、贛諸事付達開，尋陷進賢、東鄉、安仁，破撫州。

translations.literal: Xiucheng increasingly entrusted Anhui and Jiangxi affairs to Dakai; soon Jinxian, Dongxiang, and Anren fell and Fuzhou was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng gave Dakai ever broader authority over Anhui and Jiangxi. Soon Jinxian, Dongxiang, and Anren fell, and Fuzhou was overrun.

sentences.zh: 未幾，建康、南昌相繼失。

translations.literal: Before long, Jiankang and Nanchang were lost in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Before long both Jiankang and Nanchang were lost.

sentences.zh: 澤南念國藩艱危，日夜憂憤，督戰益急。

translations.literal: Zenan, mindful of Guofan's peril, worried and grieved day and night, supervised battle ever more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Guofan's danger, Zenan fretted day and night and pressed the fighting ever harder.

sentences.zh: 秦日綱嬰城待援，士卒多傷亡，陰穴城為突門。

translations.literal: Qin Rigang held the city awaiting relief; soldiers suffered many casualties and deaths; they secretly tunneled through the wall for a sally gate.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Rigang held the city awaiting relief. Casualties mounted, and the defenders secretly dug a sally port through the wall.

sentences.zh: 會達開率九江援黨至，開城迎之。

translations.literal: When Dakai led Jiujiang relief bands arrived, they opened the city to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: When Dakai arrived with reinforcements from Jiujiang, the garrison opened the gates to admit them.

sentences.zh: 澤南要之突門，寇出直衝澤南軍。

translations.literal: Zenan intercepted them at the sally gate; rebels came out and charged straight at Zenan's army.
translations.idiomatic: Zenan waited at the sally port; the rebels burst out and charged straight at his line.

sentences.zh: 澤南三退三進，軍幾潰，槍丸中左額，收軍還，創發而歿。

translations.literal: Zenan retreated three times and advanced three times; the army nearly collapsed; a musket ball struck his left forehead; he withdrew the army, the wound festered, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zenan fell back three times and advanced three; his army nearly broke. A bullet struck his left forehead. He withdrew, the wound festered, and he died.

sentences.zh: 以李續賓領其眾。

translations.literal: Li Xubing was appointed to command his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xubing took command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 續賓初建議分屯窯彎絕寇糧，既代澤南，仍屯洪山，以游兵巡窯彎、塘角間。

translations.literal: Xubing had originally proposed dividing encampments at Yaowan to cut off rebel grain; after replacing Zenan he still encamped at Hongshan, using mobile troops to patrol between Yaowan and Tangjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xubing had first proposed holding Yaowan to cut rebel supplies. After succeeding Zenan he remained on Hongshan and sent mobile detachments to patrol between Yaowan and Tangjiao.

sentences.zh: 古隆賢率萬人來援武昌，約城寇舉燧為識，林翼諜知，佯舉火，城寇出，陷伏大敗。

translations.literal: Gu Longxian led ten thousand men to relieve Wuchang, arranging with city rebels to raise beacon fires as signal; Linyi learned by espionage and feigned raising fires; city rebels came out and fell into ambush, suffering great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Longxian brought ten thousand men to relieve Wuchang and arranged beacon signals with the city garrison. Linyi learned of the plan and lit decoy fires; when the garrison sallied, they were ambushed and routed.

sentences.zh: 達開援眾號十萬，林翼分水陸力戰，焚敵船七十，平八十壘。

translations.literal: Dakai's relief force claimed one hundred thousand; Linyi divided land and water forces for fierce battle, burning seventy enemy boats and leveling eighty fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai's relief army was said to number one hundred thousand. Linyi fought them by land and water, burning seventy boats and leveling eighty fortifications.

sentences.zh: 武昌寇大窘，城守益固。

translations.literal: Wuchang rebels were greatly cornered and defended the city ever more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuchang garrison was driven into a tight corner and tightened its defense of the city.

sentences.zh: 而江西請師日數至，義寧寇復犯崇通，九江寇合興國、大冶土寇自武昌縣進至葛店，謀襲巡撫大營。

translations.literal: Yet Jiangxi sent appeals for troops day after day; Yining rebels again invaded Chong and Tong; Jiujiang rebels joined Xingguo and Daye local bandits advancing from Wuchang county to Gedian, plotting to raid the governor's grand camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yet appeals for help poured in from Jiangxi. Rebels from Yining struck Chongyang and Tongcheng again, while Jiujiang rebels joined local bandits from Xingguo and Daye, advancing from Wuchang county toward Gedian to raid the governor's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 林翼以江西待援，分軍四千一百人，以國藩弟國華統之，率劉騰鴻、劉連捷等道義寧，收咸寧、蒲圻、崇陽、通城、上高。

translations.literal: Linyi, with Jiangxi awaiting relief, divided four thousand one hundred troops under Guofan's younger brother Guohua, leading Liu Tenghong, Liu Lianjie, and others by the Yining route, recovering Xianning, Puqi, Chongyang, Tongcheng, and Shanggao.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiangxi desperate for aid, Linyi detached 4,100 men under Guofan's younger brother Guohua, with Liu Tenghong, Liu Lianjie, and others marching through Yining to retake Xianning, Puqi, Chongyang, Tongcheng, and Shanggao.

sentences.zh: 湖南所遣援軍將劉長佑收萍鄉，蕭啟江收萬載。

translations.literal: Hunan's dispatched relief army General Liu Changyou recovered Pingxiang; Xiao Qijiang recovered Wanzai.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan's relief commander Liu Changyou retook Pingxiang; Xiao Qijiang retook Wanzai.

sentences.zh: 國藩命李元度收東鄉，周鳳山等收進賢，劉子淳收豐城。

translations.literal: Guofan ordered Li Yuandu to recover Dongxiang; Zhou Fengshan and others recovered Jinxian; Liu Zichun recovered Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan ordered Li Yuandu to retake Dongxiang; Zhou Fengshan and others retook Jinxian; Liu Zichun retook Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 五月，畢金科將千人防饒州，陷，旋收復。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Bi Jinke with a thousand men defended Raozhou, it fell, then was soon recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Bi Jinke defended Raozhou with a thousand men; the city fell but was soon retaken.

sentences.zh: 黃虎臣將三千五百人攻建昌，遇寇死。

translations.literal: Huang Huchen with thirty-five hundred men attacked Jianchang, met rebels and died.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Huchen attacked Jianchang with 3,500 men and was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 六月，彭玉麟收復南康。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Peng Yulin recovered Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Peng Yulin retook Nankang.

sentences.zh: 七月，劉騰鴻至瑞州，戰寇，走之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Liu Tenghong reached Ruizhou, fought rebels, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Liu Tenghong reached Ruizhou, fought the rebels, and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 是時江西列縣陷者四十餘城，廣東和平土寇犯定南、安遠、信豐、長寧、上猶、崇義、雩都，省城不能救，軍報數月不相聞。

translations.literal: At that time over forty prefectures and counties in Jiangxi had fallen; Guangdong Heping local bandits invaded Dingnan, Anyuan, Xinfeng, Changning, Shangyou, Chongyi, and Yudu; the provincial city could not rescue them and military reports went months without connection.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty Jiangxi prefectures and counties had fallen. Guangdong bandits from Heping raided Dingnan, Anyuan, Xinfeng, Changning, Shangyou, Chongyi, and Yudu, and the provincial capital could not relieve them; for months no reliable reports arrived.

sentences.zh: 瑞州居江、湘之衝，有南北城，中隔一河。

translations.literal: Ruizhou lay at the junction of the Yangtze and Xiang; it had north and south cities with a river between.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizhou stood at the junction of the Gan and Xiang rivers and was divided into north and south cities by the stream between them.

sentences.zh: 劉騰鴻援南城，韋昌輝自臨江來援，至北城，遽挑戰，騰鴻乘其弊攻之，從北岸渡河抄其後，南城兵角其前，寇大敗。

translations.literal: Liu Tenghong relieved Nancheng; Wei Changhui came from Linjiang to relieve, reached the north city and abruptly offered battle; Tenghong exploited their weakness to attack, crossed from the north bank to strike their rear while Nancheng troops engaged from the front—the rebels suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tenghong relieved Nancheng. Wei Changhui marched from Linjiang to reinforce the north city and offered battle abruptly. Tenghong struck at their weakness, crossed from the north bank to hit their rear while Nancheng troops engaged from the front, and the rebels were routed.

sentences.zh: 至是江湖路通，自長沙以至南昌無道梗憂。

translations.literal: By then the river-lake route was open; from Changsha to Nanchang there was no fear of blocked roads.
translations.idiomatic: The river route was open again, and the road from Changsha to Nanchang was no longer cut.

sentences.zh: 寇自陷吉、袁、瑞、臨諸府，大修戰船，議秋間圍攻省城。

translations.literal: Rebels, having seized Ji, Yuan, Rui, and Lin prefectures, greatly rebuilt warships and planned to besiege the provincial city in autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Having taken Ji'an, Yuanzhou, Ruizhou, and Linjiang, the rebels rebuilt their fleet and planned a autumn siege of the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 瑞、臨寇船出而下，湖口寇船入而上，困我水師，復於生米口築立堅壘。

translations.literal: Rui and Lin rebel boats came downriver, Hukou rebel boats came upriver, trapping our naval force; they also built firm fortifications at Shengmi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel boats from Ruizhou and Linjiang moved downstream while boats from Hukou moved upstream, trapping the imperial fleet, and they fortified Shengmi Pass.

sentences.zh: 七月，由松湖帶戰船三十餘艘、陸寇千餘，將抵瑞河口，我水師偵知，豫釘排樁。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, from Songhu they brought over thirty warships and over a thousand land rebels, about to reach Ruihekou; our naval force detected them and in advance drove in stake barriers.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month more than thirty warships and over a thousand rebel troops left Songhu for Ruihekou. The imperial fleet detected them and drove in stake barriers in advance.

sentences.zh: 寇甫至，我軍衝入，縱火焚之，復堵城寇於臨江口，焚其船壘。

translations.literal: As rebels had just arrived our army charged in and set fires to burn them, also blocked city rebels at Linjiang mouth and burned their boats and fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the rebels arrived, imperial forces charged in and set them afire, then blocked the Linjiang mouth and burned the city garrison's boats and works.

sentences.zh: 生米口之寇聞之亦遁。

translations.literal: Shengmi Pass rebels, hearing this, also fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels at Shengmi Pass fled on hearing the news.

sentences.zh: 八月，劉騰鴻等敗臨川偽指揮黃某，收復靖安、安義。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Liu Tenghong and others defeated the false Linjiang commander Huang and recovered Jing'an and Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Liu Tenghong and others defeated the false Linjiang commander Huang and retook Jing'an and Anyi.

sentences.zh: 寧都土寇襲陷建昌、鉛山、貴溪，圍廣信。

translations.literal: Ningdu local bandits raided and seized Jianchang, Qianshan, and Guixi, besieging Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: Ningdu bandits raided Jianchang, Qianshan, and Guixi and besieged Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 浙將饒廷選赴援，寇遁走。

translations.literal: Zhejiang General Rao Tingxuan went to the rescue; bandits fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang General Rao Tingxuan marched to the relief and the bandits fled.

sentences.zh: 時江西寇勢浩大，黨類眾多，欲以全力困江西。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangxi rebel momentum was vast with many factions, intending to use full strength to pin down Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel strength in Jiangxi was enormous and divided among many leaders, who meant to pin down the entire province.

sentences.zh: 自去年十一月至本年二月，以石達開為主；

translations.literal: From last year's eleventh month to this year's second month, Shi Dakai was chief;
translations.idiomatic: From the eleventh month of the previous year through the second month of this year, Shi Dakai held chief command;

sentences.zh: 三、四、五月，以黃玉崑為主；

translations.literal: in the third, fourth, and fifth months, Huang Yukun was chief;
translations.idiomatic: in the third, fourth, and fifth months, Huang Yukun;

sentences.zh: 六、七月，以韋昌輝為主。

translations.literal: in the sixth and seventh months, Wei Changhui was chief.
translations.idiomatic: in the sixth and seventh months, Wei Changhui.

sentences.zh: 九江則林啟容，瑞州則賴裕新，湖口則黃文金，撫州則三檢點，建昌則張三和，袁州則李能通，皆劇寇也。

translations.literal: Jiujiang had Lin Qirong, Ruizhou Lai Yuxin, Hukou Huang Wenjin, Fuzhou the Three Inspectors, Jianchang Zhang Sanhe, Yuanzhou Li Nengtong—all fierce rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiujiang stood Lin Qirong; at Ruizhou, Lai Yuxin; at Hukou, Huang Wenjin; at Fuzhou, the Three Inspectors; at Jianchang, Zhang Sanhe; at Yuanzhou, Li Nengtong—all formidable rebel commanders.

sentences.zh: 統計江西境內近十萬人。

translations.literal: In total within Jiangxi territory there were nearly one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In all, nearly one hundred thousand rebels operated within Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 九月，國藩視師瑞州，李元度以撫州不克，餉益絀，乃分軍略旁縣募糧，且分寇勢，遂收宜黃，復崇仁。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Guofan went in person to command at Ruizhou; Li Yuandu, with Fuzhou not taken and supplies ever more strained, divided forces to seize nearby counties to raise grain and divide rebel strength, thus taking Yihuang and recovering Chongren.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Guofan took command at Ruizhou in person. With Fuzhou still untaken and supplies running short, Li Yuandu divided his force to seize neighboring counties for grain and to split rebel strength, retaking Yihuang and Chongren.

sentences.zh: 是日城寇出攻江軍，林原恩敗死，元度突圍免。

translations.literal: That day city rebels sallied to attack the Jiangxi army; Lin Yuan'en was defeated and died, while Yuandu broke out of the encirclement and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: That day the city garrison attacked the Jiangxi force. Lin Yuan'en was killed in defeat; Li Yuandu broke out and escaped.

sentences.zh: 撫州軍俱潰，元度移屯貴溪。

translations.literal: The Fuzhou army all collapsed in rout; Yuandu shifted his encampment to Guixi.
translations.idiomatic: The Fuzhou troops collapsed, and Yuandu withdrew to Guixi.

sentences.zh: 十月，復陷宜黃、崇仁，分陷金溪。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Yihuang and Chongren fell again, and Jinxian was seized in a separate thrust.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the rebels retook Yihuang and Chongren and seized Jinxian in a separate attack.

sentences.zh: 福建援軍將張從龍援建昌，軍潰，特詔起黃冕知吉安府，率軍往，以國藩弟國荃為軍主。

translations.literal: Fujian relief army General Zhang Conglong went to aid Jianchang; the army collapsed in rout; by special edict Huang Mian was recalled to serve as magistrate of Ji'an Prefecture and lead troops thither, with Guofan's younger brother Guoquan as army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian relief commander Zhang Conglong marched to aid Jianchang but his force was routed. By special edict Huang Mian was recalled as prefect of Ji'an and sent with troops, with Guofan's brother Guoquan as army commander.

sentences.zh: 當是時，江西軍分為四，湘軍最強。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangxi forces were divided into four; the Xiang Army was strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi forces were then divided into four columns; the Xiang Army was the strongest.

sentences.zh: 國藩居水軍中，劉長祐屯袁州，派隊攻克分宜，援寇路絕。

translations.literal: Guofan dwelt among the naval forces; Liu Changyou encamped at Yuanzhou and dispatched detachments to take Fenyi, cutting off the rebel relief route.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan remained with the fleet while Liu Changyou held Yuanzhou, sent detachments to take Fenyi, and cut the rebels' line of relief.

sentences.zh: 十一月，偽將李能通啟西門納官軍，袁州復。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the rebel general Li Nengtong opened the west gate to admit government troops, and Yuanzhou was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the false general Li Nengtong opened the west gate to imperial troops and Yuanzhou was retaken.

sentences.zh: 國荃收安福。

translations.literal: Guoquan recovered Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan retook Anfu.

sentences.zh: 江西諸軍稍振。

translations.literal: Jiangxi armies recovered somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi forces began to recover their footing.

sentences.zh: 初，武昌久不下，林翼謂戰易攻難，以分兵牽寇斷其援路為要。

translations.literal: Earlier, with Wuchang long untaken, Linyi said that fighting was easy but storming was hard, and that dividing forces to tie down rebels and cut their relief routes was essential.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, with Wuchang still untaken, Linyi argued that battle was easier than siege and that the key was to divide forces, pin the rebels down, and sever their relief routes.

sentences.zh: 是月，唐訓方等敗石達開於葛店。

translations.literal: That month, Tang Xunfang and others defeated Shi Dakai at Gedian.
translations.idiomatic: That month Tang Xunfang and others routed Shi Dakai at Gedian.

sentences.zh: 寇增召戰艦復犯葛店，蔣益澧總六營往，逆戰，克之。

translations.literal: Rebels gathered more warships and again invaded Gedian; Jiang Yili commanded six camps to go, met them in battle, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels gathered more warships and struck Gedian again. Jiang Yili led six camps to meet them and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 追奔至樊口，合水師燔其船，入武昌縣城。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rout to Fankou, they joined the naval force to burn their boats and entered Wuchang county seat.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing to Fankou, they joined the fleet in burning rebel boats and entered Wuchang county.

sentences.zh: 石達開憤樊口之敗，大集黨萬餘，由廣濟、蘄水、黃岡至漢鎮，密約偽丞相鍾某堅守以待。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai, enraged at the defeat at Fankou, massed over ten thousand followers, came from Guangji, Qishui, and Huanggang to Hankou, and secretly arranged with the rebel chancellor Zhong to hold firm and await him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged by the defeat at Fankou, Shi Dakai massed more than ten thousand men from Guangji, Qishui, and Huanggang at Hankou and secretly arranged with the false chancellor Zhong to hold and await him.

sentences.zh: 官文獲其偽諜，令都興阿、多隆阿馬步兜擊，寇大潰。

translations.literal: Guan Wen captured their rebel spy, ordered Du Xing'a and Dolonga's cavalry and infantry to slaughter in encirclement, and the rebels collapsed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen captured a rebel spy and ordered Du Xing'a and Dolonga to encircle and rout the rebels.

sentences.zh: 我軍乘勝攻黃州，不能克。

translations.literal: Our army pressed the advantage to attack Huangzhou but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial forces pressed the attack on Huangzhou but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 舒興阿、舒保等將馬隊四百人渡江，寇於青山、魯港間增十三壘相持。

translations.literal: Shu Xing'a, Shu Bao, and others led four hundred cavalry across the river; rebels added thirteen fortifications between Qingshan and Lugang to hold them off.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xing'a and Shu Bao led four hundred cavalry across the river while rebels built thirteen forts between Qingshan and Lugang to block them.

sentences.zh: 水陸合擊破之，追奔至葛店。

translations.literal: Land and naval forces jointly attacked and broke them, pursuing the rout to Gedian.
translations.idiomatic: Land and naval forces attacked together, broke the rebel line, and pursued to Gedian.

sentences.zh: 寇懾於騎軍，乃大奔。

translations.literal: Rebels were cowed by the cavalry and fled in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified by the cavalry, the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 自是水陸馬步相輔，軍勢日盛，益募陸軍五千、水軍十營，增長圍困之。

translations.literal: From then on land, naval, cavalry, and infantry aided one another; military momentum grew daily; they further recruited five thousand land troops and ten naval camps and extended the long encirclement to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter land, naval, cavalry, and infantry worked together, imperial strength grew daily, and five thousand more infantry and ten naval battalions were raised to tighten the siege.

sentences.zh: 武昌、漢陽同克復，擊斃偽丞相鍾某、偽指揮劉滿，生擒偽將軍、師帥、旅帥、兩司馬五百餘名。

translations.literal: Wuchang and Hanyang were recovered together; the rebel chancellor Zhong and rebel commander Liu Man were killed in battle, and over five hundred false generals, division chiefs, brigade chiefs, and deputy marshals were captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang and Hanyang fell together. The false chancellor Zhong and false commander Liu Man were killed, and more than five hundred false officers from general down to deputy marshal were captured alive.

sentences.zh: 武昌寇分七隊突門出，生擒偽檢點古文新等四人，斃先鋒悍黨八百餘，死兩萬有奇。

translations.literal: Wuchang rebels divided into seven columns and burst through the gates; four including the false inspector Gu Wenxin were captured alive, over eight hundred vanguard fierce partisans were killed, and deaths exceeded twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang rebels broke out in seven columns. Four prisoners including the false inspector Gu Wenxin were taken, more than eight hundred elite vanguard fighters were killed, and rebel dead exceeded twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 蓋武漢自五年三月失守，至是已二十餘月矣。

translations.literal: Wuhan had been lost since the third month of the fifth year; by now more than twenty months had passed.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhan had been in rebel hands since the third month of the fifth year—more than twenty months by now.

sentences.zh: 尋復武昌縣、黃州、興國、大冶、蘄州，民兵復蘄水、廣濟、黃梅。

translations.literal: Soon Wuchang county, Huangzhou, Xingguo, Daye, and Qizhou were recovered; militia recovered Qishui, Guangji, and Huangmei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wuchang county, Huangzhou, Xingguo, Daye, and Qizhou were retaken, and militia recovered Qishui, Guangji, and Huangmei.

sentences.zh: 陳師九江城下。

translations.literal: They pressed the siege below Jiujiang city.
translations.idiomatic: The siege closed on Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，國藩至九江勞軍，議統水師決取九江，以聯絡內外。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Guofan came to Jiujiang to encourage the army and discussed unifying the naval force to decide on taking Jiujiang and linking inner and outer communications.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Guofan came to Jiujiang to encourage the troops and planned to concentrate the fleet, take Jiujiang, and reopen communications between the lake and the river.

sentences.zh: 乃派千總張金璧等復建昌。

translations.literal: He then dispatched Company Commander Zhang Jinbi and others to recover Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Company Commander Zhang Jinbi and others to retake Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 李續賓追寇東下，復瑞昌。

translations.literal: Li Xubing pursued rebels eastward and recovered Ruichang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xubing pursued the rebels east and retook Ruichang.

sentences.zh: 進攻九江，派軍復德安。

translations.literal: He advanced the attack on Jiujiang and dispatched troops to recover De'an.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the attack on Jiujiang and sent troops to retake De'an.

sentences.zh: 劉長祐由袁州赴分宜，寇退踞新喻溪，遇之寶山，降將李能通匹馬衝陣，寇退入城，我軍隨之入，寇出東門遁。

translations.literal: Liu Changyou went from Yuanzhou to Fenyi; rebels retreated to hold Xinyu Stream; meeting them at Baoshan, the surrendered general Li Nengtong charged the line alone on horseback; rebels retreated into the city and our army followed in; rebels fled out the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changyou marched from Yuanzhou toward Fenyi. Rebels fell back to Xinyu Stream; at Baoshan the defector Li Nengtong charged alone on horseback, the rebels withdrew into the city, imperial troops followed, and the garrison fled out the east gate.

sentences.zh: 湖南援軍將劉拔元等收永寧、永新、蓮花廳、崇義、上猶。

translations.literal: Hunan relief army General Liu Bayuan and others recovered Yongning, Yongxin, Lianhua Department, Chongyi, and Shangyou.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan relief commander Liu Bayuan and others retook Yongning, Yongxin, Lianhua, Chongyi, and Shangyou.

sentences.zh: 寇陷鎮江至是四年矣，是年京口為張國樑所迫，秀清命四偽丞相李秀成、陳玉成、陳仕章、涂鎮興往援。

translations.literal: Zhenjiang had been fallen for four years; that year Jingkou was pressed by Zhang Guoliang, and Xiuqing ordered the four false chancellors Li Xiucheng, Chen Yucheng, Chen Shizhang, and Tu Zhenxing to go to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjiang had been in rebel hands for four years. That year Zhang Guoliang pressed Jingkou, and Xiuqing sent the four false chancellors Li Xiucheng, Chen Yucheng, Chen Shizhang, and Tu Zhenxing to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 秀成欲一人渡江，潛往京口，約兵夾擊，無敢應者。

translations.literal: Xiucheng wished to cross the river alone, secretly go to Jingkou, and arrange a pincer attack; none dared respond.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng wanted to cross alone, slip into Jingkou, and coordinate a pincer attack, but no one would agree.

sentences.zh: 玉成乃夜乘小舟潛越水寨，縱兵擊國樑軍，秀成登高見城中兵出，遣鎮興、仕章當敵，而自率奇兵繞國樑軍後擊之。

translations.literal: Yucheng then by night took a small boat to steal past the water stockade, unleashed troops to strike Guoliang's army; Xiucheng climbed high and saw city troops come out, sent Zhenxing and Shizhang to meet the enemy, while he himself led surprise troops to strike Guoliang's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng crossed by night in a small boat, slipped past the water stockade, and attacked Guoliang's army. Xiucheng watched from high ground as city troops sallied, sent Zhenxing and Shizhang to hold the front, and led a flanking force against Guoliang's rear.

sentences.zh: 乘勝擊丹徒，和春敗走，遂渡瓜洲攻揚州，陷之。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of victory they struck Dantu; He Chun was defeated and fled, then crossed Guazhou to attack Yangzhou and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the victory to Dantu, routed He Chun, crossed to Guazhou, attacked Yangzhou, and took it.

sentences.zh: 托明阿軍潰退北路，詔德興阿代領其軍。

translations.literal: Tuoming'a's army collapsed and retreated on the northern route; an edict ordered De Xing'a to take command of his army.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoming'a's army broke on the northern route. An edict put De Xing'a in command.

sentences.zh: 偽顧王吳如孝守鎮江，分兵踞高資。

translations.literal: The false Prince Gu Wu Ruxiao held Zhenjiang and divided forces to hold Gaozi.
translations.idiomatic: The false Prince Gu, Wu Ruxiao, held Zhenjiang and detached troops to hold Gaozi.

sentences.zh: 古爾杭阿檄知府劉存厚扼之，金陵寇大恐。

translations.literal: Ji'erhang'e ordered Prefect Liu Cunhou to block them; Jinling rebels were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'erhang'e ordered Prefect Liu Cunhou to block them, throwing the Nanjing garrison into alarm.

sentences.zh: 秀清遣悍黨數萬出句容來援，吉爾杭阿中砲死。

translations.literal: Xiuqing dispatched tens of thousands of fierce partisans from Jurong to relieve them; Ji'erhang'a was struck by cannon fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuqing sent tens of thousands of elite troops from Jurong to the relief, and Ji'erhang'a was killed by cannon fire.

sentences.zh: 存厚翼其屍不得出，亦戰死。

translations.literal: Cunhou tried to carry off his body but could not get out and also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Cunhou tried to recover the body but could not break out and was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 向榮急遣張國樑會救，克之。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong urgently dispatched Zhang Guoliang to join the rescue, and it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong urgently sent Zhang Guoliang to the rescue, and the position was retaken.

sentences.zh: 秀成以揚州孤懸江北，留守不便，遂棄去，竄回金陵。

translations.literal: Xiucheng, finding Yangzhou isolated north of the river and inconvenient to hold, then abandoned it and fled back to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng found Yangzhou isolated north of the river and hard to hold, so he abandoned it and fled back to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 當是時，向榮、張國樑負眾望，稱江南勁旅。

translations.literal: At that time Xiang Rong and Zhang Guoliang bore the public's hopes and were called the strongest troops of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong and Zhang Guoliang then bore the empire's hopes as the strongest force in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 然頻年征戰，餽餉乖時，士卒常忍饑赴敵，頗缺望，又分兵四出，所部兵力過單。

translations.literal: Yet after years of campaigning, supplies arrived at the wrong times; soldiers often endured hunger to face the enemy and were quite discontent; they also divided forces on four sides, so the troops under command were too thin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after years of war, pay and supplies arrived late; soldiers often fought hungry and grew resentful, and with forces divided on four fronts their numbers were spread too thin.

sentences.zh: 楊秀清知可乘，請於秀全，定夾攻大營之策。

translations.literal: Yang Xiuqing knew he could exploit this, requested Xiucheng, and set a plan for pincer attack on the grand camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiuqing saw the opening, asked Xiucheng, and planned a coordinated assault on the grand camp.

sentences.zh: 五月，密約吳如孝率鎮江寇自東而西，拊大軍之背；

translations.literal: In the fifth month he secretly arranged Wu Ruxiao to lead Zhenjiang rebels from east to west and strike the great army's rear;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he secretly arranged for Wu Ruxiao to lead Zhenjiang rebels from east to west and strike the imperial army in the rear;

sentences.zh: 金陵寇自西而東與相應，更命溧水、金柱關諸寇旁出橫截。

translations.literal: Jinling rebels from west to east would respond, and he further ordered rebels at Lishui, Jinzhuguan, and elsewhere to sally on the flanks and cut them off.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing rebels would strike from west to east in concert, while bands from Lishui, Jinzhuguan, and elsewhere would cut across the imperial line.

sentences.zh: 秀清自率勁旅出廣濟門，先遣賴漢英率紫荊山諸黨攻七橋甕以挑之。

translations.literal: Xiuqing himself led elite troops out the Guangji Gate, first dispatching Lai Hanying with Zijing Mountain bands to attack Qiqiaoweng to provoke them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuqing led elite troops out the Guangji Gate and first sent Lai Hanying with the Zijing Mountain bands to probe Qiqiaoweng.

sentences.zh: 向榮、張國樑狃常勝，併力截殺，漢英忽少卻，向榮益策大軍赴敵。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong and Zhang Guoliang, accustomed to victory, combined strength to intercept and slaughter; Hanying suddenly fell back slightly, and Xiang Rong drove the great army harder against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong and Zhang Guoliang, used to winning, threw their full strength into the intercept. Hanying feigned a slight retreat, and Xiang Rong pushed the main force harder forward.

sentences.zh: 吳如孝以鎮江黨突薄之，大營空虛，守兵驚散。

translations.literal: Wu Ruxiao with Zhenjiang bands suddenly pressed close; the grand camp was empty and defending troops scattered in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ruxiao struck suddenly with the Zhenjiang force. The grand camp was left thin, and the guards broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 向榮見大營火起，退無所據，軍立潰。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong saw fires rise in the grand camp, with no position to retreat to; the army at once collapsed in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the grand camp ablaze with nowhere to fall back, Xiang Rong's army collapsed at once.

sentences.zh: 寇數路乘之，大軍死傷遍地。

translations.literal: Rebels on several routes pressed them; the great army's dead and wounded lay across the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel columns pressed them from every side, and the field was heaped with imperial dead and wounded.

sentences.zh: 國樑獨以身翼榮出，稍收敗卒退保丹陽。

translations.literal: Guoliang alone shielded Rong with his body and led him out, then gathered scattered defeated troops somewhat and retreated to secure Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang alone shielded Rong and fought his way out, then gathered what he could of the broken force and fell back to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 寇築壘圍之，向榮以病不能進，乃以軍事付國樑，一慟而絕。

translations.literal: Rebels built fortifications to besiege them; Xiang Rong, ill and unable to advance, entrusted military affairs to Guoliang and died in a burst of grief.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels besieged them with fortifications. Too ill to advance, Xiang Rong handed command to Guoliang and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 向榮既死，寇舉酒相慶，頌秀清功。

translations.literal: After Xiang Rong died, rebels raised wine to celebrate and praised Xiuqing's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Rong died, the rebels drank to celebrate and praised Xiuqing's victory.

sentences.zh: 秀全益深居不出，軍事皆決於秀清，文報先白其府，刑賞黜陟皆由之，出諸偽王上。

translations.literal: Xiucheng withdrew ever deeper and did not emerge; all military affairs were decided by Xiuqing; documents were first reported to his residence; punishments, rewards, appointments, and dismissals all passed through him, ranking above the false kings.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng withdrew further from affairs while Xiuqing decided everything—reports went first to his mansion, and rewards, punishments, and appointments all passed through him, placing him above the false kings.

sentences.zh: 如韋昌輝、石達開雖同起草澤，比於裨將。

translations.literal: Men like Wei Changhui and Shi Dakai, though they had risen together from the marshes, were treated like subordinate generals.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Changhui and Shi Dakai, though they had risen with him from nothing, were treated as mere subordinates.

sentences.zh: 大營既潰，南京無圍師。

translations.literal: After the grand camp collapsed, Nanjing had no besieging army.
translations.idiomatic: After the grand camp fell, no imperial army remained to besiege Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 秀清自以為功莫與京，陰謀自立，脅秀全過其宅，令其下呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Xiuqing thought his achievement unmatched in the capital, secretly plotted to set himself up, compelled Xiucheng to visit his residence, and made his followers shout long life.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuqing believed no one in the capital matched his achievement, plotted to seize power, forced Xiucheng to his house, and made followers shout long life to him.

sentences.zh: 秀全不能堪，因召韋昌輝密圖之。

translations.literal: Xiucheng could not bear it and secretly summoned Wei Changhui to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng could not endure it and secretly summoned Wei Changhui to plot his downfall.

sentences.zh: 昌輝自江西敗歸，秀清責其無功，不許入城；

translations.literal: Changhui, returning defeated from Jiangxi, was blamed by Xiuqing for achieving nothing and not permitted to enter the city;
translations.idiomatic: Changhui, returning defeated from Jiangxi, was rebuked by Xiuqing for failure and barred from the city;

sentences.zh: 再請，始許之。

translations.literal: he asked again and was at last permitted entry.
translations.idiomatic: only on a second request was he allowed in.

sentences.zh: 先詣秀全，秀全詭責之，趣赴偽東王府請命，而陰授之計，昌輝戒備以往。

translations.literal: He first went to Xiucheng; Xiucheng falsely rebuked him and urged him to go to the false Eastern King's residence for orders, while secretly giving him a plan; Changhui went on guard.
translations.idiomatic: He went first to Xiucheng, who feigned rebuked him and sent him to the false Eastern King's mansion for orders while secretly giving him a plan. Changhui went armed.

sentences.zh: 既見秀清，語以人呼萬歲事，昌輝佯喜拜賀，秀清留宴。

translations.literal: Once he saw Xiuqing, he spoke of people shouting long life; Changhui feigned joy and bowed in congratulation; Xiuqing kept him for a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Xiuqing he spoke of the cries of long life. Changhui feigned delight and bowed in congratulation, and Xiuqing kept him for a banquet.

sentences.zh: 酒半，昌輝出不意，拔佩刀刺之，洞胸而死。

translations.literal: Halfway through the wine, Changhui unexpectedly drew his sword and stabbed him, piercing his chest and killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Midway through the feast Changhui drew his sword and stabbed him through the chest, killing him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 乃令於眾曰：「東王謀反，吾陰受天王命，誅之。

translations.literal: He then told the assembly: "The Eastern King plotted rebellion; I secretly received the Heavenly King's command to execute him."
translations.idiomatic: He then announced to the crowd, "The Eastern King plotted rebellion. I secretly received the Heavenly King's order to execute him."

sentences.zh: 」因出偽詔，糜其屍咽群賊，令閉城搜偽東王黨殲焉。

translations.literal: He then produced a false edict, minced his corpse to feed the rebel host, ordered the gates closed to search out and exterminate the false Eastern King's faction.
translations.idiomatic: He issued a false edict, had the corpse minced and fed to the rebels, closed the gates, and ordered a search to exterminate the Eastern King's faction.

sentences.zh: 東黨恟懼，日與北黨相鬥殺，東黨多死亡逃匿。

translations.literal: The Eastern faction panicked and daily fought the Northern faction to the death; many of the Eastern faction died or fled into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern faction panicked and fought the Northern faction day after day; many were killed or fled into hiding.

sentences.zh: 秀全妻賴氏曰：「除惡不盡，必留後禍。

translations.literal: Xiucheng's wife Lady Lai said: "If you do not root out evil completely, later trouble is sure to remain."
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng's wife, Lady Lai, said, "If the evil is not rooted out completely, trouble will remain."

sentences.zh: 」因說秀全詭罪昌輝酷殺，予杖，慰謝東黨，召之來觀，可聚殲焉。

translations.literal: She therefore persuaded Xiucheng to falsely blame Changhui for excessive killing, give him a beating, console the Eastern faction, and summon them to watch—so they could be gathered and exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: She persuaded Xiucheng to blame Changhui for excessive killing, have him beaten, console the Eastern faction, and summon them to watch so they could be trapped and slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 秀全用其策，而突以甲圍殺觀者。

translations.literal: Xiucheng used her plan and suddenly surrounded the spectators with armed men and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng followed her plan and suddenly surrounded the spectators with troops and killed them.

sentences.zh: 東黨殆盡，前後死者近三萬人。

translations.literal: The Eastern faction was nearly exterminated; dead before and after approached thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern faction was nearly wiped out; close to thirty thousand died in all.

sentences.zh: 時石達開在湖北洪山，黃玉崑在江西臨江，聞亂趨歸。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Dakai was at Hongshan in Hubei and Huang Yukun at Linjiang in Jiangxi; hearing of the turmoil they hurried back.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai was then at Hongshan in Hubei and Huang Yukun at Linjiang in Jiangxi; hearing of the chaos, both hurried back.

sentences.zh: 達開頗誚讓昌輝，昌輝怒，將併圖之。

translations.literal: Dakai reproached Changhui somewhat; Changhui grew angry and planned to destroy him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai reproached Changhui, who grew angry and plotted to destroy him too.

sentences.zh: 達開縋城走寧國，昌輝悉殺其母妻子女。

translations.literal: Dakai lowered himself by rope from the wall and fled to Ningguo; Changhui killed all his mother, wife, children, and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai lowered himself from the wall by rope and fled to Ningguo. Changhui killed his mother, wife, children, and daughters.

sentences.zh: 秀全責以太過，昌輝負誅秀清功大，不服，率其黨圍攻偽天王府，秀全兵拒敗之。

translations.literal: Xiucheng blamed him for going too far; Changhui, relying on the merit of executing Xiuqing, refused to submit and led his band to besiege the false Heavenly King's palace; Xiucheng's troops repelled and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng blamed him for excess. Changhui, claiming credit for killing Xiuqing, refused to yield and led his followers to besiege the false Heavenly King's palace, but Xiucheng's troops defeated them.

sentences.zh: 昌輝遁，渡江為邏者所獲，縛送金陵磔之，夷其族，傳首寧國。

translations.literal: Changhui fled, was caught crossing the river by patrolmen, bound and sent to Jinling to be dismembered, his clan exterminated, and his head sent to Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: Changhui fled, was seized crossing the river, sent to Nanjing to be dismembered, his clan exterminated, and his head displayed at Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 甘言召達開回，既至，或謂達開兵眾功高，請留之京師，解其兵柄，否則又一楊秀清也。

translations.literal: With sweet words Dakai was summoned back; once he arrived, some said Dakai's troops were numerous and his merit great—he should be kept in the capital and stripped of military command, or else there would be another Yang Xiuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai was summoned back with fair words. Once he arrived, some argued that with his large following and great merit he should be kept in the capital and disarmed, lest another Yang Xiuqing arise.

sentences.zh: 秀全心動，乃命如秀清故事輔朝政。

translations.literal: Xiucheng's heart was moved and he ordered him to assist court affairs as in Xiuqing's former manner.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng wavered and ordered him to assist at court in Xiuqing's former role.

sentences.zh: 達開危懼不自安，其黨張遂謀曰：「王得軍心，何鬱鬱受人制？

translations.literal: Dakai was in peril and ill at ease; his follower Zhang Suimou said: "The King has the army's hearts—why brood under another's control?
translations.idiomatic: Dakai lived in fear. His follower Zhang Suimou said, "You hold the army's loyalty—why submit to another's control?

sentences.zh: 中原不易圖，曷入川作玄德，成鼎足之業？

translations.literal: The central plains are not easy to scheme for—why not enter Sichuan like Xuande and achieve a tripartite enterprise?"
translations.idiomatic: The central plains are hard to win. Why not enter Sichuan like Liu Bei and build a realm of three parts?"

sentences.zh: 」達開從之，乃還走安徽，約陳玉成、李秀成偕行，二人不從，益不能還金陵。

translations.literal: Dakai followed this, then fled back toward Anhui, arranging with Chen Yucheng and Li Xiucheng to go together; the two did not follow, and he could even less return to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai agreed, fled back toward Anhui, and asked Chen Yucheng and Li Xiucheng to go with him. They refused, and he could not return to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 於是始起事諸悍黨略盡，乃以偽春官正丞相蒙得恩為正掌率，調度軍事；

translations.literal: By then the fierce partisans who had first risen were nearly gone; the false Spring Office chief chancellor Meng De'en was made chief controller to regulate military affairs;
translations.idiomatic: By then the fiercest of the founding rebels were nearly gone. The false Spring Office chief chancellor Meng De'en was made chief controller of military affairs;

sentences.zh: 偽成天豫陳玉成為右正掌率，偽合天侯李秀成為副掌率，兵事專屬秀成、玉成，均聽蒙得恩節制；

translations.literal: the false Chengtianyu Chen Yucheng was made right chief controller, the false Hetianhou Li Xiucheng vice controller; military affairs belonged chiefly to Xiucheng and Yucheng, both under Meng De'en's regulation;
translations.idiomatic: the false Chengtianyu Chen Yucheng became right chief controller and the false Hetianhou Li Xiucheng vice controller. Military affairs fell chiefly to Xiucheng and Yucheng under Meng De'en;

sentences.zh: 而內政則秀全兄弟偽安王洪仁發、偽福王洪仁達操之。

translations.literal: while internal administration was handled by Xiucheng's brothers the false Prince of An Hong Renfa and the false Prince of Fu Hong Renda.
translations.idiomatic: internal affairs passed to Xiucheng's brothers, the false Prince of An Hong Renfa and the false Prince of Fu Hong Renda.

sentences.zh: 時我軍自克復廬州，寇黨竄踞三河，分營金牛，一路壁壘相望，屢抗我師。

translations.literal: At that time, after our army recovered Luzhou, rebel bands fled to hold Sanhe, dividing camps at Jinniu with fortifications in sight of one another, repeatedly resisting our army.
translations.idiomatic: After imperial forces retook Luzhou, rebel remnants held Sanhe and Jinniu in linked camps, resisting again and again.

sentences.zh: 八月，和春督軍乘夜踰壕火其藥局，梯城而入，寇倉皇奪門出，追斃之巢湖。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, He Chun supervised the army crossing the moat by night to set fire to their powder store, scaling the wall to enter; rebels fled in panic out the gates and were pursued and killed at Chaohu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month He Chun led troops over the moat by night, burned the powder magazine, and scaled the wall. The rebels fled in panic and were pursued and killed at Chaohu.

sentences.zh: 生擒偽指揮張大有、偽將軍秦標盛等十一名，殲賊五千餘。

translations.literal: Captured alive eleven including the false commander Zhang Dayou and false general Qin Biaosheng; over five thousand bandits were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven prisoners including the false commander Zhang Dayou and false general Qin Biaosheng were taken, and more than five thousand rebels were killed.

sentences.zh: 江南軍克復高淳。

translations.literal: Jiangnan forces recovered Gaochun.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan forces retook Gaochun.

sentences.zh: 九月，擊敗句容、溧水，二城近金陵為犄角。

translations.literal: In the ninth month they defeated Jurong and Lishui; the two cities were horns near Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they defeated the rebels at Jurong and Lishui, the two cities that flanked Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 金陵聞其敗，氣阻，大營始安。

translations.literal: Jinling, hearing of their defeat, was discouraged in spirit, and the grand camp was at last secure.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the defeat, Nanjing lost heart, and the grand camp was at last secure.

sentences.zh: 巢縣者，寇之老巢也，其水陸連營無數，所掠糧餉悉輸金陵。

translations.literal: Chaoxian was the rebels' old nest; their land and naval linked camps were countless; grain and supplies seized were all sent to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoxian was the rebels' old stronghold, with countless linked land and naval camps and all plundered grain sent to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 巡撫福濟與編修李鴻章督軍攻復之。

translations.literal: Governor Fuji and Compiler Li Hongzhang supervised the army in attacking and recovering it.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Fuki and Compiler Li Hongzhang led the attack that retook it.

sentences.zh: 廬州所屬州邑以次肅清。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties under Luzhou were cleared in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The districts around Luzhou were cleared one by one.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，湖南援軍吳坤修克安義、靖安，與民團會攻奉新，寇棄城遁。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, Hunan relief army Wu Kunxiu took Anyi and Jing'an and with militia jointly attacked Fengxin; rebels abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year Hunan relief commander Wu Kunxiu retook Anyi and Jing'an and, with local militia, attacked Fengxin until the rebels abandoned the city.

sentences.zh: 武昌之陷也，曾國藩遣彭玉麟援鄂；

translations.literal: When Wuchang fell, Zeng Guofan had dispatched Peng Yulin to aid E Province;
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchang fell, Zeng Guofan had sent Peng Yulin to aid Hubei;

sentences.zh: 及石達開躪江西，連陷瑞、臨、袁、吉、建、撫諸郡，又檄玉麟赴援。

translations.literal: when Shi Dakai trampled Jiangxi and in succession seized the prefectures Rui, Lin, Yuan, Ji, Jian, and Fu, he again ordered Yulin to go to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: when Shi Dakai overran Jiangxi and seized Ruizhou, Linjiang, Yuanzhou, Ji'an, Jianchang, and Fuzhou in turn, he ordered Yulin to Jiangxi as well.

sentences.zh: 尋國藩以父喪歸，上命彭玉麟協同載福調度軍事。

translations.literal: Soon Guofan returned on account of his father's death; the Emperor ordered Peng Yulin to assist Zaifu in regulating military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guofan went home to mourn his father, and the emperor ordered Peng Yulin to assist Yang Zaifu in directing operations.

sentences.zh: 九江為江西重鎮，皖、楚咽喉，寇力爭天險，匯踞九江，而以對岸黃梅之小池口為外蔽，進以犯湖北，退以擾贛、皖，游行掉臂，防不勝防。

translations.literal: Jiujiang was a key town of Jiangxi, the throat of Anhui and Huguang; rebels strove for this heavenly pass, massing at Jiujiang while using Xiaochikou in Huangmei on the opposite bank as an outer screen—advancing to invade Hubei, retreating to harass Jiangxi and Anhui, roaming at will, impossible to defend against on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Jiujiang was Jiangxi's strategic key and the gateway between Anhui and Huguang. The rebels held the natural strongpoint at Jiujiang and used Xiaochikou across the river in Huangmei as an outer shield—advancing into Hubei, retreating to harass Jiangxi and Anhui, raiding wherever they chose.

sentences.zh: 大軍自達九江、宿松，諸酋聚眾數十萬，城於小池口，以遏官軍，圖上竄。

translations.literal: The great army reached Jiujiang and Susong; rebel chiefs gathered several hundred thousand followers, fortified at Xiaochikou to block government troops and plot to flee upriver.
translations.idiomatic: The main force reached Jiujiang and Susong. Rebel chiefs massed hundreds of thousands at Xiaochikou to block imperial troops and plan a breakout upriver.

sentences.zh: 是月寇分三路入犯，距黃梅縣城數十里，知縣單瀚元請空城誘入，都興阿從其計，伏軍四起殲之。

translations.literal: That month rebels invaded in three columns, coming within several tens of li of Huangmei county seat; Magistrate Shan Hanyuan asked to empty the city to lure them in, and Du Xing'a followed his plan; ambush troops rose on four sides and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: That month rebels advanced in three columns toward Huangmei. Magistrate Shan Hanyuan proposed emptying the city as bait; Du Xing'a agreed, and ambushers annihilated them on four sides.

sentences.zh: 寇棄城走，截斬其偽擣天侯陳某，偽天王婿鍾某、曾某三名。

translations.literal: Rebels abandoned the city and fled; they intercepted and beheaded the false Pounding-Heaven Marquis Chen, and three including the false Heavenly King's son-in-law Zhong and Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled the city. Imperial forces cut down the false Pounding-Heaven Marquis Chen and three others, including the false Heavenly King's sons-in-law Zhong and Zeng.

sentences.zh: 小池口寇聞之喪膽，乃築堅城為固守計；

translations.literal: Xiaochikou rebels, hearing this, lost courage and then built a strong city as a plan to hold firm;
translations.idiomatic: The Xiaochikou garrison lost heart and fortified the town for a last stand;

sentences.zh: 復於段窯、楓樹坳、獨山鎮諸處依山砌石，為壘數十，引水浚壕，阻我軍東下。

translations.literal: they also built stone on mountains at Duanyao, Fengshu'ao, Dushan Town and other places into several tens of fortifications, drew water to dig moats, and blocked our army's advance east.
translations.idiomatic: They also built dozens of stone forts at Duanyao, Fengshu'ao, and Dushan, dug moats, and blocked the eastern advance.

sentences.zh: 都興阿遣鮑超、多隆阿、王國才等分攻，悉平其壘。

translations.literal: Du Xing'a dispatched Bao Chao, Dolonga, Wang Guocai and others to attack on separate routes and leveled all their fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xing'a sent Bao Chao, Dolonga, Wang Guocai, and others to attack from several directions and leveled the forts.

sentences.zh: 四月，玉成犯湖北，眾號十萬。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Yucheng invaded Hubei; his force claimed one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Chen Yucheng invaded Hubei with a force said to number one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 李續賓壁小池，鮑超移屯黃梅，遏其衝，分途迎擊，大破之，軍威始振。

translations.literal: Li Xubing fortified at Xiaochi; Bao Chao shifted encampment to Huangmei to block their thrust, met and struck on separate routes, greatly defeated them, and military prestige began to revive.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xubing held Xiaochi while Bao Chao moved to Huangmei to block the thrust. They met the rebels on separate routes, routed them, and imperial morale revived.

sentences.zh: 五月，李續賓攻九江，掘長壕困寇，設伏敗之馬宿嶺、茶嶺諸處。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Li Xubing attacked Jiujiang, dug a long moat to trap rebels, and set ambushes to defeat them at Masu Ridge, Chaling, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Li Xubing besieged Jiujiang with a long trench, ambushed rebels at Masu Ridge and Chaling, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 越旬餘，安慶寇來援，合城寇三萬，蜿蜒數里。

translations.literal: After more than ten days, Anqing rebels came to the relief; together with city rebels they numbered thirty thousand, winding for several li.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days Anqing reinforcements arrived; with the city garrison they numbered thirty thousand and stretched for miles.

sentences.zh: 我軍水陸會剿，連戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Our army suppressed them jointly by land and water; successive battles were all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Land and naval forces fought together and won every engagement.

sentences.zh: 閏五月，玉成復犯湖北，大小二十五戰，亡七千有餘。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month, Yucheng again invaded Hubei; in twenty-five battles large and small, over seven thousand were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month Yucheng invaded Hubei again. In twenty-five engagements more than seven thousand rebels were killed.

sentences.zh: 時蘄、黃一路寇猖甚，蘄州諸軍並挫，賴舒保力戰，水師左光培扼巴河，得免上竄。

translations.literal: At that time rebels on the Qi and Huang route were very rampant; Qizhou armies were all defeated; only with Shu Bao fighting hard and naval officer Zuo Guangpei blocking the Ba River were they prevented from fleeing upriver.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels along the Qizhou-Huangzhou line were rampant and Qizhou forces were beaten back. Only Shu Bao's hard fighting and Zuo Guangpei's block at the Ba River kept them from breaking upriver.

sentences.zh: 官文令唐訓方增軍守要，約都興阿力扼黃梅，嚴防後路。

translations.literal: Guan Wen ordered Tang Xunfang to increase troops to guard key points and arranged with Du Xing'a to hold Huangmei firmly and strictly guard the rear route.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen reinforced the garrisons under Tang Xunfang and ordered Du Xing'a to hold Huangmei and guard the rear.

sentences.zh: 以是黃州上下烽火不絕，而武漢帖然無恙。

translations.literal: Because of this beacon fires above and below Huangzhou never ceased, yet Wuhan remained calm and unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Beacon fires blazed up and down the Huangzhou stretch, yet Wuhan itself stayed secure.

sentences.zh: 六月，續賓浚長壕合水師力攻九江，宿松、太湖群寇糾合皖省饑民十餘萬乘虛圖武漢，且解九江之圍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Xubing deepened the long moat and with the naval force pressed the attack on Jiujiang; Susong and Taihu bandits rallied over one hundred thousand starving people from Anhui to exploit the opening and plot against Wuhan while relieving the siege of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Xubing deepened the siege trenches and attacked Jiujiang with the fleet. Rebels in Susong and Taihu rallied more than one hundred thousand Anhui refugees to threaten Wuhan and lift the Jiujiang siege.

sentences.zh: 寇據黃梅、廣濟、蘄州、蘄水，分四路進，大小五十餘戰，死萬餘而勢不稍衰。

translations.literal: Rebels held Huangmei, Guangji, Qizhou, and Qishui and advanced in four columns; in over fifty battles more than ten thousand were killed yet their momentum did not slacken slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held Huangmei, Guangji, Qizhou, and Qishui and advanced in four columns. After more than fifty battles and ten thousand dead, their momentum barely slackened.

sentences.zh: 初，小池口之捷也，潯陽、湖口立望廓清；

translations.literal: Earlier, with the victory at Xiaochikou, Xunyang and Hukou at once looked to be cleared;
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Xiaochikou, Xunyang and Hukou seemed about to be cleared;

sentences.zh: 及皖寇上援九江，陸軍梗阻，而上游水師又難驟撤，楚軍馬隊不及萬，寇所竄伏，崎嶇泥淖，馬隊幾無可施。

translations.literal: but when Anhui rebels came upriver to aid Jiujiang, the land army was blocked, and the upstream naval force could not be withdrawn quickly; Chu Army cavalry numbered less than ten thousand, and where rebels hid was rugged mire—cavalry could hardly be used.
translations.idiomatic: but Anhui reinforcements for Jiujiang blocked the land columns, the upstream fleet could not be pulled back quickly, and with fewer than ten thousand cavalry in broken, muddy country, horses were nearly useless.

sentences.zh: 惟將士一心，屹然不為所撼。

translations.literal: Only officers and soldiers were of one mind and stood firm without being shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Only the unity of officers and men kept the army from buckling.

sentences.zh: 楊載福、李續賓督水陸上援，多隆阿、鮑超攻賊童司牌，敗之十里鋪。

translations.literal: Yang Zaifu and Li Xubing supervised land and naval forces in relief upriver; Dolonga and Bao Chao attacked the rebel position at Tongsipai and defeated them at Shilipu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaifu and Li Xubing led the combined relief force upriver while Dolonga and Bao Chao attacked Tongsipai and routed the rebels at Shilipu.

sentences.zh: 寇造浮橋河中，東通北湖，西達武穴。

translations.literal: Rebels built a floating bridge in the river, east connecting to North Lake and west reaching Wuxue.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels bridged the river, linking North Lake in the east with Wuxue in the west.

sentences.zh: 續賓渡江平南岸寇屯，水師復焚寇艇，燬浮橋，寇不得逞。

translations.literal: Xubing crossed the river and pacified south-bank rebel encampments; the naval force again burned rebel boats and destroyed the floating bridge, and rebels could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Xubing crossed the river and cleared the south-bank camps. The fleet burned rebel boats and destroyed the bridge, and the rebels were stopped.

sentences.zh: 七月，黃梅寇以弱兵守壘，而以強悍驍勇者遍伏村落。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Huangmei rebels used weak troops to hold fortifications while placing fierce and valiant fighters in ambush throughout villages.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Huangmei rebels manned the forts lightly while hiding their best fighters in the villages.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿偵知，約鮑超直衝村落，斃五千餘，而其在蘄、黃者仍不下數萬。

translations.literal: Dolonga learned by reconnaissance and arranged with Bao Chao to charge straight into the villages, killing over five thousand; yet those in Qi and Huang still numbered not less than tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Dolonga learned this and sent Bao Chao straight into the villages, killing more than five thousand, but tens of thousands still held the Qi-Huang line.

sentences.zh: 官文督軍五路進攻，杜其上竄，擒渠掃穴，蘄、黃路通。

translations.literal: Guan Wen supervised the army in five routes of attack to block their flight upriver, captured chiefs and swept nests, and the Qi-Huang route was opened.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen attacked on five routes, cut off their retreat upriver, captured rebel chiefs, and reopened the Qi-Huang corridor.

sentences.zh: 尋又大破皖寇於黃岡、蘄水界，克復瑞州，我軍直抵小池口。

translations.literal: Soon they again greatly defeated Anhui rebels on the Huanggang-Qishui border, recovered Ruizhou, and our army pressed straight to Xiaochikou.
translations.idiomatic: They soon routed Anhui rebels on the Huanggang-Qishui border, retook Ruizhou, and pressed on to Xiaochikou.

sentences.zh: 小池口與潯城隔江對峙，為江、皖入楚衝途。

translations.literal: Xiaochikou faced Xuncheng across the river; it was the thoroughfare for Jiang and Anhui entering Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochikou faced Xuncheng across the river—the gateway from Jiangxi and Anhui into Hubei.

sentences.zh: 寇壘石為城，深溝高壘。

translations.literal: Rebels piled stone into a city with deep moats and high ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had piled stone into walls with deep moats and high ramparts.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼以寇燄正衰，約諸軍先拔小池口，親督唐訓方、李續宜等由蘄水達黃梅坡下，建碉以塞宿松上竄之路。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi, seeing rebel flames were declining, arranged with the armies first to take Xiaochikou; he personally supervised Tang Xunfang, Li Xuyi, and others from Qishui to reach below Huangmei slope and built blockhouses to block the Susong upriver route.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing rebel strength fade, Hu Linyi ordered the armies to take Xiaochikou first. He led Tang Xunfang and Li Xuyi from Qishui to Huangmei, building blockhouses to block escape toward Susong.

sentences.zh: 偵知城內爨具已毀於砲，炊煙斷熄，乃令水陸環攻，射火入城。

translations.literal: Scouts learned that cooking vessels inside the city had been destroyed by cannon fire and cooking smoke had ceased; he then ordered land and naval encirclement and shot fire into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts reported cooking pots shattered by shellfire and no smoke from the kitchens. Hu ordered a combined assault and fired into the city.

sentences.zh: 我軍乘亂而登，寇盡殄滅。

translations.literal: Our army took advantage of the chaos to ascend; rebels were entirely exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops stormed the walls in the chaos and wiped out the garrison.

sentences.zh: 全楚始一律肅清。

translations.literal: All of Chu was at last uniformly cleared and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei was at last cleared.

sentences.zh: 江西軍隨復東鄉。

translations.literal: Jiangxi forces then recovered Dongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi forces then retook Dongxiang.

sentences.zh: 東鄉隸撫州，寇踞之以為撫州保障，復陷萬年諸縣。

translations.literal: Dongxiang was under Fuzhou; rebels held it as a shield for Fuzhou and again seized Wannian and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Dongxiang belonged to Fuzhou. The rebels used it to shield Fuzhou and seized Wannian and other counties.

sentences.zh: 八月，將軍福興冒雨進攻，縱火平塘，絕寇竄路。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, General Fuxing advanced the attack through rain, set fires at Pingtang, and cut off the rebel escape route.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month General Fuxing attacked through the rain, burned Pingtang, and cut the rebel line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 平塘者，附城往撫州之衝也。

translations.literal: Pingtang was the pass on the road from the city toward Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pingtang guarded the road from the city to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 寇果棄城而遁。

translations.literal: Rebels indeed abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 初，寇踞石鐘山，守湖口兩岸，致水師隔絕。

translations.literal: Earlier, rebels held Shizhong Mountain and guarded both banks of Hukou, causing the naval force to be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the rebels had held Shizhong Mountain and both banks of Hukou, cutting the fleet off.

sentences.zh: 九月，克湖口，連破梅家洲，燔石鐘山寇巢，殪萬餘。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Hukou was taken; Meijiazhou was taken in succession; the Shizhong Mountain rebel nest was burned and over ten thousand were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Hukou fell, Meijiazhou followed, the Shizhong Mountain stronghold was burned, and more than ten thousand rebels were killed.

sentences.zh: 內湖外江至今三載始合。

translations.literal: Inner lake and outer river were at last united after three years.
translations.idiomatic: After three years the lake fleet and river fleet were reunited.

sentences.zh: 載福以取九江當先援彭澤，彭澤南有小孤山，寇築城其上以守彭澤，為九江聲援。

translations.literal: Zaifu held that taking Jiujiang required first aiding Pengze; south of Pengze was Little Gushan Mountain, where rebels built a city on the heights to guard Pengze as support for Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zaifu argued that Jiujiang required taking Pengze first. South of Pengze the rebels had fortified Little Gushan to cover Pengze and support Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 載福會軍攻克縣城，盡掃小孤山寇巢。

translations.literal: Zaifu joined forces, took the county seat, and swept clean the rebel nest on Little Gushan.
translations.idiomatic: Zaifu joined the assault, took the county seat, and cleared Little Gushan.

sentences.zh: 下游巨險悉夷。

translations.literal: Great downstream passes were all leveled.
translations.idiomatic: The great downstream strongpoints were all cleared.

sentences.zh: 大軍回向九江。

translations.literal: The great army turned back toward Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: The main force turned back on Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，長祐會攻臨江府，拔之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Changyou joined in attacking Linjiang Prefecture and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Changyou joined the assault on Linjiang and took it.

sentences.zh: 寇竄湖北興國州，復為續賓所殲。

translations.literal: Rebels fled to Xingguo Prefecture in Hubei and were again destroyed by Xubing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Xingguo in Hubei and were destroyed again by Xubing.

sentences.zh: 餘眾僅二百，皆鳧水而逸。

translations.literal: The remainder numbered only two hundred; all escaped by swimming.
translations.idiomatic: Only about two hundred survived, swimming away to escape.

sentences.zh: 寇之自楚北敗竄回皖也，糾合河南捻匪，撲廬州及巢縣、柘皋。

translations.literal: When rebels fled north in defeat from Chu back to Anhui, they colluded with Henan Nian bandits and struck Luzhou and Chaoxian and Zhegao.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated rebels fleeing north from Hubei into Anhui joined Henan Nian bandits and struck Luzhou, Chaoxian, and Zhegao.

sentences.zh: 我軍進平柘皋寇壘，火巢湖派河兩子鋪寇船，寇蹤遂絕。

translations.literal: Our army advanced to pacify Zhegao rebel fortifications, burned rebel boats at the two forts on the Chaohu branch river, and rebel tracks were then cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial forces cleared the Zhegao forts, burned rebel boats on the Chaohu branch, and cut off their line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 先是江南水師提督李德麟率紅單船入皖，寇遏之繁昌縣峽口，不得上，七閱月矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiangnan naval commander-in-chief Li Delin had led red-barbarian boats into Anhui; rebels blocked them at the Fanchang county gorge and they could not ascend—for seven months.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Naval Commander-in-Chief Li Delin had brought foreign gunboats into Anhui, but rebels blocked the Fanchang gorge for seven months.

sentences.zh: 載福督師東下，焚奪陳玉成所派戰船略盡。

translations.literal: Zaifu supervised the army eastward and burned and seized nearly all warships Chen Yucheng had dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Zaifu led the fleet east and burned or captured nearly all the warships Chen Yucheng had sent.

sentences.zh: 連日焚華陽鎮，復望江、東流，疾趨安慶，破樅陽大通鎮，進克銅陵，馳入峽內，與紅單船合。

translations.literal: For successive days they burned Huayang Town, recovered Wangjiang and Dongliu, hurried toward Anqing, broke Zongyang Datong Town, advanced to take Tongling, and dashed into the gorge to join the red-barbarian boats.
translations.idiomatic: They burned Huayang, retook Wangjiang and Dongliu, rushed on Anqing, broke Datong at Zongyang, took Tongling, and entered the gorge to join the gunboats.

sentences.zh: 寇望風瓦解，逼泥汊偽城，李成謀擲火焚之，斬戮過當。

translations.literal: Rebels collapsed at the wind; pressing the false city at Nizhan, Li Chengmo threw fire to burn it and killed and maimed beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke and fled. Pressing the false city at Nizhan, Li Chengmo burned it and slaughtered without mercy.

sentences.zh: 時江西寇糾黨二萬餘，由浮梁、建德、都昌、鄱陽竄湖口，而宿松、太湖寇憤九江之敗，糾黨五六萬，麇集於楓香驛、仙田鋪等處，聲勢相依。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangxi rebels rallied over twenty thousand followers, fleeing through Fuliang, Jiande, Duchang, and Poyang toward Hukou, while Susong and Taihu rebels, enraged at the defeat at Jiujiang, rallied fifty or sixty thousand at Fengxiang Post, Xiantian Shop, and other places in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi rebels mustered more than twenty thousand and fled toward Hukou through Fuliang, Jiande, Duchang, and Poyang, while Susong and Taihu rebels, furious over Jiujiang, massed fifty or sixty thousand at Fengxiang Post and Xiantian Shop.

sentences.zh: 官文檄唐訓方壁陳園，固蘄州門戶。

translations.literal: Guan Wen ordered Tang Xunfang to fortify at Chenyuan and secure the gateway of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen ordered Tang Xunfang to hold Chenyuan and guard the Qizhou gateway.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿、鮑超等迎剿太湖，李續宜會水師分三路直擣，斃寇二萬餘，寇勢大挫。

translations.literal: Dolonga, Bao Chao, and others met and suppressed Taihu; Li Xuyi joined the naval force in three columns to strike straight, killing over twenty thousand rebels, and rebel momentum suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Dolonga and Bao Chao met the Taihu rebels while Li Xuyi and the fleet struck in three columns, killing more than twenty thousand and breaking their momentum.

sentences.zh: 江南大營之退駐丹陽也，秀成踞句容，屢出窺伺。

translations.literal: When the Jiangnan Grand Camp withdrew to Danyang, Xiucheng held Jurong and repeatedly sallied to spy and probe.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiangnan Grand Camp fell back to Danyang, Xiucheng held Jurong and probed imperial lines again and again.

sentences.zh: 正月，國樑獨率精卒間道抵城下，毀其外壘，斃寇千數百名，寇不敢復出。

translations.literal: In the first month, Guoliang alone led elite troops by a hidden route to the foot of the city, destroyed their outer fortifications, killed several thousand rebels, and rebels dared not sally again.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month Guoliang led elite troops by a hidden path to the walls, destroyed the outer works, killed several thousand rebels, and the garrison dared not sally again.

sentences.zh: 二月，金陵、安慶寇偵溧水勢蹙，糾眾至鄔山，築壘為援。

translations.literal: In the second month, Jinling and Anqing rebels, seeing Lishui hard pressed, rallied masses to Wushan and built fortifications as relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Nanjing and Anqing rebels, seeing Lishui hard pressed, gathered at Wushan and built relief fortifications.

sentences.zh: 和春乘寇營未定，邀而敗之。

translations.literal: He Chun, while rebel camps were not yet settled, intercepted and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun struck while the rebel camps were still unsettled and routed them.

sentences.zh: 寇渡河復結四壘，江南軍三路敗其眾，合兵攻溧水城，前後平寇壘二十六座，殲三千，斃偽靠天侯以下十餘名。

translations.literal: Rebels crossed the river and again built four fortifications; Jiangnan forces on three routes defeated their masses; combined armies attacked Lishui city; before and after they leveled twenty-six rebel fortifications, destroyed three thousand, and killed over ten including the false Leaning-on-Heaven Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels crossed the river and built four more forts. Jiangnan forces beat them on three fronts, stormed Lishui, leveled twenty-six forts, killed three thousand, and slew more than ten officers including the false Leaning-on-Heaven Marquis.

sentences.zh: 移營已及一年，戰功此為最烈。

translations.literal: The camp had been shifted for over a year; in military achievement this was the fiercest.
translations.idiomatic: The camp had moved for more than a year; this was its fiercest victory.
