translations.literal: Earlier, Tongling and Qingyang rebels often invaded the junction of Nanling and Jing counties; our army held Yunling and Suling and set ambushes at Chaoshan Pass and Sanlidian; Regiment Commander Fang Guohuai made a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: Tongling and Qingyang rebels had raided the Nanling-Jing border until imperial forces held Yunling and Suling, ambushed Chaoshan and Sanlidian, and Fang Guohuai struck by surprise.

sentences.zh: 寇屢犯三里甸，陷國淮壘，復竄越雲嶺，陷觀嶺防營。

translations.literal: Rebels repeatedly invaded Sanlidian, took Guohuai's fortification, again fled over Yunling, and seized Guanling garrison camp.
translations.idiomatic: They took Sanlidian and Guohuai's fort, crossed Yunling again, and seized Guanling.

sentences.zh: 天受調金友堵清弋江，寇北走南陵，陳大富擊之，寇復退入涇境。

translations.literal: Tianshou transferred Jin You to block the Qingyi River; rebels fled north to Nanling; Chen Dafu struck them; rebels again retreated into Jing territory.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshou sent Jin You to block the Qingyi. Rebels fled toward Nanling, were hit by Chen Dafu, and withdrew into Jing.

sentences.zh: 自玉成回援安慶後，秀成獨屯浦口，寇勢已孤。

translations.literal: After Yucheng returned to relieve Anqing, Xiucheng alone encamped at Pukou; rebel momentum was already isolated.
translations.idiomatic: After Yucheng went back to Anqing, Xiucheng alone held Pukou and rebel strength was increasingly isolated.

sentences.zh: 時金陵困急，援兵皆不至。

translations.literal: At that time Jinling was in urgent distress and relief troops all did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing was desperate and no relief came.

sentences.zh: 秀成以玉成兵最強，請加封王號寄閫外，秀全乃封玉成英王，賜八方黃金印，便宜行事。

translations.literal: Xiucheng, because Yucheng's troops were strongest, asked to be enfeoffed as king with power beyond the capital; Xiucheng then enfeoffed Yucheng as Prince Ying, bestowed eight-sided gold seals, and allowed discretionary action.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng asked that Yucheng be made a king with independent command. Xiucheng made him Prince Ying with gold seals and full discretion.

sentences.zh: 然玉成雖專閫寄，而威信遠不如秀成，無遵調者。

translations.literal: Yet though Yucheng held sole military commission, his authority and prestige were far less than Xiucheng's; none obeyed his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yucheng's authority never matched Xiucheng's, and few obeyed his orders.

sentences.zh: 李世忠因致書秀成曰：「君智謀勇功，何事不如玉成？

translations.literal: Li Shizhong therefore wrote to Xiucheng saying: "Your wisdom, stratagem, courage, and achievement—what do you not surpass Yucheng in?
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhong wrote to Xiucheng: "In wisdom, courage, and achievement, what do you lack that Yucheng has?

sentences.zh: 今玉成已王，而君尚為將，秀全之憒憒可知矣。

translations.literal: Now Yucheng is already a king while you remain a general—the muddleheadedness of Xiucheng is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng is a king and you are still a general. Xiucheng's folly is plain.

sentences.zh: 吾始反正，清帝優禮有加。

translations.literal: I first returned to allegiance and the Qing Emperor treated me with added favor.
translations.idiomatic: I defected first, and the Qing emperor treated me generously.

sentences.zh: 以君雄才，胡為鬱鬱久居人下？

translations.literal: With your heroic talent, why brood long in subjection to another?
translations.idiomatic: With your talent, why stay beneath others so long?

sentences.zh: 盍從我遊乎！

translations.literal: Why not follow me!
translations.idiomatic: Come join me!

sentences.zh: 」時偽兵部尚書莫仕葵以勘軍在秀成營，書落其手，閱之大驚，以示秀成。

translations.literal: " At that time the false Minister of War Mo Shikui was inspecting troops in Xiucheng's camp; the letter fell into his hands; reading it he was greatly alarmed and showed Xiucheng.
translations.idiomatic: " The false Minister of War Mo Shikui, inspecting troops in Xiucheng's camp, seized the letter and showed it to him in alarm.

sentences.zh: 秀成曰：「臣不事二君，猶女不更二夫。

translations.literal: Xiucheng said: "A subject does not serve two lords, as a woman does not take two husbands.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng said, "I serve one master only, as a woman has one husband.

sentences.zh: 昭壽自為不義，乃欲陷人耶？

translations.literal: Zhaoshou himself acted unjustly—does he wish to entrap others?
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoshou acted unjustly. Does he think to trap me?

sentences.zh: 」仕葵曰：「吾知公久矣。

translations.literal: " Shikui said: "I have known you long."
translations.idiomatic: " Mo Shikui said, "I have known your loyalty for years.

sentences.zh: 」乃代奏之，秀全命封江阻秀成兵，並遣其母、妻出居北岸，止其南渡。

translations.literal: He then memorialized on his behalf; Xiucheng ordered the river sealed to block Xiucheng's troops and also sent his mother and wife to live on the north bank, stopping his southward crossing.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for Xiucheng, but Hong Xiuquan sealed the river, moved Xiucheng's mother and wife to the north bank, and barred his crossing south.

sentences.zh: 仕葵曰：「如此，則大事去矣！

translations.literal: Shikui said: "If it is thus, the great enterprise is lost!
translations.idiomatic: Mo Shikui said, "Then the cause is lost!

sentences.zh: 」乃偕蒙得恩、林紹璋、李春發入偽宮切諫曰：「昭壽為敵行間，王奈何墮其計，自壞長城？

translations.literal: " He then with Meng De'en, Lin Shaozhang, and Li Chunfa entered the false palace and urgently remonstrated: "Zhaoshou acts as the enemy's agent—why does the King fall into his plot and destroy his own Great Wall?
translations.idiomatic: " He entered the palace with Meng De'en, Lin Shaozhang, and Li Chunfa and pleaded: "Zhaoshou is the enemy's agent. Why destroy your own Great Wall?

sentences.zh: 京師一線之路，賴秀成障之。

translations.literal: The capital's single-thread route depends on Xiucheng to screen it.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's one lifeline depends on Xiucheng.

sentences.zh: 玉成總軍數月，不能調一軍，其效可睹矣。

translations.literal: Yucheng has commanded armies for months and cannot move one army—the effect is visible.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng has commanded for months and cannot move one army—that proves the point.

sentences.zh: 今宜優詔褒勉，以安其心。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to issue a gracious edict of praise and encouragement to settle his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Issue a gracious edict to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 臣等願以百口保之。

translations.literal: We your subjects are willing to guarantee it with our hundred mouths.
translations.idiomatic: We stake our lives on his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」秀全悟，召秀成入，慰之曰：「如卿忠義，而誤信謠傳，朕之過也。

translations.literal: " Xiucheng understood, summoned Xiucheng in, and consoled him saying: "Such loyalty as yours, yet believing rumors in error—is Our fault.
translations.idiomatic: " Hong Xiuquan relented, summoned Xiucheng, and said, "Your loyalty is clear. Believing rumors was my fault.

sentences.zh: 卿宜釋懷，勠力王室！

translations.literal: You should release your heart and strive for the royal house!
translations.idiomatic: Set your heart at ease and serve the cause!

sentences.zh: 」即進封偽爵為忠王榮千歲。

translations.literal: " He then advanced his false title to Loyal King Rong Thousand Years.
translations.idiomatic: " He made Xiucheng Loyal King, Rong Thousand Years.

sentences.zh: 寇自楊、韋搆殺，秀全以其兄弟仁發等主持偽政，偽幼西王蕭有和，蕭朝貴子也，秀全尤倚任之，而以一偽將畜秀成，不與聞大計。

translations.literal: Since the Yang and Wei mutual slaughter, Xiucheng had his brothers Renfa and others manage false government; the false Young Western King Xiao Youhe, Xiao Chaogui's son, Xiucheng especially relied on him, yet kept Xiucheng as a mere false general, not letting him hear great plans.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yang and Wei purges, Hong Xiuquan's brothers ran the state while the Young Western King Xiao Youhe held favor, yet Xiucheng was kept from high policy.

sentences.zh: 至是晉偽爵為王，乃大悅，以為秀全任己漸專，不料其疑己也。

translations.literal: Only now advanced to false king rank, he was greatly pleased, thinking Xiucheng's trust in him was gradually exclusive, not knowing he was suspected.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to king, Xiucheng rejoiced, thinking trust was complete—unaware suspicion remained.

sentences.zh: 浦口當金陵咽喉要地，迫於大軍，而糧援無措；

translations.literal: Pukou was the throat vital point of Jinling, pressed by the great army, and grain relief had no recourse;
translations.idiomatic: Pukou guarded Nanjing's throat but was pressed by imperial forces and starved of supplies;

sentences.zh: 南渡時，見秀全問計，秀全語以「事皆天父排定，奚煩計慮？

translations.literal: when crossing south he saw Xiucheng to ask plans; Xiucheng told him: "All affairs are arranged by the Heavenly Father—why trouble with planning?
translations.idiomatic: crossing south he asked Hong Xiuquan, who said, "Heaven arranges all—why plan?

sentences.zh: 」又與仁發等謀留其助守金陵，秀成不可，曰：「官軍既以長圍困我，當謀救困法，俱死於此無益也。

translations.literal: " He also plotted with Renfa and others to keep him to help defend Jinling; Xiucheng would not agree, saying: "Government troops have already long-encircled us—we should plan a method to relieve distress; all dying here is without benefit.
translations.idiomatic: " They wanted him to stay and defend Nanjing. Xiucheng refused: "The long encirclement demands relief, not useless death.

sentences.zh: 」渡還，以黃子隆、陳贊明屯浦口，親赴上游糾合皖南蕪湖、寧國死黨，謀間道犯浙江，分江南大營兵力，還解長圍之困，其志固不在浙也。

translations.literal: " Crossing back, he placed Huang Zilong and Chen Zanming at Pukou, personally went upstream to rally diehard bands of south Anhui Wuhu and Ningguo, plotting a hidden route to invade Zhejiang, divide Jiangnan Grand Camp strength, and return to relieve long-encirclement distress—his aim was never truly on Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: " He left Huang Zilong and Chen Zanming at Pukou, rallied Anhui diehards, and feinted into Zhejiang to split the Jiangnan camp and ease the siege—not to conquer Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 連日援太湖寇、捻攻鮑超潛山小池驛營壘不克，楊輔清、古隆賢用內應陷池州。

translations.literal: For successive days they aided Taihu rebels and Nian in attacking Bao Chao's Qianshan Xiaochi Post fortifications without success; Yang Fuqing and Gu Longxian used inside collaborators to seize Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: They failed to take Bao Chao's Xiaochi forts with Nian aid, while Yang Fuqing and Gu Longxian seized Chizhou by treachery.

sentences.zh: 韋志俊突圍屯泥灣，收合散亡，移屯香口；

translations.literal: Wei Zhijun broke out of encirclement and encamped at Niwan, gathered scattered fugitives, and shifted encampment to Xiangkou;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhijun broke out to Niwan, gathered fugitives, and moved to Xiangkou;

sentences.zh: 迭敗寇於八都坂、栗樹街，俘斬偽將軍陳松剋等三十餘人。

translations.literal: in succession defeated rebels at Badu Slope and Chestnut Tree Street, capturing and beheading over thirty including false general Chen Songke.
translations.idiomatic: he beat rebels at Badu Slope and Chestnut Street and took more than thirty officers including Chen Songke.

sentences.zh: 是年，秀全大封諸王。

translations.literal: That year, Xiucheng greatly enfeoffed all as kings.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hong Xiuquan enfeoffed a host of kings.

sentences.zh: 初，秀全定都金陵，一切文武之制，悉由偽東王楊秀清手定。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiucheng established the capital at Jinling, all civil and military systems were entirely set by the false Eastern King Yang Xiuqing by hand.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing became the capital, Yang Xiuqing had designed the whole civil and military order.

sentences.zh: 是時為秀全建國極盛時代，其宮室制度：第一，為龍鳳殿，即朝堂也，主議政、議戰諸大事。

translations.literal: At that time was the era of Xiucheng's state's greatest flourishing; his palace institutions: first, the Dragon-Phoenix Hall, that is the court, managing deliberation on government and war and other great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of the Taiping state, the Dragon-Phoenix Hall served as the court for policy and war.

sentences.zh: 每有大事，鳴鐘擊鼓，會議，秀全即升座，張紅幔。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a great affair, bells and drums were sounded for council; Xiucheng ascended the seat and spread a red curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Great affairs were announced with bells and drums; Hong Xiuquan took the throne beneath a red curtain.

sentences.zh: 諸王丞相兩旁分坐，依官職順列。

translations.literal: False kings and chancellors sat on both sides in order of office.
translations.idiomatic: Kings and chancellors sat by rank on either side.

sentences.zh: 賊將則侍立於後。

translations.literal: Rebel generals then stood in attendance behind.
translations.idiomatic: Generals stood behind them.

sentences.zh: 議畢，鳴鐘伐鼓退朝。

translations.literal: When deliberation ended, bells and drums sounded to dismiss court.
translations.idiomatic: Bells and drums closed the session.

sentences.zh: 第二，說教臺，每日午，秀全御此，衣黃龍袍，冠紫金冕，垂三十六旒。

translations.literal: Second, the Sermon Platform; daily at noon Xiucheng attended here, wearing yellow dragon robe, crowned with purple-gold coronet with thirty-six tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Second was the Sermon Platform, where Hong Xiuquan appeared daily at noon in yellow dragon robes and a tasseled purple-gold crown.

sentences.zh: 後有二侍者持長旗，上書「天父、天兄、天王、太平天國」。

translations.literal: Behind were two attendants holding long banners inscribed "Heavenly Father, Heavenly Elder Brother, Heavenly King, Taiping Heavenly Kingdom."
translations.idiomatic: Attendants bore banners reading "Heavenly Father, Heavenly Elder Brother, Heavenly King, Taiping Heavenly Kingdom."

sentences.zh: 臺式圓，高五丈，階百步。

translations.literal: The platform was round, five zhang high, with a hundred steps of stairs.
translations.idiomatic: The round platform stood five zhang high with a hundred steps.

sentences.zh: 說教時，官民皆入聽。

translations.literal: At sermon time, officials and people all entered to listen.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people gathered to listen.

sentences.zh: 其有意見者，亦可登座陳說。

translations.literal: Those with opinions could also ascend to state them.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone with a view could speak from the platform.

sentences.zh: 文左上，武右上。

translations.literal: Civil officials upper left, military upper right.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials to the upper left, military to the upper right.

sentences.zh: 士民由前後路直上，立有一定之位。

translations.literal: Gentry and people ascended straight by front and rear routes, standing in fixed positions.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners entered by set paths to fixed places.

sentences.zh: 第三，軍政議事局，軍事調遣、糧餉、器械總登所。

translations.literal: Third, the Military-Government Deliberation Bureau, the general registry for military dispatch, grain pay, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Third was the Military-Government Bureau, which tracked troops, grain, and arms.

sentences.zh: 秀全自為元帥，當日偽東王為副元帥，北王、翼王為左、右前軍副元帥，六官左、右副丞相為局中管理。

translations.literal: Xiucheng himself was commander-in-chief; then the false Eastern King was deputy commander-in-chief, Northern and Wing Kings left and right vanguard deputy commanders-in-chief, and the six offices' left and right vice chancellors managed the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Xiuquan was commander-in-chief; Yang Xiuqing was deputy; the Northern and Wing Kings led vanguards; vice chancellors ran the bureau.

sentences.zh: 各科員中，分軍馬、軍糧、軍械、軍衣、軍帳、軍船、軍圖、軍俘、軍事諸科。

translations.literal: Among section officers were divided sections for horses, grain, arms, clothing, tents, boats, maps, prisoners, and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sections covered horses, grain, arms, clothing, tents, boats, maps, prisoners, and operations.

sentences.zh: 又有糧餉轉運局、文書管理局、前鋒告急局、接濟局，皆屬軍政議事局。

translations.literal: There were also grain transport, document management, vanguard emergency, and relief bureaus, all subordinate to the Military-Government Deliberation Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Grain transport, archives, emergency dispatch, and relief offices all reported to it.

sentences.zh: 內以六官左、右副丞相領之。

translations.literal: Internally the six offices' left and right vice chancellors headed them.
translations.idiomatic: Six-office vice chancellors headed the staff.

sentences.zh: 其最尊者為軍機會商局長，初以偽東王領之。

translations.literal: The most honored was the chief of the Military Council Bureau; initially the false Eastern King held it.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Council chief was highest; Yang Xiuqing held it first.

sentences.zh: 遇有戰事，籌畫一切，則偽東王中坐，諸王、丞相、天將左右坐立，各手地圖論形勢，然後出師。

translations.literal: When there was warfare, planning everything, the false Eastern King sat in the center; false kings, chancellors, and heavenly generals sat left and right, each holding maps discussing terrain, then troops went out.
translations.idiomatic: In war councils Yang Xiuqing sat central while kings and generals debated maps before marching.

sentences.zh: 秀清死，偽翼王領之。

translations.literal: After Xiuqing died, the false Wing King held it.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Xiuqing died, the Wing King took it.

sentences.zh: 石達開去後，李秀成領之。

translations.literal: After Shi Dakai left, Li Xiucheng held it.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Dakai left, Li Xiucheng held it.

sentences.zh: 秀成東入蘇、杭，則有名無實，虛懸其位矣。

translations.literal: When Xiucheng entered east into Su and Hang, it was name without reality, the post hung empty.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiucheng went east to Jiangsu and Zhejiang, the post became an empty title.

sentences.zh: 其時寇之武備頗詳盡。

translations.literal: At that time rebel armaments were quite complete in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel armaments were then remarkably detailed.

sentences.zh: 自諸偽王內訌，人心解體，秀全以為非不次拔擢，無以安諸將之心。

translations.literal: Since the mutual slaughter among false kings, hearts dissolved; Xiucheng thought that without extraordinary promotions he could not settle the generals' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: After the kings turned on one another, Hong Xiuquan promoted wildly to hold the army together.

sentences.zh: 然自此大封之後，幾至無人不王，而丞相、天將之職多攝行。

translations.literal: Yet from this great enfeoffment onward, nearly no one was not a king, while chancellor and heavenly general posts were mostly acting.
translations.idiomatic: After that nearly everyone became a king while chancellors and generals often held acting titles.

sentences.zh: 於是各持一軍，勢不相下，而調遣諸王者，僅陳玉成一人。

translations.literal: Thus each held one army, momentum not submitting to others, and of those dispatching the false kings only Chen Yucheng alone.
translations.idiomatic: Each king held his own army and obeyed little but Chen Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 故八年以前，寇之用兵，攻守並用。

translations.literal: Therefore before the eighth year rebel use of troops employed both attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Before the eighth year the Taiping armies both attacked and defended.

sentences.zh: 八年以後，不過用攻以救守，戰局遂至日危，以底於亡。

translations.literal: After the eighth year they used only attack to save defense, and the war situation daily grew perilous until ending in destruction.
translations.idiomatic: After the eighth year they attacked only to survive sieges, and the war slid toward collapse.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，偽匡王、偽奉王、偽襄王糾合偽攝王自南陵犯涇縣灣灘，游擊王熊飛退走，寇遂蔓延黃邨、焦石埠，進攻副將李嘉萬，援師為楊名聲所敗，斬偽岡天燕、賴文禾。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, the false Kuang King, false Feng King, and false Xiang King colluded with the false She King from Nanling to invade Jing county Wan Beach; Mobile Corps Wang Xiongfei retreated; rebels then spread through Huang Village and Jiaoshi Port, advanced to attack Vice Commander Li Jiawan; relief army was defeated by Yang Mingsheng, who beheaded the false Gang Heaven Swallow and Lai Wenhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year's first month false kings from Nanling struck Jing county's Wan Beach. Li Jiawan was pressed until Yang Mingsheng's relief killed the false Gang Heaven Swallow and Lai Wenhe.

sentences.zh: 寇竄踞黃柏嶺，其黨尋大至，陷涇縣。

translations.literal: Rebels fled to hold Huangbai Ridge; their band soon came in great force and seized Jing county.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held Huangbai Ridge, then overwhelmed and took Jing county.

sentences.zh: 楊名聲等退走旌德，寇踵至，明日亦陷。

translations.literal: Yang Mingsheng and others retreated to Jingde; rebels followed to the foot and the next day it too fell.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Mingsheng fell back to Jingde; rebels followed and took it the next day.

sentences.zh: 我軍還守寧國。

translations.literal: Our army returned to defend Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial forces withdrew to defend Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 是時秀成自率悍黨數千，已由寧國縣間道犯廣德。

translations.literal: At that time Xiucheng himself led several thousand fierce partisans and had already by a hidden route in Ningguo county invaded Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng himself led thousands through hidden paths from Ningguo into Guangde.

sentences.zh: 張國樑督水陸諸軍渡江期大舉，克浦口八壘，黃子隆、陳贊明遁；

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang supervised land and naval forces crossing the river expecting a great campaign, took eight Pukou fortifications; Huang Zilong and Chen Zanming fled;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang crossed the river for a major campaign, took eight Pukou forts, and drove off Huang Zilong and Chen Zanming;

sentences.zh: 攻九洑洲，克其老巢，焚之。

translations.literal: attacked Jiufuzhou, took its old nest, and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: attacked Jiufuzhou, took its nest, and burned it.

sentences.zh: 寇自咸豐四年築壘九洑洲，內蔽江寧，外通大江，踞為南北水陸要區。

translations.literal: Rebels since the fourth year of Xianfeng built fortifications at Jiufuzhou, screening Jiangning within and connecting to the great river without, holding it as the north-south land and water vital zone.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xianfeng year four rebels had fortified Jiufuzhou to shield Nanjing and command the river.

sentences.zh: 江寧長圍成後，浦口、九洑洲皆克，勢大困。

translations.literal: After the Jiangning long encirclement formed, Pukou and Jiufuzhou were both taken and momentum was greatly cornered.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Nanjing encirclement closed and Pukou and Jiufuzhou fell, the rebels were cornered.

sentences.zh: 秀成由皖犯浙，分我兵勢，而諸將又以寇在陷阱，無能為役，習為驕佚，戰志漸消，故有閏三月大營失敗之禍。

translations.literal: Xiucheng from Anhui invaded Zhejiang to divide our military strength, while the generals also thought rebels were in a trap and could not be used, growing accustomed to arrogance and ease, fighting spirit gradually fading—hence the disaster of the intercalary third month's grand camp defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng raided Zhejiang to split imperial forces while his generals grew arrogant and slack, leading to the intercalary third-month disaster.

sentences.zh: 太湖寇、捻分四股來犯我軍，知府金國琛會集諸軍敗之仰天庵、高橫嶺，生擒悍目藍承宣，向擾害蘄、黃者，寸磔之。

translations.literal: Taihu rebels and Nian divided into four columns to invade our army; Prefect Jin Guochen joined forces and defeated them at Yangtian'an and Gaohengling, capturing alive fierce officer Lan Chengxuan, who had long harmed Qi and Huang, and dismembered him inch by inch.
translations.idiomatic: Taihu rebels and Nian struck in four columns until Jin Guochen routed them at Yangtian'an, captured Lan Chengxuan, and executed him by slow slicing.

sentences.zh: 金國琛等復敗寇、捻於潛山廣福寨。

translations.literal: Jin Guochen and others again defeated rebels and Nian at Qianshan Guangfu Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Guochen beat them again at Qianshan Guangfu Stockade.

sentences.zh: 玉成率龔得樹、張洛行來援，乘霧移營於羅山衝、白沙畈，冀與城寇相通，以圖牽綴我軍。

translations.literal: Yucheng led Gong Deshu and Zhang Luoxing to relieve them, exploiting fog to shift camp to Luoshan Pass and Baisha Fan, hoping to link with city rebels to tie down our army.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng brought Gong Deshu and Zhang Luoxing through fog to Luoshan Pass and Baisha Fan to link with the garrison.

sentences.zh: 諸軍會擊，寇大敗，擒斬偽庶天侯麥烏宿、偽軍師汪遂林等。

translations.literal: Armies joined attack; rebels were greatly defeated, capturing and beheading the false Common Heaven Marquis Mai Wusu and false strategist Wang Suilin and others.
translations.idiomatic: Combined forces routed them and killed the false Common Heaven Marquis Mai Wusu and strategist Wang Suilin.

sentences.zh: 明日，鮑超等進攻小池驛，當東路；

translations.literal: The next day, Bao Chao and others advanced on Xiaochi Post, facing the east route;
translations.idiomatic: Next day Bao Chao attacked Xiaochi Post on the east;

sentences.zh: 蔣凝學等攻羅山衝，當西路；

translations.literal: Jiang Ningxue and others attacked Luoshan Pass, facing the west route;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ningxue struck Luoshan Pass on the west;

sentences.zh: 多隆阿居中路策應。

translations.literal: Dolonga held the middle route to coordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Dolonga coordinated the center.

sentences.zh: 羅山衝寇蜂擁來撲，凝學連破衝口，攻入內山，馬隊繼之，寇大敗。

translations.literal: Luoshan Pass rebels swarmed to attack; Ningxue in succession broke the pass mouth, entered the inner mountain, cavalry followed, and rebels were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels swarmed at Luoshan Pass until Ningxue broke through, cavalry followed, and the line collapsed.

sentences.zh: 值東南風作，以火焚之，燬壘百有數十。

translations.literal: A southeast wind arose and fire burned them, destroying over a hundred fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: A southeast wind fed the flames and destroyed more than a hundred forts.

sentences.zh: 寇奪路狂奔，斃偽丞相葉榮發、偽將軍舒春華等。

translations.literal: Rebels seized routes in wild flight; the false chancellor Ye Rongfa and false general Shu Chunhua and others were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels fled in chaos, leaving dead including the false chancellor Ye Rongfa and general Shu Chunhua.

sentences.zh: 城寇謀宵遁，伏軍四起擊之。

translations.literal: City rebels plotted night flight; ambush troops rose on four sides to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison tried to flee by night and was cut down in ambush.

sentences.zh: 是役也，殲寇二萬餘，益惶懼，竄入潛山。

translations.literal: In this battle over twenty thousand rebels were destroyed; they grew ever more fearful and fled into Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty thousand were killed; the rest fled into Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿督軍尾擊，克其城。

translations.literal: Dolonga supervised the army in tail pursuit and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Dolonga pursued and took the city.

sentences.zh: 秀成、侍賢等至廣德，詐為清軍，陷之，杭、湖、蘇、常並震。

translations.literal: Xiucheng, Shixian, and others reached Guangde, feigning as Qing troops, and seized it; Hang, Hu, Su, and Chang all shook.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng and Shixian took Guangde by posing as Qing troops, shaking Hangzhou, Huzhou, Suzhou, and Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 巡撫羅遵殿調徽、寧防軍援剿廣德，以保兩浙門戶。

translations.literal: Governor Luo Zundian transferred Huizhou and Ningguo garrison troops to suppress Guangde and secure the two Zhejiang gateways.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Luo Zundian sent Huizhou and Ningguo troops to hold Guangde and guard Zhejiang's gates.

sentences.zh: 張芾遣周天孚馳防長興四安鎮，鎮距廣德四十里，當蘇、浙之交。

translations.literal: Zhang Fen dispatched Zhou Tianfu in forced march to defend Changxing Si'an Town; the town was forty li from Guangde, at the Su-Zhe junction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fen sent Zhou Tianfu to Si'an, forty li from Guangde on the Jiangsu-Zhejiang border.

sentences.zh: 和春遣水陸軍來會，秀成留陳坤書、陳炳文守廣德，自率譚紹光、陳順德、吳定彩等馳攻四安鎮，陷之。

translations.literal: He Chun dispatched land and naval forces to join; Xiucheng left Chen Kunshu and Chen Bingwen to guard Guangde and himself led Tan Shaoguang, Chen Shunde, Wu Dingcai, and others in swift attack on Si'an Town and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun sent reinforcements. Xiucheng left a garrison at Guangde and stormed Si'an with Tan Shaoguang and others.

sentences.zh: 和春遣水師會攻江寧上下兩關，七里洲寇謝茂廷、壽德州寇秦禮國遣使詣大營乞降。

translations.literal: He Chun dispatched the naval force to join attack on upper and lower Jiangning passes; Qili Island rebel Xie Maoting and Shoude Prefecture rebel Qin Liguo sent envoys to the grand camp to beg surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun's fleet attacked Nanjing's river passes while rebel envoys from Qili Island and Shoude offered surrender.

sentences.zh: 江寧西北各門皆瀕大江，洲堵錯互，寇踞上、中、下三關，築壘於壽德、七里各洲，與北岸九洑洲遙相倚藉。

translations.literal: Jiangning's northwest gates all faced the great river; islets and banks intertwined; rebels held upper, middle, and lower three passes, building fortifications on Shoude and Qili islets, mutually supporting Jiufuzhou on the north bank from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing's northwest gates lined the river where rebels held three passes and islet forts linked to Jiufuzhou.

sentences.zh: 九洑洲既克，茂廷、禮國約舉火為號，於是上下關同日而克。

translations.literal: After Jiufuzhou was taken, Maoting and Liguo arranged to raise fire as signal; thus upper and lower passes fell the same day.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiufuzhou fell, Maoting and Liguo signaled by fire and both passes fell the same day.

sentences.zh: 國樑增八壘於江東門，增四壘於安德門，毛公渡南北岸關隘悉為我奪，寇益大困。

translations.literal: Guoliang added eight fortifications at Jiangdong Gate and four at Ande Gate; Mao Gongdu north and south bank passes were all seized by us; rebels grew ever more cornered.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang strengthened Jiangdong and Ande gates and took Mao Gongdu passes, tightening the noose.

sentences.zh: 秀全檄諸寇解金陵圍。

translations.literal: Xiucheng ordered all rebels to relieve the Jinling siege.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Xiuquan ordered every column to relieve Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 時秀成在皖，與其部下謀曰：「清軍精銳悉萃金陵城下，其餉源在蘇、杭。

translations.literal: At that time Xiucheng was in Anhui and plotted with his subordinates: "Qing elite troops all gather below Jinling city; their supply source is in Su and Hang.
translations.idiomatic: In Anhui Xiucheng told his chiefs: "Qing elites besiege Nanjing while living off Jiangsu and Zhejiang supplies.

sentences.zh: 今金陵城外長壕已成，清軍內圍外禦。

translations.literal: Now the long moat outside Jinling is formed; Qing troops besiege within and defend without.
translations.idiomatic: The outer moat is complete; Qing forces besiege inside and block relief outside.

sentences.zh: 張國樑又嚄唶善戰，攻之難得志，不如輕兵從間道急搗杭州。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang again was skilled in battle; attacking was hard to succeed—better to take light troops by a hidden route and swiftly strike Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang was a fierce fighter, but direct assaults stalled. Xiucheng proposed a light column by hidden paths to strike Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 杭州危，蘇州亦必震動。

translations.literal: If Hangzhou is perilous, Suzhou too must be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Threaten Hangzhou and Suzhou would shake.

sentences.zh: 清軍慮我絕其餉源，必分師奔命以救。

translations.literal: Qing troops, fearing we cut their supply source, must divide forces in desperate relief.
translations.idiomatic: Qing forces would have to split to save their supplies.

sentences.zh: 我瞷大營虛，還軍以破圍師，則蘇、杭皆我有也。

translations.literal: We spy the grand camp empty, return the army to break the besieging force, then Su and Hang are both ours.
translations.idiomatic: We could watch the grand camp thin out, wheel back, break the siege, and take both cities.

sentences.zh: 」乃自率數千精卒以行，連陷安吉、孝豐、長興諸縣。

translations.literal: " He then himself led several thousand elite troops on the march, taking in succession Anji, Xiaofeng, and Changxing counties.
translations.idiomatic: " He led several thousand elites and seized Anji, Xiaofeng, and Changxing.

sentences.zh: 以其弟侍賢犯湖州，自率悍黨陷武康，間道踰嶺犯杭州。

translations.literal: He sent his younger brother Shixian to invade Huzhou while he himself with fierce partisans seized Wukang, crossed the range by hidden route, and invaded Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian struck Huzhou while Xiucheng took Wukang, crossed the hills, and hit Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 預結捻首張洛行、龔瞎子等，使內擾清、淮，以分江、皖兵力。

translations.literal: He beforehand colluded with Nian chiefs Zhang Luoxing and Gong Xiazi and others, making them disturb Qing and Huai within to divide Jiang and Anhui military strength.
translations.idiomatic: He set Zhang Luoxing and Gong Xiazi to raid north of the Huai and split imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 上命和春兼辦浙江軍務，而以張玉良總統援浙諸軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered He Chun also to manage Zhejiang military affairs, with Zhang Yuliang as overall commander of relief armies for Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put He Chun over Zhejiang affairs and Zhang Yuliang over relief.

sentences.zh: 玉良分大營兵勇五分之二禦之。

translations.literal: Yuliang divided two-fifths of grand camp troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang detached two-fifths of the grand camp to meet them.

sentences.zh: 秀成攻杭州，以地雷崩清波門，陷之，巡撫羅遵殿等均死難。

translations.literal: Xiucheng attacked Hangzhou; land mines collapsed Qingbo Gate; it fell; Governor Luo Zundian and others all died in the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng mined Qingbo Gate, took Hangzhou, and Governor Luo Zundian and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 秀成之破杭州也，祗一千二百五十先鋒。

translations.literal: When Xiucheng broke Hangzhou, there were only twelve hundred fifty vanguard troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou fell to only 1,250 vanguard troops.

sentences.zh: 諸處援兵不知虛實，聞城破，皆潰走。

translations.literal: Relief forces everywhere did not know true numbers; hearing the city fell, all collapsed in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Relief troops, not knowing how few the attackers were, fled when they heard the city had fallen.

sentences.zh: 迨張玉良援軍至，屯武林門，秀成曰：「中吾計矣！

translations.literal: When Zhang Yuliang's relief army arrived and encamped at Wulin Gate, Xiucheng said: "Caught in my plan!
translations.idiomatic: When Yuliang reached Wulin Gate, Xiucheng said, "The trap is sprung!

sentences.zh: 」自以兵少，乃多製旗幟作疑兵，潛退出城，委之而去。

translations.literal: " Himself having few troops, he made many flags as a ruse army and secretly withdrew from the city, abandoning it and leaving.
translations.idiomatic: " With few men he raised false flags and slipped out of the city.

sentences.zh: 玉良與將軍瑞昌會擊，立復省城。

translations.literal: Yuliang joined General Ruichang in joint attack and quickly recovered the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang and General Ruichang retook the city at once.

sentences.zh: 三月，秀成回竄餘杭，陷臨安。

translations.literal: In the third month, Xiucheng fled back to Yuhang and seized Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Xiucheng doubled back to Yuhang and took Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 旋為李定泰克復。

translations.literal: Soon it was recovered by Li Dingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingtai soon retook it.

sentences.zh: 孝豐、武康寇亦退走。

translations.literal: Xiaofeng and Wukang rebels also retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels at Xiaofeng and Wukang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時秀成及侍賢回廣德，楊輔清亦自池州來會。

translations.literal: At that time Xiucheng and Shixian returned to Guangde; Yang Fuqing also came from Chizhou to join.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng and Shixian returned to Guangde, joined by Yang Fuqing from Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 李定泰等會圖廣德，寇已分走建平，陷之，連陷東壩、高淳，復詐為官軍陷溧陽。

translations.literal: Li Dingtai and others planned to take Guangde; rebels had already divided and fled to Jianping, seized it, took in succession Dongba and Gaochun, again feigned as government troops and seized Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Dingtai moved on Guangde, rebels took Jianping, Dongba, Gaochun, and seized Liyang by disguise.

sentences.zh: 自是江南大營後路驟急，蘇、常俱大震。

translations.literal: From then the Jiangnan Grand Camp's rear route was suddenly urgent; Su and Chang both greatly shook.
translations.idiomatic: The grand camp's rear was suddenly threatened and Suzhou and Changzhou panicked.

sentences.zh: 和春馳檄張玉良等還救常州，熊天喜等克廣德，而楊輔清陷溧水，詐為官軍襲金壇，為周天孚等所敗，棄壘西竄。

translations.literal: He Chun urgently ordered Zhang Yuliang and others back to save Changzhou; Xiong Tianxi and others took Guangde, while Yang Fuqing seized Lishui, feigned as government troops to raid Jintan, was defeated by Zhou Tianfu and others, abandoned fortifications and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun recalled Yuliang for Changzhou. Yang Fuqing took Lishui and raided Jintan in disguise before being beaten back.

sentences.zh: 句容亦陷，句容當大營後路，餉道所必經，且與丹陽、鎮江接壤，為常州門戶。

translations.literal: Jurong also fell; Jurong stood on the grand camp's rear route, the supply route that must be passed, and bordered Danyang and Zhenjiang, the gateway of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jurong fell on the grand camp's supply line and guarded the approach to Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 和春遣副將梁克勳赴援，不及，續遣副將張威邦由淳化進剿。

translations.literal: He Chun dispatched Vice Commander Liang Keqin to relieve them—too late—and again dispatched Vice Commander Zhang Weibang to suppress by advancing from Chunhua.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun sent Liang Keqin too late, then Zhang Weibang from Chunhua.

sentences.zh: 何桂清遣將分防丹陽、鎮江、瓜洲，冀通大營至蘇、常水陸道路。

translations.literal: He Guiqing dispatched generals to defend separately Danyang, Zhenjiang, and Guazhou, hoping to open land and water routes from the grand camp to Su and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He Guiqing tried to reopen routes to Suzhou and Changzhou through Danyang, Zhenjiang, and Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 馬德昭等出屯郡城三十餘里下弋橋，堵溧陽、宜興各路寇內犯。

translations.literal: Ma Dezhao and others encamped at Xiayi Bridge over thirty li from the prefectural city, blocking Liyang and Yixing routes of rebel invasion within.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Dezhao blocked rebel paths from Liyang and Yixing at Xiayi Bridge.

sentences.zh: 米興朝自廣德進軍克建平。

translations.literal: Mi Xingchao advanced from Guangde and took Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Xingchao took Jianping from Guangde.

sentences.zh: 閏三月，寇自昌化出於潛，分犯分水，陷而旋復，進陷淳安。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month, rebels came out of Changhua into Yuqian, divided to invade Fenshui, seized it and soon recovered it, advanced and seized Chun'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month rebels from Changhua raided Yuqian and Fenshui, then took Chun'an.

sentences.zh: 秀成約會諸酋同議救金陵之策，秀成與侍賢由淳化、輔清由溧水退秣陵關，玉成亦自江浦渡江來會，江寧寇爭出築壘接應。

translations.literal: Xiucheng arranged with all chiefs to discuss the plan to save Jinling; Xiucheng and Shixian from Chunhua, Fuqing from Lishui retreating to Moling Pass, Yucheng also from Jiangpu crossing the river to join; Jiangning rebels vied to sally and build fortifications in mutual relief.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng coordinated a Nanjing relief: columns from Chunhua, Lishui, and Jiangpu while the city garrison built outer works.

sentences.zh: 斯時大營四面受敵，而良將勁兵調援浙西者一萬三千人，淳壩、宜興防軍又調去一千有奇，大營空虛，糧路又截斷，乃改月餉積四十五日始一發。

translations.literal: At that time the grand camp was attacked on four sides, while good generals and strong troops transferred to aid western Zhejiang numbered thirteen thousand; Chunba and Yixing garrisons also transferred away over a thousand; the grand camp was empty, grain routes cut—pay was changed to accumulate forty-five days before one issue.
translations.idiomatic: The grand camp was besieged on four sides, 13,000 elites were in Zhejiang, garrisons were stripped, pay slowed to forty-five-day cycles.

sentences.zh: 兵勇皆怨，心漸攜貳。

translations.literal: Soldiers all resented it; hearts gradually divided in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers grew resentful and loyalty frayed.

sentences.zh: 時群寇麇集，和春急調張玉良回援，何桂清留之不遣。

translations.literal: At that time rebel swarms gathered; He Chun urgently recalled Zhang Yuliang; He Guiqing kept him and would not send him.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun begged for Yuliang back; He Guiqing refused.

sentences.zh: 寇至雄黃鎮，我軍禦之不克。

translations.literal: Rebels reached Xionghuang Town; our army met them and could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels reached Xionghuang Town and imperial troops failed to hold.

sentences.zh: 輔清由秣陵關至南門，玉成由江寧鎮至頭關，板橋、善橋諸寇皆集南岸。

translations.literal: Fuqing came from Moling Pass to the south gate; Yucheng from Jiangning Town to Tou Pass; Banqiao and Shanqiao rebels all gathered on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: Fuqing hit the south gate, Yucheng the head pass, and rebel columns massed on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 秀成由姚巧門進紫荊山尾，陳坤書、劉官芳由高橋門而來，侍賢由北門紅山而至，輔清由雨花臺，玉成由板橋、善橋，連日攻撲長圍。

translations.literal: Xiucheng advanced from Yaomiao Gate to the tail of Zijing Mountain; Chen Kunshu and Liu Guanfang came from Gaoqiao Gate; Shixian from north gate Hongshan; Fuqing from Yuhuatai; Yucheng from Banqiao and Shanqiao—day after day attacking and pressing the long encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng, Chen Kunshu, Shixian, Fuqing, and Yucheng hammered the encirclement from every gate for days.

sentences.zh: 國樑與王浚分督諸將力禦，十五日夜，雷雨雹雪，大寒，總兵黃靖、副將馬登富、守備吳天爵戰死。

translations.literal: Guoliang and Wang Jun separately supervised generals in hard defense; on the night of the fifteenth, thunder, rain, hail, and snow, great cold—Commander-in-Chief Huang Jing, Vice Commander Ma Dengfu, and Garrison Commander Wu Tianjue died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: On a night of storm and hail, Huang Jing, Ma Dengfu, and Wu Tianjue were killed defending the line.

sentences.zh: 大營火起，全軍潰陷。

translations.literal: Fires rose in the grand camp; the whole army collapsed and fell.
translations.idiomatic: The grand camp caught fire and the army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 和春、許乃釗退走鎮江，再退丹陽，旋馳書趣國樑亦至，留馮子材守鎮江。

translations.literal: He Chun and Xu Naigui retreated to Zhenjiang, again retreated to Danyang, soon urgently wrote urging Guoliang also to come, leaving Feng Zicai to defend Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun and Xu Naigui fled to Zhenjiang, then Danyang, recalled Guoliang, and left Feng Zicai at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 國樑語和春曰：「六年向帥大營失陷，退扼丹陽。

translations.literal: Guoliang told He Chun: "In the sixth year Commander Xiang's grand camp fell and retreated to hold Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang told He Chun, "When Xiang Rong's camp fell in the sixth year, he held Danyang.

sentences.zh: 彼時京口未復，今東門之限在於鎮江。

translations.literal: At that time Jingkou was not yet recovered; today's eastern gate limit is at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingkou was still lost then; today the eastern gate is Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 舍此不守，是導寇而東也。

translations.literal: Abandon this and not defend—it is guiding rebels eastward." He Chun ultimately could not use it, while Yixing at the same time also fell.
translations.idiomatic: Abandon Zhenjiang and you open the road east." He Chun would not listen, and Yixing fell.

sentences.zh: 」和春卒不能用，而宜興同時亦失陷。

translations.literal: Rebel momentum greatly expanded, yet Xiucheng did not reward warriors in time, all day also did not ask after government affairs, only teaching people to recognize Heaven's truth, naturally having an age of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels surged, but Hong Xiuquan neither rewarded fighters nor governed, preaching only heavenly faith.

sentences.zh: 寇勢大張，而秀全於戰士不及獎敘，終日亦不問政事，只教人認實天情，自有昇平之局。

translations.literal: Renda and Renfa envied Xiucheng's achievement and urged Xiucheng to issue a stern edict ordering Xiucheng to lead his command within one month to take Su and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Renfa and Renda envied Xiucheng and ordered him to take Suzhou and Changzhou within a month.

sentences.zh: 仁達、仁發忌秀成功，嗾秀全下嚴詔，飭秀成率所部限一月取蘇、常。

translations.literal: Rebels plundered Jintan's four townships, writing large on walls: "Attack the countryside not the cities; when the countryside is desolate the cities break themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Rebels raided Jintan's countryside with slogans: "Burn the fields, not the walls—the cities will starve."

sentences.zh: 寇掠金壇四鄉，大書於壁曰：「攻野不攻城，野荒城自破。

translations.literal: Our army encamped at six gates, fighting rebels daily with mutual victories and defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops held six gates and traded blows daily.

sentences.zh: 」我軍屯六門，日與賊戰，互有勝負。

translations.literal: Xiucheng from Jurong attacked Danyang; Guoliang opened the south gate in fierce battle; Xiucheng ordered strong men to mix into our routed soldiers and suddenly strike Guoliang; he was wounded, cried out loudly, and died entering below Yin Gong Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng attacked Danyang. Guoliang fought at the south gate until infiltrators among the fugitives struck him down at Yin Gong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 秀成自句容攻丹陽，國樑開南門酣戰，秀成命力士溷入我軍潰卒中，猝擊國樑，被創大呼，入尹公橋下而死。

translations.literal: Xiucheng entered Danyang and ordered Guoliang's corpse collected, saying: "Two states at war, each loyal to its matter.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng took Danyang and honored Guoliang's body, saying, "We served different masters in life.

sentences.zh: 秀成入丹陽，命收國樑屍，曰：「兩國交兵，各忠其事。

translations.literal: Alive we were enemies—can the dead still be foes?
translations.idiomatic: In death need we remain enemies?

sentences.zh: 生雖為敵，死尚可為仇乎？

translations.literal: " He buried him with rites below Baota.
translations.idiomatic: " He buried him with ceremony below Baota.

sentences.zh: 」以禮葬之下寶塔。

translations.literal: He Chun fled to Changzhou; rebels followed at his heels.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun fled to Changzhou with rebels at his heels.

sentences.zh: 和春奔常州，寇躡其後。

translations.literal: He Guiqing, hearing the disaster, fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: He Guiqing fled in panic on hearing the disaster.

sentences.zh: 何桂清聞變跳走。

translations.literal: That month, Chu armies aiding south Anhui jointly took Taiping, Jiande, and Shiling three counties.
translations.idiomatic: That month Chu relief took Taiping, Jiande, and Shiling in south Anhui.

sentences.zh: 是月，楚軍援皖南，會克太平、建德、石埭三縣。

translations.literal: Jing county Zhang Fen joined Zhou Tianshou and others in advancing to destroy Baihua and Yangongtang route rebel fortifications, pressed straight to below the walls, beheaded the gate and entered straight through, and recovered the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fen and Zhou Tianshou destroyed forts on the Baihua route and stormed Jing county.

sentences.zh: 涇縣張芾會同周天受等進毀白華、宴公堂一路寇壘，直抵城下，斬關直入，遂復縣城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Tianchang and Liuhe rebels, taking advantage of Jinling Grand Camp's retreat to defend, divided into three routes to invade: one from Chenjiaji toward Yang city, one from Donggou spying on Guazhou, one from Sengdao Bridge weaving rafts to steal crossing and raid Shaobo—all were intercepted and struck by our army, dared not prevail, then built fortifications at Sengdao Bridge plotting long occupation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Tianchang and Liuhe rebels struck in three columns toward Yangzhou, Guazhou, and Shaobo, were blocked, and dug in at Sengdao Bridge.

sentences.zh: 四月，天長、六合寇乘金陵大營退守，分三路進犯：一由陳家集圖揚城，一由東溝窺瓜洲，一由僧道橋編筏偷渡襲邵伯，皆為我軍所截擊，不敢逞，乃築壘僧道橋圖久踞。

translations.literal: Our army on left, right, and center three routes hurried to join attack, destroyed two fortifications, burned wooden walls, corpses piled like pillows.
translations.idiomatic: Three imperial columns rushed in, destroyed two forts, burned wooden walls, and left heaps of dead.

sentences.zh: 我軍分左、右、中三路疾趨會攻，毀二壘，焚木城，積屍枕藉。

translations.literal: Rebels combined forces and retreated to hold Chenjiaji.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels fell back to Chenjiaji.

sentences.zh: 寇合股退踞陳家集。

translations.literal: Yangzhou and Zhenjiang were lip and teeth to each other; Li Ruozhu consulted boat commander Chen Taiguo and others to block each mouth separately.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruozhu had Chen Taiguo block the river mouths between Yangzhou and Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 揚州與鎮江相為脣齒，李若珠咨艇師陳泰國等分扼各口。

translations.literal: Rebels greatly pressed Changzhou; Zhang Yuliang from Hang Prefecture led troops first to arrive and built over forty camps large and small—all were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels pressed Changzhou. Yuliang came from Hangzhou and built forty camps—all were overrun.

sentences.zh: 寇大逼常州，張玉良由杭郡率軍先至，築營寨大小四十餘，悉為所破。

translations.literal: Changzhou fell; Yuliang was defeated and fled to Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou fell and Yuliang fled to Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 常州陷，玉良敗走無錫。

translations.literal: Xiucheng led his command's elite troops secretly out Jiulong Mountain to strike Gaoqiao's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng slipped elite troops around Jiulong Mountain to hit Gaoqiao's rear.

sentences.zh: 秀成率所部精卒潛出九龍山，拊高橋之背。

translations.literal: Yuliang's army was greatly defeated; Wuxi fell; defeated he fled to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang was routed, Wuxi fell, and he fled to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 玉良軍大敗，無錫陷，敗走蘇州。

translations.literal: He Chun suffered a chest wound and died reaching Jishu Pass outside Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun was wounded in the chest and died at Jishu Pass near Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 和春創胸，至蘇州濟墅關而卒。

translations.literal: Yuliang's repeatedly defeated army could not fight again; rebels pressed Suzhou; Yuliang retreated to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang's broken army could not fight. Rebels closed on Suzhou and he fled to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 玉良連敗之師不能復戰，寇薄蘇州，玉良退走杭州。

translations.literal: Changzhou and Yuanhe two counties' militia Li Wenbing and He Xinyi opened gates to welcome Xiucheng in to hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Militia leaders Li Wenbing and He Xinyi opened Changzhou and Yuanhe to Xiucheng.

sentences.zh: 長洲、元和兩縣廣勇李文炳、何信義開門迎秀成入踞之。

translations.literal: Governor Xu Youcheng and others likewise died martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Xu Youcheng and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 巡撫徐有壬等同殉難。

translations.literal: After Xiucheng held Su, he changed the Wu family Fuzhi Garden on North Street into a false residence.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng made the Wu family's garden on North Street his palace in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 秀成踞蘇後，改北街吳氏復園為偽府。

translations.literal: Xiucheng held Su for eleven days and issued a false proclamation to pacify the people.
translations.idiomatic: After eleven days in Suzhou he issued a pacification proclamation.

sentences.zh: 秀成踞蘇十有一日，出偽示安民。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the city walls and lanes, corpses collected in all numbered over eighty-three thousand, yet followers still greatly praised Xiucheng as loving people and not addicted to killing.
translations.idiomatic: More than eighty-three thousand corpses were collected in the city, yet rebels still praised Xiucheng as merciful.

sentences.zh: 城廂內外凡收屍八萬三千餘具，而從者猶盛稱秀成愛人不嗜殺也。

translations.literal: Rebels holding Su city again wantonly seized plunder; people competed in organizing militia for self-preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels looted Suzhou while civilians organized militia for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 寇踞蘇城，復恣意擄掠，民競團練為自保計。

translations.literal: Jiang and Anhui armies aiding Zhejiang recovered cities in succession and then jointly suppressed Chun'an; rebels were defeated and fled into Huizhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: Relief armies retook Zhejiang cities and drove Chun'an rebels into Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 江、皖援浙諸軍以次克復諸城，遂會剿淳安，寇敗遁入徽州境。

translations.literal: Su rebels seized Wujiang and invaded Pingwang; Zhejiang defense troops collapsed; Jiang Changgui was wounded and retreated to Renhe Tangqi Town; Vice Commander Zhang Shouyuan also collapsed at Qingshan Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou rebels took Wujiang and hit Pingwang. Zhejiang defenses broke; Jiang Changgui was wounded and Zhang Shouyuan routed.

sentences.zh: 蘇寇陷吳江，犯平望，浙江防軍潰，江長貴負傷還走仁和塘棲鎮，副將張守元亦潰於清杉牐。

translations.literal: Jiaxing was critical; Hangzhou Province was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaxing was in peril and Hangzhou shook.

sentences.zh: 嘉興危急，杭省大震。

translations.literal: Shixian burned through Jiaxing's south gate and entered to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian burned into Jiaxing's south gate and held the city.

sentences.zh: 侍賢燒嘉興南門入踞之。

translations.literal: Yuliang attacked Jiaxing's west and south gates; Chen Kunshu and Chen Bingwen begged relief from Su.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang attacked Jiaxing while Chen Kunshu and Chen Bingwen called Suzhou for aid.

sentences.zh: 玉良攻嘉興西、南兩門，陳坤書、陳炳文求救於蘇。

translations.literal: Just then Qingpu Zhou Wenjia battled foreign troops and came reporting urgency; Xiucheng therefore first relieved Qingpu, beat back foreign troops, attacked Shanghai straight, did not prevail, then answered Jiaxing relief, returned by Songjiang and Puxi to fight, took Jiaxing and Pinghu, then to Jiaxing, fought five days, divided one column up Shimen to cut Yuliang's route—many soldiers surrendered—Yuliang returned to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng relieved Qingpu, failed at Shanghai, then beat Yuliang at Jiaxing after five days' fighting and cut his retreat at Shimen.

sentences.zh: 適青浦周文嘉與洋軍戰，來告急，秀成乃先援青浦，擊退洋軍，直攻上海，不克，遂應嘉興之援，由松江、浦邑而回戰，取嘉興、平湖，順至嘉興，連戰五日，分一股上石門，斷玉良來路，兵多降者，玉良回杭州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Guichi and Qingyang rebels invaded Jing county; Commander-in-Chief Li Jiawan and others were defeated and died; Yang Mingsheng retreated to Taiping Huanghua Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Guichi and Qingyang rebels took Jing county, killed Li Jiawan, and drove Yang Mingsheng to Huanghua Ridge.

sentences.zh: 五月，貴池、青陽寇犯涇縣，總兵李嘉萬等敗死，楊名聲退至太平黃花嶺。

translations.literal: Rebels seized Guangde; Mi Xingchao's army collapsed, fled to Xiaofeng, again retreated outside She north Zhuoling.
translations.idiomatic: Guangde fell, Mi Xingchao's force broke, and he fled toward Xiaofeng and Zhuoling.

sentences.zh: 寇陷廣德，米興朝軍潰，奔孝豐，再退歙北篛嶺外。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jing and Guangde alarmed together; Zhou Tianshou's relief all could not arrive in time; Regiment Commander Ding Wenshang defended Jing but again retreated; rebels then fled through Sanxi to Jingde Sun Village.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Guangde alarms came together; relief failed and rebels poured through Sanxi into Jingde.

sentences.zh: 初，涇縣、廣德同時告警，周天受遣援皆不及，而參將丁文尚守涇，又退走，寇遂由三谿竄旌德孫邨。

translations.literal: Guangde rebels spied on Ningguo; Tianshou beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: Guangde rebels probed Ningguo and were driven back.

sentences.zh: 廣德寇窺伺寧國，天受擊卻之。

translations.literal: Rebels from Ningguo county's east bank reached Jingde and joined forces with Jing county; Jiading fell; Xue Huan soon took it and recovered Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Ningguo's east bank joined Jingde forces. Jiading fell but Xue Huan retook Taicang.

sentences.zh: 寇由寧國縣東岸至旌德，與涇縣合勢，嘉定陷，薛煥尋克之，收太倉。

translations.literal: Rebels attacked Zhenjiang, seized Qingpu, seized Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels struck Zhenjiang, Qingpu, and Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 寇攻鎮江，陷青浦，陷松江。

translations.literal: When rebels defended Jiangning, they used Anqing and Luzhou as horns and Taiping and Wuhu as guards.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing's defense rested on Anqing, Luzhou, Taiping, and Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 寇之守江寧也，以安慶、廬州為犄角，以太平、蕪湖為衛護。

translations.literal: South of Wuhu were Gucheng, Nanyi, Danyang, and Baijiu lakes; upstream they connected to Ningguo's Shuiyang River and Qingyi River; downstream they ended at Dongba.
translations.idiomatic: South of Wuhu lay lakes linking to Ningguo's rivers and ending at Dongba.

sentences.zh: 蕪湖之南，有固城南漪、丹陽白臼諸湖，上可通寧國之水陽江、清弋江，下則止於東壩。

translations.literal: Dig Dongba and release water, then one could pass Taihu, traverse Suzhou, and reach Lou River.
translations.idiomatic: Opening Dongba could flood routes through Taihu to Suzhou and the Lou River.

sentences.zh: 掘東壩而放之，則可經太湖歷蘇州以達於婁江。

translations.literal: Wuhu stood isolated in water—easy for rebels to hold, hard for government troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhu was an island stronghold—easy to hold, hard to take.

sentences.zh: 蕪湖孤懸水中，寇守之則易，官軍攻之則難。

translations.literal: Therefore held for five years of bloody battle without retreat, while Huangchi and Wanzi repeatedly suffered defeats—all because we had no naval force and rebels endured and defended well.
translations.idiomatic: Five years of blood at Wuhu and repeated defeats at Huangchi came from lacking a fleet against stubborn defenders.

sentences.zh: 是以踞五年血戰不退，而黃池、灣沚屢次失利，皆以我無水師，寇堅忍善守。

translations.literal: Government troops besieged for years but often because there were no troops on waterways could not cut their relief.
translations.idiomatic: Years of siege failed because imperial forces could not cut river supply.

sentences.zh: 官軍圍攻屢年，往往因水路無兵，不能斷其接濟。

translations.literal: Now with Suzhou lost, water lies on every face; if rebels block rivers to defend, land armies have almost no route of advance, almost no place to camp outside walls.
translations.idiomatic: With Suzhou lost, water was everywhere; rebels could block rivers and deny camps.

sentences.zh: 今蘇州既失，面面皆水，寇若阻河為守，陸軍幾無進攻之路，城外幾無立營之所。

translations.literal: Thus to attack Suzhou one must establish Taihu naval forces, make Taihu entirely ours, then west can link Ningguo momentum, east can press Suzhou's back.
translations.idiomatic: To retake Suzhou required a Taihu fleet to command the lake and threaten the city from east and west.

sentences.zh: 則欲攻蘇州，須立太湖水師，使太湖盡為我有，而後西可通寧國之氣，東可拊蘇州之背。

translations.literal: Therefore he proposed policies to establish naval forces swiftly at Huaiyang, Ningguo, and Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: He urged rapid creation of fleets on the Huai, in Ningguo, and on Taihu.

sentences.zh: 因建淮陽、寧國、太湖速立水師之策。

translations.literal: Rebels seized Jiangyin; Yuliang repeatedly used gunboats to break Jiaxing's Three Pagodas and Puji temples, pacified Xincheng rebel fortifications, shifted camp pressing west and south gates, broke seven fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels took Jiangyin while Yuliang's gunboats cleared Jiaxing temples and seven forts at the west and south gates.

sentences.zh: 寇陷江陰，玉良連以砲艇破嘉興三塔、普濟二寺，平新塍寇壘，移營逼西門、南門，破壘七。

translations.literal: Pingwang Town was the converging place of Zhejiang's Jiaxing and Huzhou and Jiangsu's Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Pingwang was where Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Wujiang met.

sentences.zh: 平望鎮者，浙江之嘉興、湖州，江蘇之吳江總匯處也。

translations.literal: Rebels held along the river Liuli Bridge, Meiyan, and other places, building firm fortifications everywhere, densely driving stake barriers, holding difficult terrain to block Jiang and Zhe routes.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels fortified Liuli Bridge and Meiyan along the river with stakes and barriers.

sentences.zh: 寇踞沿河六里橋、梅堰諸處，遍築堅壘，密釘排樁，扼險以阻江、浙之路。

translations.literal: Huzhou's Zhao Jingxian destroyed along-river rebel fortifications, divided forces to take Pingwang, joined armies at Mishihu, burned all battery nests, and advanced to besiege Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jingxian cleared river forts, took Pingwang, burned batteries at Mishihu, and besieged Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 湖州趙景賢毀沿河寇壘，分軍進克平望，會軍於米市湖，盡燬砲臺巢穴，進圍嘉興。

translations.literal: After rebels seized Songjiang, they dispatched their band to spy on Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Songjiang rebels probed Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 寇既陷松江，遣其黨窺上海。

translations.literal: Xue Huan exploited their unpreparedness, struck straight into the south gate, killed thirteen yellow-clad officers, seized over seventy boats, and quickly recovered the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Huan surprised them at the south gate, killed thirteen officers, took seventy boats, and retook the city.

sentences.zh: 薛煥乘其不備，直搗南門而入，殺黃衣目十三名，奪船七十餘艘，立復府城。

translations.literal: From Songjiang to Shanghai, along the way militia intercepted and killed nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Militia slaughtered fleeing rebels from Songjiang to Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 自松江至上海，沿途團練截殺殆盡。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Yang Fuqing rallied Jingde and Taiping great columns to invade Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yang Fuqing massed Jingde and Taiping columns against Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 六月，楊輔清糾旌德、太平大股犯寧國。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Yang Fuqing rallied Jingde and Taiping great columns to invade Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yang Fuqing massed Jingde and Taiping columns against Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 寇自長興竄陷安吉，王有齡遣彭斯舉赴援，遇於孝豐，失利，退走昌化。

translations.literal: Rebels from Changxing fled and seized Anji; Wang Youqin dispatched Peng Siju to relieve them; they met at Xiaofeng, fared ill, and retreated to Changhua.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Changxing took Anji. Peng Siju met them at Xiaofeng, was beaten, and fell back to Changhua.

sentences.zh: 寇直犯於潛，陷之，杭省大恐。

translations.literal: Rebels directly invaded Yuqian and seized it; Hangzhou Province was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels struck Yuqian and seized it, throwing Hangzhou into alarm.

sentences.zh: 寇復由黃渡再陷嘉定，糾土匪進踞南翔鎮，逼上海四十餘里，再陷平望。

translations.literal: Rebels again from Huangdu again seized Jiading, colluded with local bandits to advance and hold Nanxiang Town, pressed within forty-odd li of Shanghai, and again seized Pingwang.
translations.idiomatic: From Huangdu they retook Jiading, rallied bandits at Nanxiang within forty li of Shanghai, and seized Pingwang again.

sentences.zh: 蘇州、嘉興寇勢復合。

translations.literal: Suzhou and Jiaxing rebel momentum combined again.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel pressure from Suzhou and Jiaxing merged again.

sentences.zh: 於潛寇連陷臨安、餘杭，分擾富陽，吳雲會洋將華爾攻青浦急，偽寧王周文嘉乞援於蘇州，秀成率大股親援，我軍敗績。

translations.literal: Yuqian rebels in succession seized Lin'an and Yuhang, harassed Fuyang in separate groups; Wu Yun joined foreign officer Ward in urgent attack on Qingpu; the false Prince of Ning Zhou Wenjia begged relief from Suzhou; Xiucheng led a great column in person to relieve; our army suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqian rebels took Lin'an and Yuhang and raided Fuyang. Ward pressed Qingpu while Xiucheng marched in person and beat imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 寇收槍砲乘船再犯松江，陷之。

translations.literal: Rebels collected guns and cannon, took boats, and again invaded Songjiang and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels gathered arms, took boats, and seized Songjiang again.

sentences.zh: 江陰寇分黨築壘申港，掠船謀北渡，李若珠飭艇師破燬之，偽丞相方得勝遁。

translations.literal: Jiangyin rebels divided bands to build fortifications at Shen Harbor, plundered boats plotting north crossing; Li Ruozhu ordered boat division to break and burn them; the false chancellor Fang Desheng fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyin rebels fortified Shen Harbor until Li Ruozhu's fleet burned their boats and the false chancellor Fang Desheng fled.

sentences.zh: 玉良以地雷崩嘉興南門城垣，寇嚴拒不得進。

translations.literal: Yuliang used land mines to collapse Jiaxing south gate wall; rebels strictly resisted and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang mined Jiaxing's south wall but could not break in.

sentences.zh: 劉季三等連克餘杭、臨安。

translations.literal: Liu Jisan and others in succession took Yuhang and Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jisan and others retook Yuhang and Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 浙西寇回竄孝豐，突犯建德。

translations.literal: Western Zhejiang rebels fled back to raid Xiaofeng and suddenly invaded Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang rebels doubled back through Xiaofeng and struck Jiande.

sentences.zh: 七月，秀成毀松江城堞，率偽會王蔡元隆、偽納王郜永寬北犯上海，號十萬，焚掠泗涇，七寶民團禦之，多死傷。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Xiucheng destroyed Songjiang's battlements, led the false Association King Cai Yuanlong and false Reception King Hao Yongkuan north to invade Shanghai, claiming one hundred thousand, burned and plundered Sijing; Qibao militia resisted them—many dead and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Xiucheng stripped Songjiang's walls and sent 100,000 men against Shanghai, ravaging Sijing while Qibao militia suffered heavily.

sentences.zh: 寇屯徐家匯，薛煥督文武登陴固守。

translations.literal: Rebels encamped at Xujiahui; Xue Huan supervised civil and military officials mounting walls to defend firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels camped at Xujiahui while Xue Huan held the walls.

sentences.zh: 寇詐為官軍賺城，城上詗知，創卻之。

translations.literal: Rebels feigned as government troops to trick the city; those on the walls detected it and wounded them in repulse.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels disguised as imperial troops but were spotted and driven off.

sentences.zh: 洋輪之泊黃浦江者，升開花砲於桅發之，寇始敗退。

translations.literal: Foreign steamers moored on the Huangpu raised explosive shells on masts and fired; rebels at last were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign gunboats on the Huangpu shelled the rebels and forced them back.

sentences.zh: 孝豐寇陷廣德，游擊黃占起、江國霖戰死。

translations.literal: Xiaofeng rebels seized Guangde; Mobile Corps Huang Zhanqi and Jiang Guolin died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofeng rebels took Guangde; Huang Zhanqi and Jiang Guolin were killed.

sentences.zh: 江長貴突圍退至安吉，米興朝奔四安。

translations.literal: Jiang Changgui broke out of encirclement and retreated to Anji; Mi Xingchao fled to Si'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Changgui broke out to Anji while Mi Xingchao fled to Si'an.

sentences.zh: 未幾，趙景賢復廣德，寇再陷踞之。

translations.literal: Before long, Zhao Jingxian recovered Guangde; rebels again seized and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jingxian briefly retook Guangde before rebels seized it again.

sentences.zh: 寇復陷江陰楊厙汛城，逼常熟二十餘里。

translations.literal: Rebels again seized Jiangyin Yangshe garrison city and pressed within twenty-odd li of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels took Jiangyin's Yangshe post and threatened Changshu.

sentences.zh: 黃浦輪船洋兵以開花砲測擊上海寇壘，六發，創及秀成。

translations.literal: Huangpu steamers' foreign troops used explosive shells to range-strike Shanghai rebel fortifications; six shots; Xiucheng was wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign shells from the Huangpu hit Shanghai's rebel works and wounded Xiucheng.

sentences.zh: 是夜秀成解圍還青浦。

translations.literal: That night Xiucheng lifted the siege and returned to Qingpu.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xiucheng withdrew to Qingpu.

sentences.zh: 時嘉興寇告急，遂趨浙江。

translations.literal: At that time Jiaxing rebels reported urgent distress, so he hurried to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaxing's alarm then pulled him back to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 初，副將陳汝霖率民團救松江，迨上海解圍，洋將華爾會守松江，賜號常勝軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Vice Commander Chen Rulin led militia to save Songjiang; when Shanghai's siege was lifted, foreign officer Ward joined in defending Songjiang and was granted the title Ever-Victorious Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Shanghai was relieved, Ward helped hold Songjiang as the Ever-Victorious Army.

sentences.zh: 秀成陷嘉善，陷平湖，錫齡阿兵勇皆潰，寇旋去，收之。

translations.literal: Xiucheng seized Jiashan and Pinghu; Xiling'a's troops all collapsed; rebels soon left and it was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng took Jiashan and Pinghu, then withdrew and imperial forces reoccupied them.

sentences.zh: 寇陷金壇，知縣李淮守百四十餘日，糧盡援絕，川兵通寇，殺參將周天孚，陷之，李淮等皆戰死。

translations.literal: Rebels seized Jintan; Magistrate Li Huai defended over 140 days; grain exhausted and relief cut off; Sichuan troops colluded with rebels, killed Regiment Commander Zhou Tianfu, seized it; Li Huai and others all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Jintan fell after 140 days when Sichuan troops turned traitor, killed Zhou Tianfu, and slaughtered the garrison including Li Huai.

sentences.zh: 丹陽寇糾黨六七千由新豐等處分道撲水師，謀掠舟北渡，並沿河築壘，架砲轟射。

translations.literal: Danyang rebels rallied six or seven thousand partisans from Xinfeng and other places to attack the naval division on separate routes, plotting to seize boats and cross north, also building fortifications along the river and mounting cannon to bombard.
translations.idiomatic: Danyang rebels mustered thousands to seize boats, cross north, and shell the river line.

sentences.zh: 周希濂督艇師乘煙霧對擊，寇不支，遁回丹陽。

translations.literal: Zhou Xilian supervised the boat division to strike facing them in fog; rebels could not support it and fled back to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xilian attacked in fog and drove them back to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 玉良攻嘉興兩月不下，先後集兵三萬有奇，而蘇、常以北無牽掣之師，松江、青浦之寇可直入嘉興，常州、宜興之寇可直入長興，建平、廣德之寇可直入安吉，寧國、涇縣之寇可直入於潛。

translations.literal: Yuliang attacked Jiaxing two months without success; in all gathered over thirty thousand troops, yet north of Su and Chang there was no tying-down army; Songjiang and Qingpu rebels could enter Jiaxing straight; Changzhou and Yixing rebels could enter Changxing straight; Jianping and Guangde rebels could enter Anji straight; Ningguo and Jing rebels could enter Yuqian straight.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang had 30,000 men at Jiaxing but rebels could strike it from every direction because no force tied them down elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 寇前自長興逕逼省垣，雖經擊退，並立復數城，而廣德遂至不守。

translations.literal: Earlier rebels from Changxing pressed straight on the provincial walls; though beaten back and several cities recovered, Guangde came to be unheld.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Changxing had once threatened Hangzhou; Guangde was lost again.

sentences.zh: 迨收復廣德，而嘉善、平湖又復失陷。

translations.literal: When Guangde was recovered, Jiashan and Pinghu again fell.
translations.idiomatic: Jiashan and Pinghu fell again even as Guangde returned.

sentences.zh: 寇處處牽掣我軍，近復添築營壘砲臺，又偷劫五龍橋頭卡，多方誤我軍，實有罷乏不堪之勢。

translations.literal: Rebels tied down our army everywhere; recently they added fortifications and batteries, also secretly raided Wulong Bridge head stockade, misleading our army in many ways—truly showing exhaustion unbearable.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels pinned imperial forces everywhere, built new forts, and raided supply posts until the army was exhausted.

sentences.zh: 秀成以嘉興圍急，率大股來援。

translations.literal: Xiucheng, with Jiaxing siege urgent, led a great column to relieve.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng marched a great column to relieve Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 玉良督戰五日，勝負未決。

translations.literal: Yuliang supervised battle five days; victory and defeat undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang fought five days without a decision.

sentences.zh: 秀成分股上趨石門，謀斷大營後路。

translations.literal: Xiucheng divided forces to hurry up toward Shimen, plotting to cut the grand camp's rear route.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng sent a column toward Shimen to cut Yuliang's retreat.

sentences.zh: 地形多支河，塘路絕，無可歸。

translations.literal: Terrain had many branch rivers; dyke roads cut off; no return possible.
translations.idiomatic: Branch rivers and dyke roads cut off escape.

sentences.zh: 我軍懼奔，玉良負創，疾馳還杭省。

translations.literal: Our army feared flight; Yuliang was wounded and galloped back to Hangzhou Province.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops panicked. Yuliang was wounded and fled to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊既解嘉興之困，復陷石門，分兩路直逼杭省：一趨塘棲，民團禦之，退掠新市；

translations.literal: Bandits having relieved Jiaxing's distress again seized Shimen; divided two routes pressing straight on Hangzhou Province: one toward Tangqi, militia resisted, retreated to plunder Xinshi;
translations.idiomatic: Rebels freed Jiaxing, took Shimen, and pressed Hangzhou on two roads—toward Tangqi and toward Linping.

sentences.zh: 一趨臨平，吳再升敗之，轉走海寧。

translations.literal: one toward Linping; Wu Zaisheng defeated them, turned to flee to Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zaisheng beat the Linping column and drove it toward Haining.

sentences.zh: 彭斯舉等擊斬頗眾，寇悉退還石門。

translations.literal: Peng Siju and others attacked and beheaded quite many; rebels all retreated back to Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Siju killed many and the rebels withdrew to Shimen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，石門寇亦退，再升進駐石門。

translations.literal: Before long, Shimen rebels also retreated; Zaisheng advanced to garrison Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shimen was clear and Zaisheng occupied it.

sentences.zh: 馬德昭由臨平、長安相繼前進。

translations.literal: Ma Dezhao from Linping and Chang'an advanced in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Dezhao advanced from Linping and Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 八月，寇陷昭、常，再攻平湖、嘉善，陷之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, rebels seized Zhao and Chang, again attacked Pinghu and Jiashan, and seized them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month rebels took Shaoxing and Changzhou prefectures and again seized Pinghu and Jiashan.

sentences.zh: 是時秀成自嘉興還蘇州，奉秀全偽詔，趨還江寧，令經營北路。

translations.literal: At that time Xiucheng returned from Jiaxing to Suzhou, received Xiucheng's false edict, hurried back to Jiangning, and was ordered to manage the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng returned to Suzhou, obeyed a false edict, and was sent back to Nanjing to manage the northern front.

sentences.zh: 初，咸豐三年，林鳳祥、李開芳北犯不返，秀成未敢輕舉。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the third year of Xianfeng, Lin Fengxiang and Li Kaifang invaded north and did not return; Xiucheng did not dare act lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Since Lin Fengxiang and Li Kaifang's northern expedition in Xianfeng year three, Xiucheng had been cautious about marching north.

sentences.zh: 適江西、湖北匪目四十餘人具降書投秀成，邀其上竄，自稱有眾數十萬備調遣。

translations.literal: Just then over forty Jiangxi and Hubei bandit chiefs submitted surrender letters to Xiucheng, inviting him upriver, claiming tens of thousands ready for dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty Jiangxi and Hubei chiefs offered surrender and urged him upriver with tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 秀成覆書允之，留陳坤書駐守蘇州，自返江寧，請先赴上游招集各股，再籌進止。

translations.literal: Xiucheng replied agreeing, left Chen Kunshu to garrison Suzhou, himself returned to Jiangning, asked first to go upstream to rally all columns, then plan advance or halt.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng agreed, left Chen Kunshu at Suzhou, returned to Nanjing, and asked to rally upstream forces first.

sentences.zh: 秀全大怒，責其違令。

translations.literal: Xiucheng was greatly enraged and blamed him for disobeying orders.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Xiuquan raged at the disobedience.

sentences.zh: 秀成反復爭辯，堅執不從，秀全卒不能強。

translations.literal: Xiucheng argued back and forth repeatedly, stubbornly refusing; Xiucheng ultimately could not force him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng argued until Hong Xiuquan could not force him.

sentences.zh: 於是取道皖南，上竄江、鄂。

translations.literal: Thus he took the route through south Anhui and fled upriver to Jiang and E.
translations.idiomatic: He marched through south Anhui toward Jiangxi and Hubei.

sentences.zh: 秀成之在偽京與諸黨會議也，曰：「曾國藩善用兵，將士聽命，非向、張可比。

translations.literal: When Xiucheng was in the false capital in council with all bands he said: "Zeng Guofan is skilled in using troops; officers and soldiers obey orders—not comparable to Xiang and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In council at Nanjing Xiucheng said Zeng Guofan was a greater threat than Xiang Rong or Zhang Guoliang.

sentences.zh: 將來七困天京，必屬此人。

translations.literal: In the future when the Heavenly Capital is seven times besieged, it must be this man.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing was besieged seven times, he said, it would be Zeng who threatened it.

sentences.zh: 若皖省無他故，尚不足慮。

translations.literal: If Anhui has no other incident, it is still not enough to worry.
translations.idiomatic: Anhui alone was not yet the danger.

sentences.zh: 一旦有失，則保固京城，必須多購糧食，為持久之計。

translations.literal: Once there is loss, then to secure the capital city one must buy much grain food as a plan for endurance.
translations.idiomatic: But loss in Anhui would require stockpiling grain to endure a long siege.

sentences.zh: 」秀全聞之，責秀成曰：「爾怕死！

translations.literal: " Xiucheng heard this and blamed Xiucheng: "You fear death!
translations.idiomatic: Hong Xiuquan snapped that Xiucheng feared death.

sentences.zh: 我天生真主，不待用兵而天下一統，何過慮也？

translations.literal: I am Heaven's true lord by birth; without needing troops the realm is unified—why excessive worry?
translations.idiomatic: He boasted that Heaven would unify all without armies.

sentences.zh: 」秀成歎息而出，因與蒙得恩、林紹璋等再三計議，僉以秀成之策為然。

translations.literal: " Xiucheng sighed and went out; with Meng De'en, Lin Shaozhang, and others he deliberated again and again; all judged Xiucheng's plan correct.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng withdrew sighing; Meng De'en and Lin Shaozhang agreed with his plan.

sentences.zh: 因議定自偽王侯以下，凡有一命於朝者，各量其力出家財，廣購米穀儲公倉，設官督理之。

translations.literal: They therefore resolved that from false kings and marquises down, all who held court rank should contribute family wealth according to ability, widely purchase rice grain and store in public granaries, with officials supervising.
translations.idiomatic: They ordered every ranked rebel to buy grain for public granaries.

sentences.zh: 俟缺乏時，平價出糶，如均輸故事，以為思患預防之計。

translations.literal: When lacking, sell at fair price like the equal transport precedent, as a plan to think of trouble beforehand and prevent it.
translations.idiomatic: Grain would be sold at fair prices in shortage, following the old equal-transport model.

sentences.zh: 洪仁發等相謂曰：「此亦一權利也。

translations.literal: Hong Renfa and others said to one another: "This is also a profit opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Renfa and others saw profit in it.

sentences.zh: 」因說秀全用鹽引、牙帖之法，分上、中、下三等：上帖取米若干石，中、下以次遞減。

translations.literal: " They therefore persuaded Xiucheng to use salt monopoly and license methods, divided into upper, middle, and lower three grades: upper license took so many piculs of rice, middle and lower decreasing in turn.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed salt licenses in three grades priced in rice.

sentences.zh: 此帖即充偽樞府諸偽王祿秩。

translations.literal: This license then served as false Pivot Mansion false kings' salary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Licenses doubled as salaries for false kings.

sentences.zh: 收入後無須撥解，而稍提其稅入公，大半皆入私橐。

translations.literal: After collection no need to remit upward; only a little tax提 to public, the greater part all entering private purses.
translations.idiomatic: Most revenue went to private pockets, not the public store.

sentences.zh: 商販非執有帖者，粒米不得入城，犯者以私販論罪。

translations.literal: Merchants without licenses could not bring a grain of rice into the city; violators were punished as private traders.
translations.idiomatic: Unlicensed grain was banned on pain of death.

sentences.zh: 如是，則法可行而利可獲矣。

translations.literal: Thus the law could be enforced and profit obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The scheme was meant to enforce control and profit.

sentences.zh: 洪氏諸偽王乃分售帖利，上帖售價有貴至數千金者。

translations.literal: Hong clan false kings then divided and sold license profits; upper licenses sold for as much as several thousand gold.
translations.idiomatic: Hong princes sold licenses for thousands of taels.

sentences.zh: 及商販至下關，驗帖官皆仁發輩鷹犬，百端挑剔，任意勒索。

translations.literal: When merchants reached Xiaguan, inspecting license officials were all Renfa's henchmen, picking flaws on every side, extorting at will.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaguan, Renfa's agents extorted licensed merchants at will.

sentences.zh: 商販呼籲無門，漸皆裹足；

translations.literal: Merchants cried out with no door; gradually all wrapped their feet;
translations.idiomatic: Merchants stopped coming.

sentences.zh: 而諸偽王侯又因成本加重，售價過昂，不願多出貲金，米糧反絕。

translations.literal: while false kings and marquises also because costs increased sold at excessive prices, unwilling to put out much gold—rice grain反而 cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Kings raised prices and stopped funding grain purchases, so supplies dried up.

sentences.zh: 秀成言之秀全，請廢洪氏帖。

translations.literal: Xiucheng spoke to Xiucheng, asking to abolish Hong clan licenses.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng asked Hong Xiuquan to abolish the Hong licenses.

sentences.zh: 秀全以詰仁發，仁發以：「奸商每借販米為名，私代清營傳遞消息。

translations.literal: Xiucheng interrogated Renfa; Renfa said: "Wicked merchants often use selling rice as pretext, secretly relaying Qing camp messages.
translations.idiomatic: Renfa claimed merchants smuggled intelligence to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 設非洪氏，誰能別其真偽？

translations.literal: If not the Hong clan, who can distinguish true from false?
translations.idiomatic: Only the Hong clan, he said, could tell traitors from traders.

sentences.zh: 此實我兄弟輩之苦心，所以防奸，非以罔利也。

translations.literal: This is truly our brothers' painstaking effort to prevent traitors, not to seek profit.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted it was security, not profit.

sentences.zh: 」秀全信其言，置之不問，秀成憤然而去。

translations.literal: " Xiucheng believed his words and set it aside without inquiry; Xiucheng left in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Xiuquan believed him. Xiucheng left furious.

sentences.zh: 寇陷寧國，提督周天受等死之。

translations.literal: Rebels seized Ningguo; Commander-in-Chief Zhou Tianshou and others died.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels took Ningguo and killed Commander-in-Chief Zhou Tianshou.
